About the role
The Industrials team automates and adds intelligence to heavy machinery across construction, mining, and agriculture. As a Senior Robotics & Integration Engineer, you will own the software and hardware platform that our intelligent autonomy stack runs on — everything from networking, time synchronization, sensors and drivers, and middleware, down to embedded systems, drive-by-wire, and low-level controls actuation. This role sits at the intersection of hardware, software, and robotics, blending 0→1 development with production systems and direct product and customer-facing work. You will partner with core teams across the company — such as electrical, middleware, firmware, and hardware, etc. — and bring their work together, adapting it into products that enable customer success. As a tech lead, you will coordinate and prioritize the work of multiple engineers on the team as well as cross-functional efforts with internal teams.


At Applied Intuition, you will:

 - Own the vehicle platform end-to-end: networking, time synchronization, sensor selection and drivers, middleware integration, embedded software, drive-by-wire, and low-level controls actuation

 - Architect and deliver full-system platform capabilities spanning hardware and software, taking them from 0→1 prototypes through to reliable production systems deployed on heavy machinery

 - Integrate the cross-functional work of internal teams into cohesive, product-ready platforms adapted to customer machines and use cases

 - Interact directly with customers to identify target use cases, define platform requirements, and drive integrations through to successful deployment in the field

 - Lead and coordinate a team of engineers: set technical direction, prioritize across competing workstreams, and manage cross-functional dependencies with internal teams

 - Design and bring up test rigs and validation infrastructure for end-to-end system testing, hardware-in-the-loop verification, and on-vehicle validation

 - Debug, test, and troubleshoot complex interactions across the full stack — from sensor timing and network behavior to actuation and controls — to ensure reliability and system performance in harsh, real-world environments

We're looking for someone who has:

 - 5+ years of experience in robotics, systems integration, or platform software development, with demonstrated technical leadership or tech lead experience

 - Bachelor's or Master's Degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, or a related area

 - Deep, hands-on experience across the robotics platform stack: sensors and drivers, networking and time synchronization, middleware (e.g., ROS 2, DDS, or proprietary frameworks), and embedded systems

 - Strong development experience in C/C++ on Linux, including debugging and testing complex real-time systems

 - Experience with vehicle actuation and low-level controls, such as drive-by-wire systems and controller integration

 - Strong understanding of electronic systems and how to set up, instrument, and debug them

 - Ability to coordinate and prioritize across multiple engineers and cross-functional teams to deliver on customer commitments

Nice to have:

 - Experience with heavy machinery, off-road vehicles, agriculture, mining, or construction equipment

 - Experience with automotive and industrial communication technologies, including CAN, J1939, LIN, Ethernet/TSN, PTP/gPTP, AUTOSAR, etc.

 - Experience taking robotic systems from prototype to production, including safety considerations, release processes, and CI/CD for embedded targets

 - Experience interacting directly with customers to scope, deliver, and support projects that meet their requirements

 - Firmware development experience or familiarity with microcontroller-based systems

 - Skills in adjacent areas (electrical/harness design, CAD/3D printing, PCB design, etc.)

About the Role 
We are looking for highly ambitious engineers with a passion for driving customer success at the highest levels. This is not a typical engineering role; it's a unique opportunity to operate at the intersection of groundbreaking technology and critical customer impact in the mining industry. You will own the outcome of our most strategic site-operator engagements and be the single accountable owner for shipping autonomous hauling systems (AHS) to production and sustaining it in the field — directly accelerating the industry's adoption of safe, software-centric, AI-driven machines globally.

At Applied Intuition, you will

 - Own end-to-end leadership for Applied's AHS delivery across strategic site operators

 - Develop and run a New Product Introduction (NPI) process with clear gateways for internal execution, from initial production through every subsequent field release

 - Own regular SteerCos with site operators — build the presentation material, run the meetings, and get sign-off on what was delivered

 - Align workstream leads across Engineering, Finance, Quality, Product Support, Procurement, and Legal on the goals for each gateway, and hold them accountable to execute.

 - Cultivate executive-level connections with site operators, becoming a trusted advisor through production and beyond

 - Identify the signal in the noise. Ensure the right work is done, at the right time, to the highest standard of quality — every gateway, every release



We're looking for someone who has:

 - 5+ years leading complex, cross-functional technical programs in automotive, industrial, or robotics domains

 - Strong communication skills and a track record of driving alignment across engineering, quality, and business functions



Nice to have

 - Prior experience in mining, construction, ports, or industrial site operations

 - Prior work in autonomous vehicle or robotics development

 - Prior experience running steering committees or executive-level program reviews

About the Role

Applied Intuition builds and deploys autonomous systems across automotive, trucking, and industrials programs. As we scale, we need one company standard: consistent procedures, consistent records, and evidence we can put in front of any customer or regulator, in any program.

This role owns that standard. You will build and run the operational safety compliance and assurance framework across every program — procedures, incident classification, compliance obligations, and the records that evidence all of it.

This is a cross-program mandate, not a program-embedded one. Individual programs will continue to execute; your job is to make sure they execute against the same standard and can prove it.

At Applied Intuition, you will:

 - Establish a unified operational framework across automotive, trucking, and industrials, including SOPs, readiness checklists, and incident taxonomy.

 - Own the operational safety ownership map, identifying responsibilities, gaps, and cross-functional dependencies.

 - Develop and maintain safety-driven operational procedures in partnership with Systems Engineering and Program Management.

 - Represent Operations in change control and deployment readiness reviews, ensuring execution readiness.

 - Own the operational compliance framework, including permits, authorizations, customer obligations, audits, and regulatory changes.

 - Ensure fleet compliance requirements are met and documented, including inspections, maintenance, safety-critical parts, defect containment, and DOT drug/alcohol testing.

 - Own incident management end to end, from classification and response through RCA, CAPA, and verified effectiveness.

 - Drive cross-program incident and safety trend analysis, ensuring lessons learned reach all field teams.

 - Define and maintain operational safety evidence, support safety cases and customer assurances, and report safety performance to leadership.

 

We're looking for someone who has:

 - 7+ years in operational compliance, transportation safety, program management, or a related field, including 3+ years in a safety-critical or regulated environment.

 - Proven ownership of compliance programs, including building and maintaining the underlying framework.

 - Experience standardizing processes across multiple programs, sites, or business units.

 - Strong experience with root cause analysis and CAPA through verified closure.

 - Proven ability to build audit-ready documentation and recordkeeping systems.

 - Excellent written communication, with the ability to create clear operator procedures and concise executive-level summaries.

Nice to have:

 - Experience in autonomous vehicles, trucking, mining, aviation, rail, or another safety-critical, regulated industry.

 - Experience across multiple operating domains, with the ability to distinguish true regulatory differences from local practices.

 - Working knowledge of DOT, FMCSA, OSHA, and MSHA requirements, plus familiarity with state AV permitting.

 - Familiarity with safety case methodologies and standards such as ISO 26262, SOTIF, or UL 4600.

 - Relevant safety certification (e.g., CSP, OSHA 500/501, or MSHA Part 46/48).

 - Experience supporting multiple customer programs with differing contractual and safety requirements.

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Navy is racing to break decades of closed, single-vendor ship architectures. Combat systems, C4I, and hull, mechanical, and electrical (HM&E) systems run on separate, vendor-locked compute with no shared data plane.  The Navy is modernizing ship systems and requires a platform to unify it.  A warship operating system (WarshipOS) is Applied's answer: the onboard and offboard infrastructure and application layer that create a unified compute and data platform across a ship and test across the manned and unmanned fleet. The goal is to become the software integrator for the Navy, and it is built directly on Applied's commercial automotive VehicleOS foundation.

We are hiring a Head of Engineering to build and lead the DefenseOS engineering organization, with an initial focus on building WarshipOS. You will own technical strategy and delivery across the product's four pillars: a zonal compute architecture, a data transport and SDK layer that frees data from proprietary subsystems, and a modern SIL/HIL test environment with a digital twin. You will hire and grow a multi-disciplinary team and its technical leads, set the bar for engineering quality, and partner directly with product, Navy customers, and shipbuilders. This is a leadership role: you will direct specialists across combat-systems architecture, hardware and EE, perception, and integration rather than owning every domain yourself.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build and lead the DefenseOS engineering organization. Hire, structure, and grow a multi-disciplinary team across platform and software, EE and hardware architecture, perception and fusion, and integration and test, and develop its technical leads.

 - Own the technical strategy and roadmap across the four WarshipOS pillars: zonal compute, data transport / API / SDK, AI/ML perception and fusion platform, and modern SIL/HIL test with a digital twin, aligned to the broader DefenseOS strategy.

 - Lead the zonal architecture. Drive the design and deployment of location-based zone controllers and centralized compute that replace federated, domain-based designs, and their interfaces to prime-built combat, C4I, and HM&E systems.

 - Stand up the software and data platform. Direct the middleware, APIs, and SDKs that extract and unify data from sensor and mission systems behind a common data plane across classification levels.

 - Set engineering best practices across hardware and software: architecture, code review, CI/CD, automated and hardware-in-the-loop test, performance, and quality metrics suited to mission-critical, field-deployed systems.

 - Own program execution. Plan releases, track progress against milestones across anchor programs, surface risks early, and deliver on schedule and to quality under acquisition and field constraints.

 - Partner with product, defense customers, and shipbuilders/integrators as a design-informed engineering leader, shaping operator-facing capability and the trade-offs that keep the roadmap mapped to operational value.

 - Communicate status, risk, and outcomes to senior leadership, escalate clearly, and provide engineering input into program and business decisions.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Engineering leadership at scale. Typically 12+ years in software and systems engineering with 6+ years leading engineering teams, including managing other managers and technical leads, and a track record of building and scaling a team from a small core.

 - Software platform depth. Shipped complex software platforms that integrate real-time, mission- or safety-critical systems: middleware, data transport, and APIs / SDKs that unify heterogeneous subsystems behind a common data plane.

 - Hardware / software systems fluency. Led programs spanning hardware and software (compute architecture, sensor and system integration, lab-to-platform test), enough to set direction for EE / hardware and integration leads.

 - Integrating modern compute with legacy, closed subsystems. Built the gateways, adapters, and abstraction layers that connect proprietary or undocumented interfaces into a unified data plane.

 - Delivery under hard constraints. Ownership of the full lifecycle from requirements through deployment and sustainment under reliability, latency, safety, and field-readiness constraints, with disciplined execution in ambiguous, fast-moving programs.

 - Cross-functional leadership and communication with product, hardware, operations, customers, and senior leadership, including clear escalation of technical and schedule risk.


SECURITY REQUIREMENTS:

 - Must be a U.S. Citizen

 - Must hold or be eligible for a U.S. Secret security clearance

For more information about U.S. security clearances: click here https://www.state.gov/securityclearances.




NICE TO HAVE

 - Software-defined vehicles (SDVs) or analogous commercial platforms where a zonal architecture and centralized compute replaced distributed, domain-based controllers, directly transferable to a warship operating system.

 - Naval or maritime subsystems: combat / mission systems, shipboard communications (C5I, tactical data links, SATCOM), or HM&E.

 - Unmanned surface vessels (USVs) or other unmanned / autonomous platforms; familiarity with shipboard size, weight, power, and survivability constraints.

 - Prior naval service or fleet / operational experience.

About the role

Our defense business is one of the fastest growing parts of the company, and we are looking for a strategic operator to lead finance for it. You will sit on the Strategic Finance team and embed with the Defense organization, helping build and scale the business as it takes on more ambitious programs and customers.

This is a highly visible role at a hyper-growth, pre-IPO technology company. We build a dual-use software platform with applications across both commercial and defense markets. You will act as the financial counterpart to the Head of Defense and their leadership team across product, engineering, and go-to-market, operating with the breadth of a business unit CFO: the person in the room who can say what a decision is worth, what it costs, and what it means for the trajectory of the business.

At Applied Intuition, you will:

 - Work alongside the Head of Defense and the product, engineering, and go-to-market leaders on the questions that shape the business, from where to invest to which opportunities are worth chasing. Own the financial picture of the business and make it legible to the executive team and the Board.

 - Develop how we price our platform in defense markets and structure agreements as our offering and customer base evolve. Build the models that connect price to cost of delivery and margin, and bring judgment to novel situations where there is no precedent to copy.

 - Partner with go-to-market, Legal, and Contracts on pursue/pass decisions, proposal economics, and negotiation strategy for major opportunities. Own the financial case for what we go after and what we decline.

 - Develop a defensible view of where defense budgets are heading, which funding sources our platform can reach, and how long it takes money to move from customer interest to signed contract. Turn that into a plan leadership can plan against.

 - Advise on where to invest R&D dollars and how to resource the business. Translate product roadmaps and customer requirements into cost, margin, and headcount implications, and bring rigor to how we choose between competing bets.

About the Role

We are looking for a performance engineer who specializes in making large-scale machine learning workloads fast and cost-efficient in the datacenter. This role is focused on distributed training runs spanning many nodes, and high-throughput batch inference sweeping petabytes of real-world autonomy logs for auto-labeling, data mining, ground-truth generation, and evaluation.

The optimization target here is not tail latency on a vehicle - it is throughput, cluster goodput, and cost per unit of data processed. A training run that wastes 30% of its GPU-hours on stalled data loaders, or an offline inference sweep that takes a week instead of a day, directly slows down how fast the whole company can iterate. You will own the gap between what our fleet of accelerators is theoretically capable of and what our workloads actually achieve: profiling across the stack, finding where the compute and the wall-clock time actually go, and closing the difference.

You will work at the intersection of accelerators, ML frameworks, and large-scale data infrastructure, partnering with the teams who own each layer to land wins that show up in training time-to-result and offline processing cost. At Applied, we encourage all engineers to take ownership over technical and product decisions, closely interact with users to collect feedback, and contribute to a thoughtful, dynamic team culture.

At Applied, you will:

 - Profile and optimize distributed training end to end - data loading and preprocessing, augmentation, kernel execution, gradient communication, and checkpointing

 - Optimize large-scale offline and batch inference over petabyte-scale sensor logs: batching and scheduling strategies, quantization and low-precision execution, graph optimization, and accelerator saturation across long-running sweeps

 - Establish roofline and performance models for our workloads, quantify the gap between achieved and theoretical performance, and stack-rank optimization opportunities by impact and effort

 - Improve multi-node scaling efficiency: sharding and parallelism strategies, collective communication, interconnect utilization, and memory-bandwidth and kernel-fusion bottlenecks

 - Drive cluster goodput - reduce GPU idle time from input pipeline stalls, storage and network I/O, scheduling gaps, stragglers, and failure recovery on long-running jobs

 - Build the benchmarking, observability, and regression-detection tooling that keeps performance from silently degrading as models and code evolve

 - Collaborate with engineers across functions to solve complex data and compute problems at scale

 - Contribute to a team culture that values effective collaboration, technical excellence, and innovation


WE'RE LOOKING FOR SOMEONE WHO HAS:

 - Hands-on ML performance engineering experience: profiling, roofline analysis, throughput optimization, and root-cause investigation in production systems

 - Experience with distributed multi-node training at scale (FSDP, DeepSpeed, Megatron, NCCL, or equivalent), including diagnosing scaling inefficiency as node count grows

 - Deep familiarity with GPU or accelerator performance concepts - memory bandwidth, kernel launch overhead, occupancy, quantization, collective communication

 - Experience with high-throughput or batch inference systems (NVIDIA Triton Inference Server, TensorRT, ONNX Runtime, Ray, or similar)

 - Fluency in Python and proficiency in C++ or another systems language

 - Excellent debugging, analytical, and problem-solving skills

 - A deep understanding of machine learning foundations, and the ability to develop technical solutions for problems with no established playbook

Nice to have:

 - GPU kernel development experience: CUDA, Triton, CUTLASS, or hand-tuned attention implementations

 - Experience with profiling toolchains such as Nsight Systems/Compute, PyTorch Profiler, or perf

 - Experience with GPU scheduling and orchestration on Kubernetes, Slurm, or Ray, including multi-tenant cluster utilization

 - Experience with fault tolerance and elastic training for long-running jobs - checkpointing strategy, straggler mitigation, preemption recovery

 - Familiarity with autonomy or robotics data (ROS, OpenCV, multi-sensor log formats)

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Stack Tooling team builds software infrastructure across multiple autonomy verticals to help engineering teams test, analyze failures, and deploy faster. The team works on problems central to production autonomy rollout: local and cloud simulation realism, performance, and scale-up, autonomy CI and deployment pipelines, data pipelines for fast decision-making on new changes.

As a Software Engineer on this team, you will execute highly cross-functional projects supporting autonomy developers, systems engineers, and triage and release teams. The work done by the team aims to cover multiple autonomy domains at once — a change that impacts trucking can quickly scale out to cars and offroad vehicles.




AT APPLIED INTUITION, YOU WILL:

 - Work on consolidating common dependencies (simulation artifacts, testing methods, agentic development loops, etc.) into a single ecosystem

 - Integrate with cutting edge neural rendering tools and Applied's Dana platform to enable faster analysis and stronger conclusions.

 - Enable safety-critical event analysis and response, pushing the limits of realistic log resimulation

 - Increase hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) simulation testing fidelity so autonomy engineers detect issues before rollout to the road.

 - Stabilize, generalize, and scale code deployment and offboard vehicle pre-checks to eliminate vehicle downtime and maximize testing uptime


WE'RE LOOKING FOR SOMEONE WHO HAS:

 - Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Robotics, or a related engineering field

 - 3+ years of professional software engineering experience shipping production-grade code

 - Strong foundational programming experience in C++

 - Experience maintaining critical path developer tooling infrastructure

 - Experience with cloud infrastructure and/or managing resources in customer environments


NICE TO HAVE:

 - Preferred Master’s degree in Robotics or other autonomy-related engineering field

 - Prior experience with data pipelining architectures, maps validity, or metrics and evaluation frameworks

 - Exposure to software simulation tooling and either RL-based, physics-based, or reconstruction-based simulation runtimes

 - Prior experience working on perception modeling, planning, controls, or other onboard robotics functions

 - Previous background working with automotive OEMs, autonomous vehicles, or robotic development platforms

About the role

We are looking for a Legal Operations Generalist to join our Legal team in Sunnyvale, California. Reporting to and partnering closely with the Chief Legal Officer, you will be the day-to-day point of contact for legal requests across the company — the person who keeps things moving, follows up relentlessly, and makes sure nothing slips. This role requires genuine range: you will move fluidly across intake triage, signature coordination, system administration, knowledge management, global entity maintenance, insurance support, and compliance support.

At Applied Intuition, you will:

 - Serve as the air traffic control hub for the Legal team — own the legal intake system, triage all incoming requests, route to the right owner, and ensure nothing falls through the cracks

 - Identify and pilot AI-native approaches to legal operations and bring the team along on adoption, using and building enterprise AI in day-to-day operations.

 - Own our CLM operations day-to-day: maintain and run automated workflows for NDAs, vendor agreements, and commercial contracts. Support attorneys and contract managers on process and system questions

 - Support in leveraging AI and MCP capabilities to enable self-service contract data queries and trend analysis

 - Own the Legal team’s repository. Build and maintain an organized, searchable document repository; document standard operating procedures and close gaps in existing coverage

 - Manage the Legal team’s new hire onboarding process and maintain key templates, playbooks, and training materials

 - Track and report on legal operations metrics including request volume, turnaround times, and outside counsel spend

 - Support entity management and corporate filings, coordinating with outside vendors and relevant counsel to keep corporate records current

 - Assist with ESG and regulatory compliance execution under attorney direction — data gathering, tracking, and reporting

 - Support outside counsel and vendor management, including tracking billing against budgets and assisting with performance reviews

 - Coordinate and chase signatures across the organization — track all documents pending execution, follow up proactively with signatories, and ensure agreements close on time

 - Manage the DocuSign environment, including envelope creation, template management, user permissions, and integrations with the broader legal tech stack

 - Arrange notarization of documents as needed, coordinating with internal stakeholders and external notary services

 - Evangelize legal processes to cross-functional partners — build self-service resources and show internal clients why following the process makes them faster, not slower



We’re looking for someone who has:

 - Bachelors degree in Political Science, Legal Studies, Data Science, or related field

 - 4–8 years of experience in legal operations, business operations, contracts management, or a similar operational role in a technology company or law firm

 - Hands-on system experience, ideally as a workflow designer or administrator; experience with DocuSign, Ironclad, Jira, and Google Suite strongly preferred

 - A genuinely generalist operational profile — you have owned a wide range of work across systems, documentation, reporting, and cross-functional coordination without settling into a single specialty

 - Strong process-builder instincts: you create structure and documentation where none exists

 - Comfort with ambiguity and a bias toward action — willingness to take on any task, big or small, to get the job done

 - Strong organizational, time management, and project management skills with the ability to handle high volume and balance competing demands

 - Good judgment and a high level of professional integrity, discretion, and ability to maintain confidentiality

 - Genuine curiosity about AI tools and a desire to find smarter, more scalable ways to work

Nice to have:

 - Prior experience in a high-growth technology company or autonomous systems / defense environment

 - Experience with entity management and corporate filings

 - Familiarity with e-billing platforms and outside counsel management

 - Experience sourcing and implementing legal technology solutions

 - Active California Notary Public commission or willingness to obtain one

Based in the Otemachi area, the Tokyo site consists of more than 70 employees who previously came from Google, Mobileye, Tesla, TIER IV, Woven by Toyota, and other renowned companies.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for a Service Manager to lead our engineering technician team in Japan. Our test vehicles and rigs are the physical foundation of everything we build — every autonomy release, every customer demonstration, and every on-road validation program depends on them being safe, correctly built, and available when engineers need them.

You'll manage and grow the technician team, run our vehicle service operation end to end, and be the person accountable for fleet readiness, workshop safety, and regulatory compliance in Japan. This is a hands-on management role: you'll spend real time in the shop and on vehicles, not only in planning meetings.

At Applied Intuition, we encourage our teams to take ownership over technical and operational decisions. You'll have wide latitude to build the service function the way it should be built.

 


AT APPLIED INTUITION, YOU WILL:

 - Lead, coach, and grow a team of engineering technicians — setting standards, running reviews, and developing careers

 - Own fleet readiness: plan and prioritize vehicle buildouts, modifications, maintenance, and repairs to minimize downtime for engineering and customer programs

 - Run the workshop as a safe, organized, efficient operation, including tooling, layout and safety procedures.

 - Ensure all vehicle modifications and inspections comply with Japanese safety regulations (Safety standards) and Vehicle inspection requirements, coordinating vehicle modification application and dealings with authorities as needed

 - Partner closely with autonomy engineering, hardware, and vehicle operations teams in Japan and the US, and support OEM customer engagements that involve our vehicles

 


WE'RE LOOKING FOR SOMEONE WHO HAS:

 - 7+ years of technical experience in automotive service, mechanical, electrical, or robotics environments, including 2+ years leading or supervising technicians

 - Practical experience as a certified vehicle inspector (Automobile inspector)

 - Working knowledge of Japanese vehicle safety regulations (Safety standards) and the review process for vehicle modifications

 - Demonstrated ownership of a service or workshop operation 

 - Strong organization and communication skills, and the judgment to prioritize competing requests from multiple engineering teams

 - Native-level Japanese and business-level English

 


NICE TO HAVE:

 - Commercial truck maintenance and repair experience

 - Experience managing a Certified factory or Designated factory, or standing up a workshop from scratch

 - Practical experience with AV components such as LiDARs, radars, and cameras

 - Ability to design, draw, and prototype custom harness cables

ROBOTICS SOFTWARE ENGINEER



About Applied Intuition Defence

Applied Intuition UK is a software and infrastructure supplier that accelerates the deployment of next-generation autonomous capabilities to the warfighter across air, land, sea, and space. Based in London, our seasoned defence team hails from Palantir, Anduril, SpaceX, Google, Lockheed Martin, and the UK and US Armed Services. Learn more at appliedintuitiondefense.com http://appliedintuitiondefense.com.



About the role
As a Robot Software Engineer, your day-to-day life will vary. Some days you might find yourself out in the field, integrating hardware and software directly onto vehicle platforms and pushing autonomy algorithms through live testing. Other days you'll be back in the office, deep in SIL and HIL environments, working through the complex autonomy and vehicle intelligence systems that span both hardware and software domains. And some days you'll be on-site with a customer, demoing what you built and troubleshooting in real time as they put it to the test. Every day is different, and each one moves the work forward.

Along the way, you'll touch whatever it takes to make the platform work, such as behaviours development, platform integration, navigation, and everything in between. You'll collaborate closely with cross-functional teams to deliver robust, scalable autonomy solutions for defense customers, drawing on computer networking, code integration, and a genuine passion for robotics. You'll build, test, and deploy your software, and then watch it actually fly.



At Applied Intuition you will:

 - Develop and adapt mission behavior, navigation, and decision-making logic to meet the needs of diverse defense platforms and missions

 - Design and implement autonomy capabilities that are modular and reusable across different vehicle types and programs

 - Integrate and deploy autonomy solutions onto embedded Linux and other hardware platforms, including interfacing with sensors and collecting data

 - Conduct system-level setup, testing, and validation, including software-in-the-loop (SIL) and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) evaluations

 - Support live flight test of autonomy software on Group 1-5 unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs)

 - Troubleshoot complex software and integration issues to ensure high reliability and performance across the stack

 - Collaborate with 3rd party UAS vendors and cross-functional teams to bring autonomy software to life on OEM and Applied hardware alike
   
   

Who we’re looking for:

 - BS or MS in Robotics, Computer Science, or related engineering field

 - 3+ years of hands-on experience working with robotic systems (hardware, software, and integration)

 - Experience with modern C++

 - Experience developing autonomy behavior and decision-making logic (e.g., behavior trees, state machines) and/or navigation algorithms for robotic or autonomous systems

 - Experience integrating autonomy/robotics products with Pixhawk autopilots (ArduPilot and/or PX4)

 - Experience integrating with communication busses & protocols: UART/RS232/RS422/RS485, SPI/QSPI, I2C, Ethernet

 - Experience developing in Docker, containerized deployment environments, and using Linux-based operating systems (e.g., RHEL, Ubuntu)

 - Familiarity with real-time, edge computing, and safety-critical systems operating in software-in-the-loop (SIL), hardware-in-the-loop (HIL), test & operational environments

 - Excellent communication skills and a customer-oriented project delivery mindset



Travel Requirements:

 - General willingness to travel for company business between our offices, as well as to customer sites



Security Requirements:

 - Must have ability to hold UK Security Clearance (current or previous preferred)

ABOUT THE ROLE

Physical AI is the next wave beyond LLMs, and the stakes are highest in defense: fragmented systems cause missed threats, and clunky interfaces cost operators time they can't get back. Applied is one of a small number of companies with the product surface, field access, and engineering depth to fix this.

The Defense team has proven its autonomy, simulation, and onboard systems in real deployments. Now we're turning bespoke, program-driven wins into products that scale across customers, platforms, and theaters — and design carries a lot of that weight.

We're hiring a Product Designer to own that experience end to end, across two connected surfaces:

 - Real-time operator interfaces for command, control, and situational awareness — on tablets, ground stations, and shipboard/airborne environments with constrained compute and connectivity.

 - Enterprise web platforms that defense engineering teams, customers, and partners use to build, simulate, test, and ship autonomy.

You don't need to arrive as a defense expert — you need to be a fast, rigorous learner who can turn a complex domain into a clear point of view. You'll conduct primary research with warfighters, analysts, and engineers, and pair with a strong PM and engineering bench to ship. Expect up to 25% travel, including internationally, to bases, ranges, and customer sites.

Reports to the head of product design; partners with PMs across DroneStack, Defense OS, autonomy platforms, and simulation, plus the engineers building each system.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the design of one or more Defense products end to end — research, interaction and visual design, prototyping, shipped UI.

 - Become the voice of the operator through primary research, ride-alongs, and exercises with warfighters and partners.

 - Design real-time edge interfaces that reduce cognitive load and shorten the decide-act loop under contested comms and limited compute.

 - Design the trust model for agentic autonomy — approval and escalation patterns that keep humans meaningfully on the loop.

 - Design the enterprise tools used to build, simulate, validate, and ship autonomy.

 - Extend the Defense design system to serve both real-time and enterprise workflows without splintering.

 - Turn one-off program deliveries into repeatable products.

 - Represent design at demos, program reviews, and industry events; help grow the design practice as the vertical scales.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 8+ years of product design experience across at least two meaningfully different environments (industries, product types, stages, or customer segments).

 - Track record shipping products end to end — research through launch and iteration — including hard calls on what not to build.

 - Strong research instincts: proven ability to learn a new domain from scratch and turn findings into design direction.

 - A portfolio showing judgment on information density, decision UI, and multi-user workflows.

 - Comfort learning and designing for technically complex systems (no autonomy/robotics background required).

 - Strong engineer collaboration and ability to partner with EMs/tech leads on tradeoffs.

 - Clear communication — from design briefs to presentations for senior leadership.

 - Proficiency with modern prototyping tools.


SECURITY REQUIREMENTS

 - U.S. citizenship required.

 - Must hold or be eligible for a U.S. security clearance (TS/SCI target; Applied will sponsor).


NICE TO HAVE

 - Active DoD Secret/Top Secret/TS-SCI clearance.

 - Experience with defense, intelligence, maritime, aerospace, or first-responder users.

 - Background in C2, air traffic, cockpit/EFB, geospatial, or real-time simulation interfaces.

 - Experience with developer platforms, MLOps, data labeling, or test/observability tools.

 - Design experience for edge/constrained-compute environments.

 - Experience shaping trust/approval patterns for AI copilots or agentic systems.

 - Prior military, intelligence, or fleet operational service.

 - Experience helping build a design practice from the ground up.


COMPENSATION

Includes base salary, equity, and benefits (medical/dental/vision/life/disability, 401(k) match, learning/wellness stipends, PTO). Base salary range for this Sunnyvale-based role: $150,000–$200,000. Actual salary depends on experience, skills, and level.

GNC ENGINEER

 

About Applied Intuition Defence

Applied Intuition UK is a software and infrastructure supplier that accelerates the deployment of next-generation autonomous capabilities to the warfighter across air, land, sea, and space. A subsidiary of Applied Intuition, we deliver dual-use solutions to national security customers that build upon several years of product development and experience from commercial autonomy programs. Based in London, our seasoned defence team hails from Palantir, Anduril, SpaceX, Google, Lockheed Martin, and the UK and US Armed Services. Learn more at appliedintuitiondefense.com http://appliedintuitiondefense.com.

 

About the role

As a Guidance, Navigation & Control Engineer at Applied, you'll be at the forefront of defense aerial autonomy. You'll design, integrate, and rigorously test core flight autonomy capabilities across the full range of aerial UAS platforms, from agile quadrotors to long-range fixed wings. Partnering with teams across the company, you'll create and adapt GNC algorithms to the unique requirements of each program, contributing directly to our core software stack so your work becomes a reusable capability that powers every program, not just one. The mission is bold and the stakes are real: you'll be engineering the systems that give our military an unmatched edge in the skies.

 


AT APPLIED, YOU WILL:

 - Write software that operates real autonomous aircraft systems including group 1-5 unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), as well as simulated models to accomplish tactical military missions

 - Build, leverage, and improve aerial autonomy software architectures that are ultimately tested and deployed on real systems to accomplish military missions

 - Collaborate with 3rd party UAS vehicle vendors to develop and integrate aerial autonomy software onto OEM hardware
   
    


WE'RE LOOKING FOR SOMEONE WHO HAS:

 - Master's degree in Aerospace, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science or similar field

 - 6+ years of hands-on experience developing GNC software for autonomous systems

 - Experience developing autonomy algorithms in C++

 - Experience developing or implementing outer-loop control systems or path planning algorithms

 - Strong foundation in control theory, dynamics, and optimization, with experience applying them to real-world autonomous systems

 - Experience developing and simulating 3DoF or 6DoF models of air vehicles to support GNC algorithm development

 - Experience with flight testing and performing data analysis

 - Experience with UAS GNC/navigation systems such as PX4 and Ardupilot

 - Strong functional, procedural, data-oriented, and object-oriented programming experience
   
    

Travel Requirements:

 - General willingness to travel for company business between our offices, as well as to customer sites

 

Security Requirements:

 - Must have ability to hold UK Security Clearance (current or previous preferred)
   
    


NICE TO HAVE:

 - Ability to use data visualization and debugging tools to support autonomy control development

 - Experience developing in Docker and containerized development environments, using Linux-based operating systems (e.g., RHEL, Ubuntu), source control systems, and artifact registries

 - Understanding of key technologies: C++, Python, DevOps, Containers, Linux

 - Familiarity with software-in-the-loop (SIL) and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) development and testing

 - Experience with Bazel

 - Experience working projects related to national security for one or more government agencies

 - References who will describe them as low-ego, highly motivated, thoughtfully opinionated, strong communicators and curious listeners

ABOUT THE ROLE

Seeking a Systems Safety Engineer with hands-on experience in system-level safety analysis, hazard identification, risk assessment, and safety case development for autonomous and semi-autonomous heavy machinery. The role focuses on enabling safe deployment of mining and industrial autonomous systems through practical safety engineering activities. Looking for someone who can build and drive machine-level safety cases end-to-end, develop safety requirements from operational hazards, and work directly with engineering teams to close safety gaps through design, validation, and operational controls.

AT APPLIED INTUITION, YOU WILL:

 - Develop and own machine-level safety cases for autonomous mining vehicle deployments and driverless operations

 - Design, develop hazard identification and risk assessment activities for machine functions and operational scenarios, including:
   
   - HAZOP
   
   - System FMEA
   
   - Functional Failure Analysis
   
   - Operational Risk Assessment
   
   - Safety Gap Analysis

 - Perform safety analysis and derive Machine Safety Requirements (MSRs) for:
   
   - Brake-by-Wire systems
   
   - Steer-by-Wire systems
   
   - Throttle-by-Wire systems
   
   - Shift / Transmission-by-Wire systems
   
   - Emergency Stop systems
   
   - Autonomous motion control systems
   
   - Remote operation functions

 - Analyze hazardous machine behavior, failure modes, and fault propagation paths to identify required prevention, detection, and mitigation measures

 - Translate operational hazards and engineering findings into clear, implementable system safety requirements and verification criteria

 - Support architecture reviews and identify safety gaps across sensing, compute, controls, hydraulics, actuation, communication, and operational processes

 - Work across vehicle functions including braking, steering, propulsion, autonomy, operator controls, machine monitoring, and site integration activities

 - Support development of validation strategies and safety acceptance criteria for machine-level demonstrations and driverless deployments

 - Collaborate with systems, controls, autonomy, software, hardware, and validation teams to ensure safety requirements are implemented and verified end-to-end

 - Participate in machine bring-up, fault injection activities, safety validation, field testing, and site acceptance activities

 - Review HW FMEDAs, reliability analyses, diagnostic coverage assumptions, and fault detection mechanisms to support machine-level safety arguments

 - Support customer safety reviews, regulator discussions, operational readiness reviews, and deployment sign-offs.


WE'RE LOOKING FOR SOMEONE WHO HAS:

 - Bachelor’s or master’s degree in electrical engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, Systems Engineering, Software Engineering, or a related technical discipline

 - 3+ years of system safety experience with a primary focus safety per ISO 26262 Part 6

 - Hands-on experience developing system-level safety analyses and safety artifacts for complex electromechanical systems

 - Strong experience with HAZOP, FMEA, safety requirement derivation, risk assessment, and safety case development

 - Good understanding of vehicle and machine control systems including braking, steering, propulsion, hydraulics, and autonomous control functions

 - Ability to analyze interactions between hardware, software, controls, operators, and operational environments

 - Experience collaborating across software, hardware, and systems engineering teams to implement safety requirements end-to-end

 - Experience defining safety requirements and mitigation strategies from identified hazards and failure modes

 - Experience supporting verification and validation activities for safety-critical systems

 - Hands-on experience producing safety work products across the V-cycle

 - **Candidates with automotive functional safety experience, particularly ISO 26262 Part 4, HARA, FSC/TSC development, ADAS, or autonomous driving systems, are considered relevant and transferable to this role

We are looking for a founding senior Research Scientist with a TL growth path within the Research Group at Applied Intuition. Robotics is a core vertical of our physical AI platform alongside autonomous vehicles — early stage, but with the full backing, resources, and infrastructure of a $15B company behind it. Our vision is for robotics to grow into its own vertical, and the person in this role will play a defining part in shaping that trajectory.

Humanoids and dexterous manipulation represent one of the last unsolved frontiers of physical AI, and this is where the most interesting research problems live. Unlike an academic lab constrained by professor-driven agendas, or a VC-backed startup optimizing for the next demo, this role offers something rare: real research autonomy paired with a concrete path to real-world deployment. You will help set the research agenda, work on a flat team in close collaboration with senior researchers Yihan Hu and Wei, and see your methods deployed into humanoid robots and dexterous hands through Applied's tools and infrastructure.

Our Research Group is composed of leading experts from top institutions and companies, recognized for their exceptional academic and industry contributions — including eight Best Paper awards at premier conferences and journals such as CVPR and ICRA. Learn more at appliedintuition.com/research http://appliedintuition.com/research.

We are hiring someone who has strong convictions about their technical roadmap and is looking for a place with the resources and scope to execute on them.

At Applied Intuition, you will:

 - Set and drive the research agenda for humanoid robotics, with a focus on dexterous manipulation and relevant frontier research problems

 - Conduct original research on world-action foundation models and reinforcement learning, delivering manipulation policies for humanoid robotic systems

 - Serve as a founding senior researcher on the humanoid effort, shaping both the technical direction and the growth of the team

 - Publish at top-tier venues (CoRL, ICRA, RSS, and similar) alongside other Research Scientists and interns

 - Collaborate closely with Research Engineers and product teams to deploy your work into real humanoid platforms and dexterous hands

 - Partner with senior researchers Yihan Hu and Wei on cross-cutting problems spanning autonomy and robotics

We’re looking for someone who has:

 - 1+ years of industry research experience, or a completed post-doc in a relevant field

 - A strong research record in robotics, manipulation, robot learning, or closely related areas, with publications in top-tier conferences or journals such as CoRL, RSS, ICRA, IROS

 - PhD in machine learning, computer vision, robotics, or a closely related field

 - Strong technical convictions and a clear point of view on where the field is going — and the self-motivation to drive that vision to execution for a team of researchers

 - Technical and professional maturity: able to operate independently as a senior IC and set direction for others

 - Passion for scalable, real-world robotics and physical AI, not just benchmark performance

Nice to have:

Hands-on experience in one or more of the following:

 - Humanoid robotics platforms, dexterous manipulation and multi-fingered hands

 - VLA/WAM and post-training for robotics

 - Large-scale RL in robotic simulation, and sim-to-real transfer

 - Imitation learning from teleoperation or human demonstration data

 - Prior Tech Lead or founding-team experience

ABOUT THE ROLE

As a technical lead for controls, you will own the technical direction of our controls stack across its full lifecycle — from 0→1 development on new vehicle platforms to hardening, calibrating, and scaling controllers across production fleets. The systems you lead are high performance and safety-critical, operating under tight timing constraints on real machines in the field.

This role spans the full controls stack: low-level actuation and vehicle characterization on one end, and high-level trajectory tracking — both lateral and longitudinal. We work on a variety of different vehicle platforms: haul trucks, excavators, wheel loaders, dozers, and other heavy equipment across construction, mining, and agriculture.

In addition to your technical leadership, you will mentor and grow the existing controls team, set priorities across competing work streams, and set the standard for best practices. We move fast and we focus on excellence, for our products and for our business. If you are hands-on and looking for a place to have a multiplying effect on making autonomous systems a reality, Applied Intuition is the place for you!




AT APPLIED INTUITION, YOU WILL:

 - Set the technical direction for the controls stack across both 0→1 platform bring-up and production programs, and see designs through from prototype to deployed fleet

 - Design and implement controllers at every level of the stack, from low-level actuator control to lateral and longitudinal trajectory tracking

 - Design safe, redundant control systems that live within a safety-critical environment.

 - Characterize the dynamics of customer vehicles across many embodiments — haul trucks, excavators, wheel loaders, dozers, and more — to create tailored controls solutions and close the gap between simulation and real-world behavior

 - Build calibration and vehicle characterization workflows that scale controls performance from a single prototype to fleets of vehicles without per-vehicle hand-tuning

 - Lead, mentor, and grow the existing controls team; set priorities, unblock engineers, and raise the technical bar through design reviews and hands-on collaboration

 - Evaluate and apply academic research to create optimal-control-based solutions using techniques like nonlinear MPC and MPPI control

 - Collaborate with customers' engineers in construction, mining, and agriculture, and manage those relationships through field deployments


WE'RE LOOKING FOR SOMEONE WHO HAS:

 - Passion for tackling challenging control problems involving a wide array of vehicles in varied and unstructured environments

 - 6+ years of experience building production software using modern software practices, including experience leading engineers or owning a technical area

 - Hands-on experience taking controls solutions from first prototype through deployment on real, production-grade vehicles

 - Demonstrated ability to mentor engineers, prioritize a team's roadmap, and drive technical decisions across multiple concurrent workstreams

 - Fluency in differential equations, numerical optimization, numerical analysis, and physics

 - Enthusiasm for coming up with practical solutions to cutting-edge challenges in a fast-paced environment, and for building towards an end-to-end strategy


NICE TO HAVE:

 - MSc or PhD in mechanical engineering, robotics, or computer science with coursework or research experience in controls

 - Experience writing safety-critical, high-performance software using modern C++

 - Experience in quadratic programming and nonlinear optimization to create robust and performant controllers

 - Experience with heavy equipment or off-road platforms in construction, mining, or agriculture

 - Experience building calibration pipelines or system identification tooling used across a fleet

The Release Management team owns the infrastructure and process that gets validated software out the door — release cuts, version uprevs, build pipelines, and artifact management — across our automotive platform. We collaborate with Program Validation for release gate sign-off and work alongside the Embedded, UX/HMI, and OTA domain teams to maintain release momentum and prevent last-minute emergencies.



About the Role

We are looking for a Build & Release Engineer to own release cuts from our Git repositories, manage uprevs (dependency/firmware version updates), build and maintain our CI/CD pipelines, and administer build artifact management. You will also own our internal Release Management portal — the system where all build artifacts and binaries are tracked, managed, and released — as its primary engineer. This hands-on software engineering position demands robust coding proficiency alongside deep CI/CD expertise, as you will actively build and maintain a live application rather than just configuring pipelines.

At Applied Intuition, you will: 

Release Engineering & Orchestration

 - Execute release cuts from Git repositories across multiple product lines and branches.

 - Manage version uprevs end to end, coordinating dependency and firmware bumps with upstream teams.

 - Define and own release branching, tagging, and versioning strategies.

 - Investigate and resolve complex build failures, coordinating fixes across development teams.

CI/CD Infrastructure

 - Design, build, and maintain scalable software release CI/CD pipelines for build, test orchestration, and deployment.

 - Automate build infrastructure to reduce manual effort and enforce pipeline quality gates.

 - Troubleshoot pipeline failures to ensure high availability and reliability for development teams.

Artifact Lifecycle Management

 - Own the artifact lifecycle, including versioning, signing, storage, and cross-environment promotion.

 - Maintain strict artifact provenance and traceability from commit to release.

 - Administer and optimize artifact repositories (e.g., Artifactory).

Internal Tooling & Portals

 - Develop and maintain the internal Release Management portal — the system of record for build artifacts, binaries, and release status.

 - Ship new features for the portal as its primary engineer, including UI, backend services, and external integrations.

 - Integrate the portal with CI/CD systems, artifact repositories, and downstream release workflows.

Cross-Functional Alignment

 - Partner with the Program Validation team and TPMs on release gate criteria and final sign-off.

 - Coordinate with domain teams (Embedded, UX/HMI, OTA etc) on release timing, risks, and blockers.

 - Communicate release status and critical path risks to stakeholders.

We're looking for someone who has:

 - Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field and graduating by December 2026. 

 - 3+ years of professional software development experience, with strong coding ability in at least one modern language (e.g., Python, Go, Java, or JavaScript/TypeScript)

 - Experience building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines (e.g., Jenkins, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Buildkite)

 - Strong Git experience, including branching, tagging, and release workflows

 - Experience with artifact management systems (e.g., JFrog Artifactory, Nexus, or equivalent)

 - Experience designing, building, or maintaining internal tools or portals

 - Strong troubleshooting skills across build, dependency, and release issues

Nice to Have:

 - Experience with containerization (Docker, Kubernetes)

 - Experience with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP)

 - Experience with embedded/automotive release processes (multi-ECU uprevs, ASPICE-aligned release workflows)

 - Experience with monitoring/observability tools (Grafana, Kibana, Splunk)

 - Experience with Jira, Polarion, or similar issue tracking tools

We're seeking a talented Engineer to work on a brand new initiative designing and developing the world representation layer at the heart of Applied Intuition's Axion simulation stack. If you've spent your time building the spatial worlds that games, simulations, or autonomous systems inhabit, defining how environments are structured, queried, and updated at high frequency this role was written for you.

This is deeply technical position sitting at the intersection of computational geometry, real-time world modeling, and large-scale simulation. You'll join a new team at the foundational scene and mapping systems that downstream sensor fusion and path planning both depend on: defining 4D spatial abstractions, Entity Component Systems, and the high-performance data structures that make multi-agent reasoning across air, ground, and maritime domains possible.

The ideal candidate has participated in a game engine, a robotics simulator, or an autonomous vehicle stack and knows what it takes to make those representations fast, accurate, and scalable under real operational constraints.




AT APPLIED INTUITION, YOU WILL:

 - Develop World & Scene Representation Systems: Design and implement core spatial data structures, including Entity Component System frameworks, spatial indexing, occupancy representations, and 4D object management for large-scale multi-agent environments.

 - Own Mapping & Geometry Pipelines: Build and optimize the computational geometry and world-state systems that sit between raw sensor data and the path planning stack — including coordinate frame management, spatial queries, and environment abstraction layers.

 - Drive Performance to the Metal: Write highly optimized C++ (C++20) with a focus on low-latency, cache-efficient, and memory-conscious design. You should be comfortable profiling hot paths, eliminating allocations, and squeezing real-time performance out of complex spatial systems.

 - Technical Strategy & Integration: Participate in driving architectural decisions and design clean APIs that enable cross-domain integration across air, ground, and maritime autonomy stacks.




WE'RE LOOKING FOR SOMEONE, WHO HAS:

 - 2+ years of professional software engineering experience, with deep expertise in spatial systems, world modeling, or simulation environments

 - Expert-level C++ skills (C++20 or later), including template metaprogramming, move semantics, SIMD, and performance optimization at the systems level

 - Hands-on experience building world or scene representations — from a game engine, sim platform, or autonomous system — including managing dynamic object state, spatial indexing, and real-time updates

 - Strong background in computational geometry: coordinate transformations, spatial data structures (BVH, octrees, k-d trees), geometric algorithms, and collision/proximity systems

 - Deep intuition for low-latency, high-throughput software design in real-time environments

 - Strong proficiency in Python and shell scripting for tooling and automation

 - Experience with agentic coding tools (Cursor, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot) and AI-assisted development workflows
   
   

Travel Requirements:

 - Must be willing to travel as projects requires; average travel varies, but can be up to once a month for up to 1 week (~20%)

Security Requirements:

 - Must be a U.S. Citizen

 - Must hold or be eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance 


For more information about U.S. security clearances: click here https://www.dcsa.mil/Personnel-Security/Background-Investigations-for-Applicants/Investigations-Clearance-Process/.




NICE TO HAVE:

 - Expertise with the Linux/Docker/C++ toolchains (including build systems like Nix and Bazel) and cross-compilation.

 - Experience with temporal reasoning systems and 4D scene representation (space + time)

 - Background in game development, simulation, or virtual environments

 - Understanding of autonomous systems or robotics software architectures

We are seeking a Learning Experience Designer to join our Vehicle Operations team to design and scale learning experiences that build the skills, knowledge, and operational readiness required to safely and effectively operate, test, maintain, and support our vehicle fleet and associated operations. This role is critical in ensuring our operators and operations staff are prepared, safe, and aligned with best practices. You'll manage training content, drive onboarding, track compliance, and work cross-functionally to improve team knowledge and performance.

This is a highly hands-on role at the intersection of Learning & Development, Vehicle Operations, Engineering, and Technology. You will work closely with Vehicle Operations leaders, subject matter experts, engineers, and other cross-functional partners to translate complex operational processes and technical requirements into practical, engaging, and measurable learning experiences.

You will own the design of learning experiences across the employee lifecycle—from onboarding and foundational skills through advanced technical training, certification, qualification, and ongoing proficiency. You will also leverage AI and emerging learning technologies to make learning more scalable, personalized, experiential, and closely connected to the flow of work.

The ideal candidate is a strong learning designer who enjoys working in complex technical environments, can quickly learn unfamiliar operational domains, and approaches learning as a capability and performance problem—not simply a content-development exercise.



At Applied Intuition, you will:

 - Design Vehicle Operations learning programs that build role-specific skills, knowledge, and operational readiness—from onboarding and foundational training through advanced technical skills, qualification, certification, and ongoing proficiency.

 - Hands-on experience testing or operating autonomous or unmanned systems in a relevant domain (air, ground, or sea)

 - Comfort and demonstrated ability working on vessels offshore for extended periods, in potentially harsh conditions

 - Experience with agile program management tooling such as Atlassian Jira

 - Strong technical writing skills, with the ability to draft clear test reports and after action reports

 - Willingness and ability to travel up to 30% of the time, including periods spent offshore on vessels of various sizes

In addition to your technical skills, you will need to be adaptable and quick to learn new technologies, as the field of deep learning and autonomous systems is rapidly evolving. Strong communication skills are essential, as you will be working in a fast-paced environment with large code bases and collaborating with cross-functional teams.

We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join our Corporate Engineering team — the team that treats Aurora's internal platform ecosystem as an engineering problem, not a ticket queue. You'll own a portfolio of SaaS platforms end-to-end: not just administering them, but understanding what each one is for, who uses it and how, how it connects to everything else, and where it should go next. Today that portfolio centers on our collaboration platforms (Google Workspace, Slack) and incident management platforms (FireHydrant, OpsGenie); over time it will change as our stack evolves — and your ability to reach deep ownership of a platform you've never touched is exactly what we're hiring for.

Support requests will cross your desk — access issues, permissions, broken workflows. Your job is not simply to work that queue; it's primarily to make categories of it disappear. You'll classify what's coming in, root-cause why it exists, and then eliminate it: automate it away, redesign the process that generates it, build self-service, or put an AI agent in the loop. If you measure your impact in classes of problems that no longer exist rather than tickets closed, this is your seat.


IN THIS ROLE YOU WILL

 - Own platforms at the architectural level. For each platform in your portfolio, be the person who can answer: what is this for, what are the use cases, how do users actually interact with it, how does identity and lifecycle flow through it, and how does it fit into Aurora's larger application ecosystem. Set the technical strategy and roadmap for the domain.

 - Engineer away toil. Treat recurring requests as bugs. Categorize inbound work, find the systemic cause, and eliminate it — through automation against platform APIs, workflow redesign, self-service tooling, or AI agents handling the loop. Write real software to do it (Python, TypeScript/JavaScript), in version control, with review.

 - Design and automate identity and lifecycle workflows — onboarding, offboarding, role changes — across the enterprise ecosystem using APIs, webhooks, SCIM, and IAM tooling (Okta, SSO) and integration platforms (e.g., Workato).

 - Lead platform lifecycle end-to-end as our stack evolves: assess and pilot new tools, drive phased rollouts and integrations, govern configuration, and deprecate what we outgrow. Define build-vs-buy and licensing strategy using usage data to keep SaaS spend disciplined.

 - Put AI to work in the enterprise. Drive adoption of Enterprise AI tooling (Claude and similar) and build agentic automation into support and business workflows — partnering with Security to do it safely.

 - Serve as the escalation point for the hardest problems on these platforms — with the standing goal that the same problem never needs escalating twice.


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - 6+ years across software engineering, systems engineering, or platform engineering, with substantial time spent building automation and integrations for enterprise/SaaS ecosystems.

 - Strong software engineering fundamentals: proficiency in at least one language (Python, TypeScript/JavaScript), working in version control with code review, and owning automations or services that run in production.

 - A demonstrated track record of eliminating manual work at scale — you can point to categories of requests or processes you made permanently disappear, not just tasks you completed.

 - Deep, hands-on experience integrating SaaS platforms via APIs, webhooks, and event-driven patterns, including identity and lifecycle automation (SSO, SCIM, Okta or similar).

 - Proven ability to take architectural ownership of a platform you didn't previously know: rapidly building a mental model of its purpose, use cases, data flows, and integration points. We care more about this adaptability than about experience with our exact stack.

 - Systems thinking across an application ecosystem — you reason about how tools connect, where data and identity flow, and what the second-order effects of a change are.

 - Proven ability to partner across teams and with senior leadership spanning IT, Software, Operations/Services, and Security.


DESIRABLE QUALIFICATIONS

 - Hands-on depth in our current stack: Google Workspace, Slack, incident management platforms (FireHydrant, OpsGenie, PagerDuty), Atlassian tools, or integration platforms like Workato.

 - Experience building LLM-powered or agentic automation (Claude, MCP, agent frameworks) for internal workflows.

 - Infrastructure as Code (e.g., Terraform), CI/CD pipelines, and hands-on experience with a major cloud platform (AWS, GCP).

 - Experience with SaaS license management, usage analytics, and cost governance.

 - Experience building reusable automation frameworks and self-service tooling used by other teams.

We’re searching for a Staff Hardware Reliability Engineer. The Hardware Reliability team is dedicated to ensuring the robustness and dependability of hardware systems in the Aurora hardware stack. Our team is responsible for designing tests, and validating the hardware components that form the backbone of Aurora’s autonomous systems, ensuring they meet the highest Automotive standards of performance and durability under our tough field conditions.

 

In this role you will

 - Lead and oversee hardware reliability testing and validation for automotive power and compute hardware used in autonomous vehicles.

 - Experience working with firmware development teams and a solid understanding of firmware and hardware interactions.

 - Demonstrated ability to lead root cause analysis and corrective action processes (e.g., 8D, 5-Why, Fishbone) for hardware reliability issues.

 - Architect Core DSP Pipelines: Lead the algorithmic strategy, modeling, and architectural implementation of end-to-end signal processing pipelines for next-generation coherent lidar systems.

 - Verification and Bring-Up: Drive the testing, verification, and performance tuning of DSP IP across simulation, hardware emulation targets, initial ASIC silicon bring-up, and real-world system testing.

Required qualifications

 - Education & Experience: BSc, MSc or Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Physics, or a related quantitative field, paired with 10+ years of relevant industry experience in advanced DSP design.

 - Advanced Mathematical & DSP Foundation: Expert-level mastery of foundational and advanced signal processing mathematics (e.g., spectral estimation, filtering, phase recovery, modulation/demodulation, detection theory and noise mitigation).

 - Relevant Cross-Industry Expertise: Proven track record applying advanced DSP principles within signal-dense domains such as modern radar systems, optical or RF telecommunications, or computational physics.

 - Embedded Hardware Targeting: Demonstrated experience mapping and optimizing high-throughput algorithms onto hardware architectures with tight latency, bandwidth, and compute constraints (FPGAs, SoC/SIMD vector engines, and/or ASICs).

 - High-Level Modeling Skills: Expert proficiency in Python, C/C++, or MATLAB for modeling, simulation, algorithmic verification, and data analysis.

 - High Speed Mixed Signal Integration: Familiarity with high-speed optical/RF front-ends, ADCs/DACs, and the associated digital impairment compensation techniques.

 - Vector & SIMD Optimization: Background writing low-level, compute-optimized code for SIMD architectures, vector engines, or modern DSP hardware accelerators.

As a Project Manager supporting Command Center Operations, you will independently lead cross-functional projects and continuous improvement initiatives that strengthen operational performance, introduce new capabilities, and support the continued evolution of Aurora’s commercial operations.

You will translate complex operational needs into structured project plans, align stakeholders across Operations, Product, Engineering, Safety, and other functions, and drive initiatives from problem definition through implementation and sustained adoption. This role requires strong judgment, operational understanding, and the ability to create structure, manage competing priorities, and drive measurable results in a fast-paced and ambiguous environment.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Independently lead moderately complex projects from definition through implementation, establishing scope, milestones, dependencies, risks, resource needs, and measures of success.

 - Manage multiple concurrent initiatives, balancing shifting priorities, resource constraints, and cross-functional dependencies to deliver against business objectives.

 - Use operational metrics, performance trends, and stakeholder feedback to identify improvement opportunities, prioritize work, and implement sustainable changes.

 - Lead cross-functional teams across Operations, Engineering, Safety, and other partners to define requirements, align ownership, resolve dependencies, and drive decisions and execution.

 - Proactively identify project risks and operational constraints, develop mitigation plans, and escalate material issues with clear recommendations and tradeoffs.

 - Develop and improve scalable processes, standard operating procedures, and operating mechanisms that strengthen Command Center reliability, effectiveness, and operational readiness.

 - Drive successful adoption of new technologies, tools, workflows, and operational capabilities through implementation planning, stakeholder communication, readiness, and post-launch evaluation.

 - Provide leadership with clear visibility into project progress, performance, risks, decisions, and outcomes, translating lessons learned into ongoing continuous improvement.


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Safety-focused, operationally minded, with the ability to understand interconnected systems and evaluate impacts across safety, engineering, operations, and customer outcomes.

 - 5+ years of experience in project management, program management, operations, or a related field.

 - Demonstrated experience leading cross-functional initiatives from planning through implementation.

 - Experience managing multiple concurrent projects or initiatives, including scope, milestones, dependencies, risks, resource constraints, and measures of success.

 - Strong problem-solving and situational judgment, with the ability to create structure in ambiguity, evaluate tradeoffs, and determine when escalation is required.

 - An understanding of development operations and the ability to relate them to commercial operations.

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to influence, align, and gain cooperation from cross-functional stakeholders.

 - Experience using data, metrics, dashboards, or reporting tools to identify trends, inform decisions, and communicate project or operational performance.

 - Ability to work independently, create structure in ambiguous situations, and exercise sound judgment in time-critical environments.


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience in autonomous vehicles, technology, logistics, transportation, or another operationally complex environment.

 - Experience supporting remote operations, teleoperations, operational technology deployments, product launches, or new capability rollouts.

 - Experience with project management tools such as Jira, Smartsheet, Asana, MS Project, or similar platforms.

 - Experience with data visualization or reporting tools such as Power BI, Tableau, advanced Excel, or similar platforms.

 - Experience with continuous improvement methodologies such as PMP, Lean Six Sigma, Agile/Scrum, or similar project or process improvement certifications.

 - Technical fluency or familiarity with tools such as SQL, Python, or similar technologies.
