As a Software Engineer on our Labelling and Data Automation team, you will build pipelines, tools, and workflows to accelerate the development of our AI-first self-driving technology.  The Labelling & Data Automation team plays a critical role in Waabi’s training pipeline.  We are one of the first steps in the process of training machine learning models and are responsible for building practical, scalable tools and automation for extracting interesting and relevant data, creating high-quality ground truth labels, and providing this data to our expert machine learning scientists and engineers.
 
You will..
- Design and implement tools, pipelines, and metrics to accelerate the development of our AI-first autonomy system and generative AI simulator. 
- Own the process, criteria, and tooling for efficiently finding interesting and relevant data across the petabytes of real world data that Waabi has collected
- Build high reliability systems for extracting and labelling the interesting data with various vendors and integrate it back into our system
- Work with both internal and third party stakeholders to define taxonomy, validation rules and success criteria for our labelling projects
- Design and manage the end-to-end deployment of data solutions to deliver high quality labelled data for various ML teams to use in experiments and model improvement
- Deploy open-set / embedding models to our production environment - empowering new search and curation modalities
- Champion engineering excellence, ensuring high-quality, well structured, and tested code.
- Contribute to project roadmap planning, prioritization, and delivery.
 
Qualifications: 
- 4+ years of industry experience.
- Bachelor's in computer science, engineering, machine learning, or a related technical discipline.
- Proficient in Python programming and strong software engineering fundamentals with real-world experience writing high quality, well-structured, and well-tested code.  
- A willingness and ability to learn new skills, technologies, and software libraries as required. 
- Strong experience with data pipelines for large-scale processing and analysis.
- Strong communication and organizational skills 
- Understanding of cloud job orchestration, monitoring, and instrumentation best-practices.
- Open-minded and collaborative team player with the willingness to help others.
- Passionate about self-driving technologies, solving hard problems, and creating innovative solutions.
 
Bonus Points:
- Experience with ML pipelines, including dataset curation, labelling, training and evaluation. 
- Previous experience in self-driving technology or related fields.
- Familiar with linear algebra (projections, transforms) and 3D geometry.
- Experience with MapReduce frameworks (Apache Hadoop/Spark) or orchestration frameworks (Apache Airflow/Apache Beam/Google Dataflow/AWS Step Functions).
- Experience with with front end development
- Experience working with open-set / embedding models and deploying them in a production setting
- Experience working with infra as code (Terraform, CloudFormation, etc)

About the Role
Waabi's Commercial Product team defines and delivers the end-to-end commercial product that makes autonomous trucking deployable, scalable, and valuable to customers. We sit between autonomy, operations, business development, and customers, turning driverless capability into a real-world product that can be launched, sold, operated, and scaled.
We are hiring a Staff Commercial Product Manager to own critical commercial product workstreams that bring the Waabi Driver to market. This person will define the operating models, service capabilities, partner workflows, and customer-facing product requirements required to bring the Waabi Driver to market and scale it from commercial pilots into a broader autonomous trucking network.
This is not a traditional software PM role. You will help define how autonomous trucking commercialization works in the real world: how trucks launch and land, how missions are monitored, how exceptions are handled, how customers are onboarded, how partners integrate, how sites are qualified, and how the product scales.
What You'll Do
You will own high-impact commercial product workstreams end-to-end. Near-term areas of focus may include Command Center / fleet oversight, Life of a Load (end-to-end service delivery), launch and land operations, AV hubs and customer launch sites, Waabi Services (maintenance, inspections, roadside, data offload, mission support, customer operations), partner and ecosystem integration, and pilot-to-scale playbooks.
Across those workstreams, you will:
Define the "how" behind novel autonomous trucking challenges through process mapping, operating model design, requirements definition, and cross-functional alignment.
Translate customer, operations, autonomy, and business needs into clear product requirements and deployment plans.
Build structured frameworks for site readiness, service design, partner integration, customer onboarding, launch readiness, and operational scalability.
Build repeatable pilot-to-scale playbooks that move customers, lanes, and sites from pilot to qualified, mature, and driverless-ready deployments.
Lead cross-functional workstreams with autonomy, operations, engineering, business development, safety, legal, and external partners.
Drive workshops with internal teams and external partners, including agenda design, decision framing, progress tracking, and follow-through.
Identify key tradeoffs across customer value, autonomy readiness, operational complexity, cost, speed, and long-term scalability.
Inform partnership requirements and operating models with OEMs, customers, service providers, and facility partners, in close partnership with BD.
Produce executive-ready decision memos, operating playbooks, and product artifacts for your workstreams.
Work closely with engineering and autonomy teams to understand technical constraints, risks, readiness levels, and product implications.
Communicate clearly with technical, operational, commercial, and executive audiences.
What Success Looks Like
Success in this role means you have helped Waabi move from promising autonomous capability to a commercially deployable trucking product. Specifically, you will have:
Turned ambiguous commercial problems into clear product requirements, operating models, and execution plans.
Created scalable playbooks that reduce friction for future customers, lanes, sites, and partners.
Helped internal teams make faster, better trade-off decisions.
Built trust with operations, autonomy, engineering, commercial teams, and external partners.
Improved Waabi’s ability to launch, operate, support, and scale driverless trucking missions.
Created artifacts and systems that become foundational to Waabi’s commercial deployment model.
Qualifications
Required
8+ years in product management, operations, strategy, or program leadership in a complex technical/operational environment (autonomous vehicles, trucking, freight, logistics, robotics, or other physical-AI deployment)
Demonstrated experience standing up an operating model from scratch in a physical-world business — services + workflows + tools, not just software
Track record of designing, launching, or scaling complex B2B products, services, programs, or operating models
Strong systems thinking and first-principles judgment — able to break ambiguous problems into clear frameworks, requirements, decisions, and execution plans
Track record of leading cross-functional initiatives without formal authority
Executive-grade written and verbal communication
High EQ, low ego, and bias toward ownership and action
Strongly Preferred
Experience with B2B enterprise customers, strategic partnerships, OEMs, or service provider ecosystems
Experience designing operational processes, customer onboarding flows, service models, or scaled deployment playbooks
Zero-to-one product or program experience at an early-stage or scaling startup
Direct experience in autonomous trucking, freight tech, or AV commercialization (vs. adjacent physical-AI domains)
Track record of owning end-to-end outcomes, not just deliverables (e.g., business unit, product line, or service area ownership).
Nice to have
Experience working with internal or outsourced operations teams
Experience standing up or scaling a Command Center, NOC, fleet operations function, or similar 24/7 operating environment
MBA

With offices in Toronto, San Francisco, Dallas, and Pittsburgh, Waabi is growing quickly and looking for diverse, innovative and collaborative candidates who want to impact the world in a positive way. To learn more visit: www.waabi.ai


Waabi builds generative AI for the physical world, starting with autonomous trucks. The intelligence only ships if the system underneath it is safe by design — and that safety has to be carried all the way down, from the vehicle-level safety concept into the embedded platform's requirements, architecture, and interfaces.
As a Systems Engineer on our Embedded Systems team, you'll own that translation. Our overarching systems and safety group defines the vehicle-level safety concept — the hazard analysis, the safety goals, the functional safety concept. You'll be their embedded counterpart: taking that concept and decomposing it into an embedded architecture and technical safety requirements that our electrical engineering and embedded software groups can build against. You'll live on the left side of the ISO 26262 V at the embedded level, turning a functional safety concept into technical requirements and a hardware/software architecture the whole team can trust — and you'll be the person who keeps the embedded org fluent in the wider world of automotive standards.
You Will…
Partner with the systems and safety group. Take the vehicle-level safety concept, safety goals, and functional safety requirements as your inputs, and feed embedded expertise back into their hazard analysis and concept work. You're the bridge between their concept and our hardware and firmware.
Own the embedded technical safety concept. Derive technical safety requirements from the functional safety concept allocated to the embedded system, and allocate each to the right architectural element.
Architect across hardware and software. Define the embedded system architecture and the hardware/software partition, including the hardware-software interface (HSI), so both groups design against one coherent picture.
Manage requirements and traceability. Maintain bidirectional traceability from the safety goals handed down to you all the way to hardware and software requirements, and keep the work products that feed the safety case.
Steward automotive standards for the embedded org. Stay current on the standards that apply to our work — functional safety, SOTIF, cybersecurity, autonomous-product safety, process and component qualification — and fold them into how the embedded team designs, documents, and works day to day.
Set up the right side of the V. Your requirements and architecture define what verification and validation later prove. You'll partner closely with the V&V effort — and support Development Interface Agreements (DIAs) with OEM partners and suppliers — without owning the downstream test execution yourself.
Qualifications
BS/MS in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a related field — or equivalent hands-on experience.
8+ years in embedded systems, with real depth spanning both hardware and software.
Strong ISO 26262 experience concentrated on the system-design phase (Part 4) and its handoffs to hardware (Part 5) and software (Part 6): deriving technical safety requirements from a functional safety concept, system architectural design, and hardware/software allocation.
Working familiarity with the broader automotive standards landscape — and the judgment to operationalize it — including SOTIF (ISO 21448), automotive cybersecurity (ISO/SAE 21434), autonomous-product safety cases (UL 4600), Automotive SPICE (ASPICE), and component/coding standards such as AEC-Q10.
Fluency with requirements management and traceability — you've lived in a tool like Polarion and know why traceability matters when the safety case is questioned.
Enough range to read a schematic and reason about embedded C/C++/Rust, so your hardware/software partitioning is grounded in what each side can actually implement.
A clear grasp of the full V, so the left-side work you produce genuinely sets the right side up to succeed.
Nice-to-haves
Experience standing up or maturing a standard (ASPICE, 21434, or similar) inside an engineering org, not just complying with one.
SysML or model-based systems engineering.
AV, ADAS, or other complex safety-critical domain experience.
Direct experience authoring or negotiating DIAs with an OEM.

Produce written evaluations precise enough for engineering to act on, separating baseline from novel behavior and stating whether it reproduces.
Execute vehicle dynamics and characterization campaigns — tire evaluation, trailer stability, axle-weight verification — including offsite testing at partner proving grounds.
Serve as the qualified evaluator for operator certification: administer Knowledge and Proficiency
Checks and clear operators onto a platform.
Author and maintain platform-specific operator documentation — start-up and shutdown sequences, known-behavior references, SOP input.
Own the DOT and CVSA compliance read on new platforms.
Train operators on new platforms and move platform knowledge between sites ahead of any handover.
Escalate safety-relevant findings and stop testing when equipment or vehicle behavior warrants it. Document the basis for that call.
 
Qualifications:
8+ years as a Vehicle Operator, commercial test driver, or in a technically equivalent Class 8 operations role, including 4 years on autonomous or ADAS-equipped vehicles.
CDL Class A, current Medical Examiner's Certificate, and a clean driving record, background check, and drug screen.
Strong technical aptitude with autonomy platforms.
Demonstrated ability to characterize vehicle behavior precisely: consistent versus intermittent, reproducible versus one-off, with conditions and magnitude rather than impressions.
Strong written communication skills, translating in-cab observation into reports operations, engineering and safety can act on without follow-up.
Demonstrated familiarity with closed-course and proving-ground protocols, including edge-case and failure-mode testing.
Solid understanding of FMCSA and DOT requirements for test and development vehicles — DVIR, Hours of Service, DOT annual inspection, CVSA out-of-service criteria, and 49 CFR Parts 393 and 396.
Experience training, coaching, or certifying other commercial drivers is highly desirable.
CVSA Enhanced Pre-trip certification, Proving ground experience or licenses, a strong plus.
Comfort maintaining written documentation and willingness to learn the team's reporting tooling.
Passion for self-driving technologies, solving hard problems, and building a culture of safety and operational excellence.
Ability to work flexible shifts, including days, nights, and weekends.
Travel to other operational sites and partner proving grounds will be required.
Day Shift Schedule and Flexibility:
Base shift: 7:30 AM – 4:30 PM MT. Day shift crews are expected to be flexible.

As a member of Waabi’s Training and Compliance Team, you’ll be the primary hands-on trainer and subject matter expert responsible for developing our Fleet Specialist (FS) workforce—the team that keeps our autonomous trucks running safely and efficiently in the field.  You will partner closely with the Training Manager to design, build, and continually iterate learning programs.
 
Drawing on your own experience as a Fleet Specialist, you will deliver the technical curriculum that builds FS proficiency in vehicle systems, hardware and software interfaces, troubleshooting procedures, Platform Shakeout Tests, and Mixed Reality Training scenarios. With cutting-edge autonomous technology and an uncompromising commitment to safety, we’re shaping the future of autonomous trucking, and we need technically sharp, experienced professionals like you to ensure every Fleet Specialist is fully certified and operationally ready before they ever support a live deployment.
 
 
You will…
Partner with the Training Manager to design, develop, and update technical learning materials, SOPs, job aids, interactive modules, and assessment using established instructional design methodologies (e.g., ADDIE, SAM).
Directly conduct new-hire onboarding for Fleet Specialists, executing the full training curriculum from classroom instruction through field certification.
Deliver structured instruction across all VO and  FS phases.
Participate in VO and FS training ridealongs as a Fleet Specialist resource, providing trainees with real-time context on vehicle systems, operational support responsibilities, and FS-VO coordination in the field.
Guide FS trainees to meet all defined proficiency thresholds.
Serve as the primary technical instructor for autonomous vehicle systems, onboard hardware, software interfaces, diagnostic tools, and fleet support procedures used by Fleet Specialists.
Deliver and assess Platform Shakeout Test (PST) training and Mixed Reality Training (MRT) modules, ensuring all FSs can execute these procedures accurately, independently, and safely.
Execute the continuous learning framework by delivering refresher training and recertification following new SOPs, truck upfits, software updates, and feature releases.
Act as a key liaison between the Training Manager and Dispatch (FS Supervisors) to ensure engineering-driven changes are translated into clear, executable field instruction.
Utilize the Daily Training Tracker and Jira update processes to formally log and monitor FS trainee progress and ongoing development activities.
Mentor high-performing Fleet Specialists through the Senior FS Trainer (Train-the-Trainer) program and support delivery of the Demo Readiness Certification.
Support the Training Manager in overseeing training schedules, tracking completion metrics, managing LMS records, and driving continuous improvement across all FS learning programs. 
 
Qualifications:
Minimum of 3+ years of direct experience as a Fleet Specialist or in a technically equivalent field operations role supporting autonomous or Class 8 vehicles.
Strong technical aptitude with hands-on experience diagnosing, troubleshooting, and operating autonomous vehicle systems, onboard hardware, and software interfaces.
Demonstrated familiarity with fleet support procedures including Platform Shakeout Tests, Mixed Reality Training scenarios, and pre/post-trip inspection protocols.
Demonstrated ability to deliver structured, safety-critical training and conduct performance assessments in a hands-on field environment.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to translate complex technical concepts into clear, actionable instruction for trainees at all experience levels.
Strong organizational skills and meticulous attention to detail, including consistent and accurate record-keeping in LMS or tracking systems.
Passion for self-driving technologies, solving hard problems, and building a culture of safety and operational excellence.
Occasional travel to other operational sites may be required.
 
Bonus:
Experience with Learning Management Systems (LMS) and training record administration.
Prior experience delivering formal training, coaching, or mentorship to peers or new hires in a technical field operations environment.
Experience as a certified trainer or assessor, including participation in a Train-the-Trainer or similar instructor certification program.
Familiarity with Jira, dispatch systems, or fleet management software used in autonomous trucking operations.

Waabi is building generative AI for the physical world, starting with autonomous trucks. Our Texas road operations run both R&D testing and revenue freight out of our Lancaster terminal, and day shift is the core of that operation.
Vehicle Operators are the professional drivers behind the program. You will manually drive Class 8 combination vehicles, supervise the Waabi Driver on public roadways and test tracks, and provide the experienced judgment that keeps our testing and commercial operations safe. On day shift you run the highest mission volume we operate, with the full operations and engineering team around you. The Waabi Driver improves because experienced operators tell us precisely what they saw and why they took control; that feedback loop is the core of the job.
 
You will…
Manually drive Class 8 commercial vehicles and passenger vehicles safely and compliantly, including mapping and shadow missions, yard moves, transports, drayage, scouting, and repositioning.
Operate Class 8 autonomous vehicles on public roadways and test tracks in supervised autonomy, maintaining readiness to assume manual control at any moment.
Apply Waabi’s Takeover Guidance and Policy Takeovers, maintaining floating-hands or slip-grip technique, active mirror scanning, and priority callouts for upcoming intentions and actors.
Disengage when a safety, stranding, or reputational risk requires it, and provide the specific situational detail our engineers need. Disengagement counts are not individual performance metrics; failing to disengage when required is.
Complete pre-trip inspections and post-trip Driver Vehicle Inspection Reports in Fleetio with clear, complete photo documentation, and support the Enhanced Inspection Program where trained and certified.
Maintain accurate Motive ELD records throughout the shift and manage your clock proactively so loads can be completed compliantly.
Exit the cab to visually assess surroundings whenever conditions warrant, including tight maneuvers and after more than two pull-ups, and use standard hand signals and a spotter for backing.
Review and follow platform-specific SOPs and startup procedures for each truck platform you are assigned to, including power-on sequencing and overnight charging.
Operate customer loads to committed gate, departure, and arrival times, verify tractor and trailer condition and weight, follow the fueling, weighing, and inspection sequence, and communicate delays as early as possible.
Provide clear, specific feedback about vehicle performance and capability, and support your Fleet Specialist in producing high-quality annotations.
Support other crews, the fleet technicians, and facilities when out of the truck, including 5-S standards, readiness work, and SOP documentation.
Maintain and improve Waabi’s culture of excellence in safety, and speak up immediately when something is not right.
 
Qualifications:
Class A Commercial Driver’s License and a valid DOT medical certification.
Minimum of three years of recent commercial driving experience with combination vehicles.
Exemplary motor vehicle record, background check, and DOT drug and alcohol screening results, reviewed on an individualized basis.
Demonstrated ability to use an electronic logging device and to manage Hours of Service compliance independently.
Ability to work in a fast-paced, frequently changing environment where priorities and schedules move.
Able and willing to work the day shift described below, including flexible start and end times and extended, potentially consecutive shifts of up to approximately 14 hours (following DOT regulations), plus weekend, holiday, and overnight travel.
Open-minded, collaborative team player with a willingness to help others and to work closely with a Fleet Specialist and with operations, engineering, and other cross-functional partners.
Able to give clear, specific verbal and written feedback about vehicle behavior.
Basic computer skills and the ability to learn Waabi’s mission, fleet, and inspection tooling quickly.
Passionate about self-driving technology, solving hard problems, and creating innovative solutions.
Previous autonomous vehicle, robotics, or vehicle testing experience, substantial prior long-haul or team-driving experience, and experience troubleshooting computer systems are all a strong plus.
Enhanced Pre-trip Inspector (EIP) certification and a million-mile safe driving record or equivalent recognition are a plus.
 
Day Shift Schedule and Flexibility:
Base shift: 7:00 AM – 5:00 PM CT, based at Waabi’s Lancaster, TX terminal.
Start and end times may shift. The shift may begin earlier or end later based on commercial and customer demand and when loads need to move. Day shift crews are expected to be flexible.

About Woven by Toyota
Woven by Toyota will contribute to Toyota's transformation into a once-in-a-century mobility company. Inspired by our history of inventing "for someone other than ourselves," our mission is to broaden the definition of mobility, expand how mobility contributes to society, and continue challenging the norms of mobility through human-centered innovation. 

We operate around four pillars: AD/ADAS for autonomous driving and advanced driver assistance system technologies; Arene, a vehicle software production platform for SDVs (Software Defined Vehicles); Woven City, a mobility test course; and Cloud & AI, the digital infrastructure that supports our collaboration foundation. Additionally, essential business functions underpin the implementation of these teams, and together we are working toward realizing a "zero-accident society" and "mass production of happiness."

About the Team
Our team is working to build and innovate cutting-edge SIL (Software-in-the-Loop) environments to further advance autonomous driving technology. Currently, we focus on two environments, ClosedSILS and OpenSILS, and conduct efficient software evaluation and verification while maximizing the characteristics of each. In addition, we are also focusing on speeding up processing speeds, which are essential for improving development efficiency. 
In ClosedSILS, simulators are connected in real time to autonomous driving software, forming feedback loops to dynamically evaluate dynamics and vehicle control logic. In this environment, efforts are underway to improve the accuracy of simulation models themselves and technology development to accurately link generated signals to actual vehicle behavior. Additionally, computational optimization and load reduction technologies are introduced to process simulations more quickly, aiming to simultaneously enhance the speed and accuracy of the development process. 
On the other hand, OpenSILS provides a foundation for verifying software behavior offline by utilizing log data from actual vehicle driving. In particular, faithfully reproducing events such as communication delays and processing delays caused by CPU load in real vehicle environments has become a crucial theme. OpenSILS not only fed log data obtained from real vehicles but also applies corrections based on load conditions and processing timing, advancing technology development that reproduces events under the same conditions as real vehicles in virtual environments. This approach enables efficient identification of root causes of problems occurring in real vehicles and effective software improvements. 
A common challenge for both ClosedSILS and OpenSILS is the acceleration of processing speed. By maximizing real-time simulation performance and providing a test environment optimized to the extreme, both have features that dramatically accelerate software development. Through this series of initiatives, we are solving the safety and reliability challenges faced by autonomous driving technology and building a future-oriented development foundation. 
Our activities provide a comprehensive environment ideal for the development of autonomous driving technology by integrating simulation with real-world vehicle data analysis. As engineers, we can take on new challenges and grow in an environment where we can contribute to future mobility technologies. 

Desired Candidates
Our team is committed to supporting the evolution of autonomous driving technology and is seeking individuals who are eager to build and improve SIL environments. We especially welcome those with the following skills and experience: 
Knowledge of simulation technology: Experience building simulation environments and feedback loops using ClosedSILS and OpenSILS.
Data Analysis Technology: Skills that accurately model and reproduce load conditions and processing delays by utilizing log data obtained from actual vehicles.
Real-time processing optimization: Understanding and practical experience in computational optimization and parallel processing technologies to achieve high-speed processing within SIL environments.
Challenge to improve accuracy: Driven by a deep understanding of simulation models, we are eager to improve the linkage accuracy between actual vehicle behavior and actual vehicle behavior.
In this role, you will deeply understand how software logic is reflected in real vehicles, contributing to solving safety and reliability challenges facing the industry. Additionally, by improving real-time performance and event analysis accuracy, you can jointly build the foundation for next-generation autonomous driving technologies. 
At our site, we provide an environment where we can solve problems by combining a wide range of expertise—including computer science, embedded systems, control logic design, and simulation technology. We are an ideal team for those who want to boldly tackle new technical challenges and pursue further growth as engineers.

Woven by Toyota is enabling Toyota’s once-in-a-century transformation into a mobility company. Business-critical functions empower these teams to execute, and together, we’re working toward one bold goal: a world with zero accidents and enhanced well-being for all.

=========================================================================

TEAM
Toyota is redefining what it means to
move
. We're challenging the current state of mobility by enhancing the movement of people, goods, information and energy. Centered around three core concepts - A Living Laboratory™, Human-Centered, and Ever Evolving City™ - Woven City serves as a test course for mobility to fulfill our purpose of well-being for all.
We do this by bringing together a diverse community of people with a shared passion for the future of mobility to co-create, develop and refine innovative products and services. This cross-section of social infrastructure, mobility, and people provides a unique opportunity for inventors, residents and visitors to interact seamlessly with new technologies throughout daily life in an environment that emulates a real city.
The Info Mobility Car team in the Mobility BU develops driver support features that provide driving suggestions
and voice prompts to drivers.
We aim to enable safer and more comfortable driving experiences by leveraging　in-cabin and external camera images and various vehicle sensor data, with driver “busyness” and state estimation algorithms as our core technology.
Working closely with software development teams and simulation-based evaluation teams, we continuously drive performance improvements of these features.
For more information about Woven City, please visit:
https://www.woven-city.global/

WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR?
We are looking for someone who can lead the development of ML-based algorithms that estimate driver
workload (busyness) by combining vehicle CAN signals, various in-vehicle sensors, and driver operation logs
as time-series data.
We welcome candidates who can leverage their expertise in driver state estimation, vehicle dynamics, sensor fusion, and machine learning to design and refine robust driver workload indices, while balancing them with other workload indicators such as surrounding-vehicle and vision-based measures.
We envision someone who is comfortable working in a high-uncertainty domain, iteratively testing hypotheses
with data, and collaborating with stakeholders to translate technical outcomes into product value.

RESPONSIBILITIES
Design, implement, and enhance ML-based driver workload (busyness) estimation algorithms that take vehicle CAN signals, various in-vehicle sensors, and driver operation logs as time-series inputs
Build and operate training data infrastructure and evaluation pipelines, including label and annotation policy design, data preprocessing, and feature engineering
Investigate and improve logics that combine CAN-based workload indicators with other workload measures, such as surrounding-vehicle information and image/vision-based indicators
Design interfaces and specifications to feed workload estimation results into driving suggestion and voice prompt logic, and continuously improve overall feature performance
Collaborate with software engineers, test engineers, UX members, and other stakeholders to align on requirements and evaluation metrics, and to organize and share experiment results and technical learnings
Participate, as required by projects and business needs, in planning and conducting evaluations using simulators and on-road test vehicles (including business trips), and drive improvement cycles based on real-world findings

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS
3+ years of practical experience in software or algorithm development primarily using vehicle CAN signals, in-vehicle sensors, and driver operation logs as time-series data
Practical experience developing algorithms using machine learning, deep learning, and/or statistical modeling
Development experience in Python using major ML/DL frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow)
Ability to independently drive the end-to-end ML development process from data preprocessing and feature design through training and evaluation
Communication skills to work with multiple stakeholders and clearly explain technical topics and evaluation results
Willingness to travel for business purposes as required by project or business needs
Business level Japanese proficiency and conversational level English

NICE TO HAVES
Ability and willingness to work at the Susono office
Development or evaluation experience in domains such as in-vehicle systems, driver assistance (ADAS), driver monitoring, or robotics
Experience in feature engineering and developing driver workload or driver state estimation algorithms using vehicle CAN signals, various in-vehicle sensors, and driver operation logs as time-series data
Experience deploying ML models to production, including edge/embedded optimization, inference pipeline construction, and model operations
Experience using simulators (e.g., Unity) for algorithm evaluation or data generation

move
. We're challenging the current state of mobility by enhancing the movement of people, goods, information and energy. Centered around three core concepts - A Living Laboratory™, Human-Centered, and Ever Evolving City™ - Woven City serves as a test course for mobility to fulfill our purpose of well-being for all.
We do this by bringing together a diverse community of people with a shared passion for the future of mobility to co-create, develop and refine innovative products and services. This cross-section of social infrastructure, mobility, and people provides a unique opportunity for inventors, residents and visitors to interact seamlessly with new technologies throughout daily life in an environment that emulates a real city.
Our team, Digital Twin Platform, as one of the core Social Infrastructures & Platforms teams under the Woven City umbrella, is responsible for contributing to the realization of Woven City's vision: "To pave the way towards the next generation of movement on a test course that empowers innovation."
By developing a robust software platform, on one hand to enable inventors and business owners to “test” their products in a virtual environment before deploying to the physical Woven City; on the other hand, to create analytics to assist in decision making based on both simulated results and more importantly operational data collected from the physical city, such as residents daily life, traffic dynamics, energy consumption, etc.
As the Digital Twin Platform is still in its early growth phase, you'll have the rare chance to influence not just what we build but how we bring it to market and experiment with different business models as the platform and its commercial strategy mature together.
For more information about Woven City, please visit:
https://www.woven-city.global/

Velocity management based on the acquired data by autonomous sensors and lane information from a high-precision map.
Virtual development and validation with closed-simulation models.
Optimal velocity and driving planning algorithms subject to environmental, perceptual capabilities, high-precision map and actuation constraints.
Cross-functional discussions about vehicle controller and actuator performance, and contribute to motion control design reviews

TEAM
Arene’s goal is to open vehicle programming to everyone by simplifying vehicle software development and increasing deployment frequency without compromising safety and security. This will create a whole new market of vehicle application developers who, through software, integrate a vehicle into our daily lives in novel ways. Arene aims to significantly improve how vehicles are designed and developed, and we’re working closely with Toyota to realize this goal in its next-generation vehicles.
 
The Arene Tools Engineering team’s mission is to streamline software delivery and enhance operational speed in the automotive industry by developing innovative test, emulation, and simulation systems. We aim to facilitate quicker software releases and elevate the overall quality of automotive solutions, maintaining an uncompromised commitment to safety. With the Tools Engineering department, the Test Rigs team delivers vehicle computer hardware emulation  and simulation environments, or "virtual vehicles," to facilitate the "shift-left" approach in software development. This supports automotive software engineers' technical requirements in collaboration with hardware and software suppliers.
 
WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR?
The ideal candidate for this role comes from a strong embedded software engineering background. This individual would have experience working with modern C++, Linux O.S. or Real-Time Operating Systems.
We are looking for software engineers who are excited to help build a state-of-the-art automotive platform that is “software first”. We envision the Arene platform will change the way vehicles are made. Our team is developing tools and systems using modern software techniques, and we need software engineers who excel at building robust software systems to solve challenging problems at scale.

Woven by Toyota is enabling Toyota’s once-in-a-century transformation into a mobility company. Business-critical functions empower these teams to execute, and together, we’re working toward one bold goal: a world with zero accidents and enhanced well-being for all.

=========================================================================

TEAM
Our team specializes in developing and advancing cutting-edge Software-in-the-Loop (SIL) environments to accelerate the evolution of autonomous driving technology. We utilize two key SIL environments, ClosedSILS and OpenSILS, leveraging their unique characteristics to efficiently evaluate and validate software. Additionally, we focus on addressing shared challenges, such as improving processing speeds, which are essential for enhancing development efficiency.
In ClosedSILS, the simulator is connected to the autonomous driving software in real time, forming a feedback loop that enables dynamic evaluation of vehicle dynamics and control logic. This environment is designed with precision in mind, as we strive to improve the accuracy of simulation models while ensuring that generated signals are correctly linked to actual vehicle behavior. Furthermore, we are implementing computational optimizations and load reduction techniques to accelerate the simulation process. These enhancements aim to boost both the speed and reliability of testing, thereby significantly improving the overall development workflow.
OpenSILS, on the other hand, leverages on-road driving log data to validate software behavior in an offline setting. A key focus here is achieving high fidelity in reproducing real-world phenomena, such as communication delays or processing delays caused by CPU load observed in physical environments. OpenSILS doesn't simply replay log data—it integrates adjustments based on the load and timing conditions recorded during real-world operation. This approach enables the environment to replicate situations under conditions that closely mirror those of the original vehicle. By doing so, we can analyze issues that occurred during physical testing, pinpoint underlying causes, and effectively drive improvements in software development.
A shared challenge across both ClosedSILS and OpenSILS is the need for faster processing. By optimizing real-time capabilities within the simulation environments, we aim to deliver highly efficient testing platforms that drastically accelerate software development cycles. These ongoing initiatives address critical issues of safety and reliability in autonomous driving technology while laying the foundation for future-focused development.
Our activities integrate simulation modeling, real-world data analysis, embedded system design, and comprehensive software development, creating an optimal environment for autonomous driving innovation. Working in this challenging yet rewarding setting will enable engineers to grow their skills while contributing to foundational advancements in next-generation mobility technology.

WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR?
We are seeking driven individuals who are passionate about supporting the evolution of autonomous driving technology and actively contributing to the development and enhancement of SIL environments. We especially welcome candidates with the following skills and experience:
Knowledge of Simulation Technology: Experience with simulation environments like ClosedSILS and OpenSILS, as well as constructing and utilizing feedback loops
Data Analysis Skills: Expertise in leveraging real-world log data to accurately model and reproduce operational conditions such as load variance and processing delays
Real-Time Optimization: Understanding of computational optimization and parallel processing techniques to achieve high-speed processing within SIL environments
Commitment to Improving Accuracy: A deep understanding of simulation models and a drive to enhance the linkage precision between simulated signals and actual vehicle behavior
In this role, you will be involved in thoroughly understanding how software logic translates into real-world vehicle performance, while contributing to solving safety and reliability challenges in the industry. By optimizing real-time capabilities and improving the accuracy of phenomena analysis, you will help build the foundation for next-generation autonomous driving technology.
Our team environment is designed to integrate diverse expertise in computer science, embedded systems, control logic design, and simulation technology to tackle complex challenges. It is an ideal place for individuals who are eager to face new technical challenges and seek personal and professional growth as engineers.

Enhancing simulation model accuracy and developing signal mapping techniques
Evaluating vehicle control logic through real-time feedback loops
Optimizing systems to achieve faster processing for high-load operations

Developing technologies to accurately reproduce phenomena using real-world driving log data

About the Team
Arene's mission is to create platforms and technologies for software-defined vehicles, supporting Toyota's efforts to evolve cars every day. Arene provides a software platform that enables Toyota and its partner companies to develop, deploy, and continuously improve in-vehicle software faster, safer, and more flexibly. 
In this position, you will work as part of the Arene product management team at the Nihonbashi (Tokyo) site, working closely in collaboration with Arene's engineering, design, commercialization teams, and as partners with Toyota Motor Corporation. 

Desired Candidates
At Arene, we are looking for product managers who understand complex technology platforms and can translate them into clear product strategies that create measurable value for customers, users, and businesses. In an evolving organization, you must be someone who can shape insights from customers and markets into a focused roadmap, collaborate with technology leaders to launch products, and drive continuous improvement. 
This position is intended for individuals with foundational skills necessary for robust product development—such as problem setting, discovery, requirements definition, and prioritization—as well as the ability to lead technically advanced and safety-critical automotive operations. We welcome those who communicate clearly with internal and external executives and engineers, and who can design and operate documentation, meetings, and regular processes to enable cross-functional teams to work in a consistent direction, rather than managing every detail themselves. 

Business Activities
Arane's Product Manager is responsible for leading consensus building across six core areas throughout the product lifecycle and cross-functional teams. 
Discovery: Insights into customers, users, markets, and competitors
For the products in charge, always keep up to date and evidence-based understanding of customer needs, user needs, and market trends.
Integrate input from UX research, commercialization, partnerships, and field teams to clearly define challenges and consolidate and clarify them into growth and business opportunities.
Collaborate with technical benchmarking, competitor intelligence, and data teams to understand Arene's market position and differentiation opportunities.
Requirements definition: Defining what and why to build
Responsible for defining roadmaps, features and requirements, and Epic (Problem Definition, Use Cases, Acceptance Criteria, Business Value, Success Metrics) for the products you are responsible for
Collaborate with product planners responsible for roadmaps and release processes to review and understand clearly prioritized and well-structured proposals, and include them in the planning process
Collaborate with technical leads, systems/architecture, UX, and project management to verify the feasibility and scope validity of defined content
During scope reviews, exclusions and their rationales must be clearly documented, and reasonable trade-offs should be made based on the impact
Delivery: From planning to software delivery
Before starting development, consult with engineering, product owners, and project management to agree on feasible scope and plans
After development begins, make quick decisions about the product to ensure team work is not delayed, visualize delivery risks, and maintain proper management
When constraints arise, support project managers and product owners with timely decision-making and scope adjustments based on clear intent (though not directly managing the project plan itself).
Release: Release to customers and users
Confirm that the functions and requirements of the product in charge meet the agreed acceptance conditions and are ready to be offered to customers, and make recommendations on whether to implement or postpone releases.
Collaborate with the Arena Release Manager to drive the Arena release process. Provide the necessary information and materials to ensure smooth and reliable launches for customer and user engagement, solutions, design, documentation.
Continuous Improvement After Release: Validation and Formulation of Improvement Policies After Release
Continuously monitor the success metrics set during the requirements definition phase. Analyze and interpret the results obtained in collaboration with the Arene Data team and field teams.
Collect feedback from customers and users systematically and continuously, either directly or via the service team, and decide whether to continue improving the features and requirements of the product in charge, expand it, or discontinue the offering.

Design and operate documentation, reviews, and regular meetings to understand and align stakeholders in engineering, UX, commercialization, partnerships, quality, safety, and more.

As a Software Engineer on the Firmware team, you will own the software integration, performance, optimization, and debugging of our TCU (Telematics Control Unit). Managing a complex architecture that integrates third-party hardware with our autonomous vehicle platform, you will analyze diagnostics and log outputs across cellular networks, 4G/5G modems, internal software layers, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth. You will not only reactively troubleshoot complex field issues but also proactively architect and develop robust host-side connectivity software to handle cellular edge cases and vulnerabilities before they impact operations.
Your work will directly safeguard the safety, reliability, and scaling of the Zoox autonomous fleet. Robust, low-latency connectivity is fundamental to autonomous vehicle deployment, powering essential real-time cloud services, fleet management pipelines, and teleoperation capabilities. By ensuring our vehicles maintain seamless, high-performance connections under the most demanding real-world conditions, you will bridge the gap between cutting-edge hardware, cloud infrastructure, and test systems to enable Zoox to deliver the future of autonomous mobility.

Responsibilities
Contribute and Develop:
Contribute to Zoox's firmware and cellular wireless connectivity stack (LTE/5G), developing and enhancing connectivity features across multiple generations of hardware.
Vendor Integration:
Act as the primary technical expert working with cellular chipset vendors (e.g., Qualcomm) to integrate their proprietary firmware, SW stacks, and L1-L3 implementations into our custom embedded Linux platform.
Architecture Definition:
Define, architect, and validate the critical software interfaces between the RF-baseband, the vendor's protocol stack (AP), and our host system, writing the host-side glue code (C/C++) needed for the Linux networking stack.
Prototyping:
Prototype and evaluate next-generation wireless platforms for future Zoox products.
Telemetry and Analytics:
Develop the telemetry and analytics platform enabling data collection, analysis, and visualization of data reported from the Zoox fleet.
Investigate and Solve:
Investigate and root-cause issues reported by QA teams and customer feedback. Differentiate between host-side bugs and vendor firmware issues using your deep knowledge of cellular protocols.
Quality and Automation:
Support test automation frameworks, collaborate with QA, manufacturing, and other software teams, and drive continuous improvements and best practices within the broader organization.

In this role, you will:
Optimize large-scale models (Multi-Modal Sensor Fusion models, LLMs, VLMs) using advanced quantization (PTQ, QAT), pruning, mixed-precision inference frameworks, and parameter-efficient fine-tuning (LoRA, QLoRA).
Architect and implement model conversion and compilation pipelines using TensorRT for edge deployment.
Perform rigorous parity checking, accuracy recovery, and latency benchmarking between PyTorch frameworks and compiled edge binaries.
Develop and optimize custom ML OPs and TensorRT Plugins with efficient CUDA kernels to minimize latency and maximize memory bandwidth on AI accelerators.
Write production-level, low latency, and memory-safe C++ and CUDA code for real-time inference on vehicle systems.

Qualifications:
Deep expertise in model quantization (PTQ, QAT) and mixed-precision inference frameworks (INT8, FP8, FP4, BF16/FP16).
Proven experience optimizing large-scale models (Multi-Modal Sensor Fusion models, LLMs, VLMs/VLAs) utilizing Efficient Attention mechanisms (e.g., FlashAttention, Linear Attention), KV-cache optimization (e.g., PagedAttention) and Speculative Decoding.
Extensive experience with model conversion/compilation pipelines (e.g., ONNX, TensorRT, torch.compile) and performing rigorous latency benchmark and model quality parity valuation.
Proficiency in low-level programming for AI accelerators, specifically developing and optimizing custom ML OPs and TensorRT Plugins with efficient CUDA kernel implementations.
Production-level C++ (14/17/20) and Python programming skills, with experience developing concurrent, memory-safe, real-time inference code for edge devices.

Bonus Qualifications:
Familiarity with SOTA autonomous driving perception algorithms (temporal 3D object detection, BEV, 3D Occupancy Networks) and multi-modal sensor processing (Vision, LiDAR, Radar).
Experience with distributed training pipelines and model/tensor parallelism (PyTorch Distributed, Ray, DeepSpeed, Megatron-LM) and runtime efficiency optimization for GPU clusters.
Experience with end-to-end autonomous driving paradigms (VLM/VLA models, Foundation models) and edge deployment technologies (e.g., TensorRT-LLM).

data.job_description:
As a Senior Staff Technical Program Manager for Body, Closures & Chassis, you will serve as the Program Lead for our Body, Closures & Chassis Systems. You will provide the overarching technical direction and leadership required to guide the vehicle program from concept through production across Body, Closures, and Chassis domains.
 
In this position, you will bridge the gap between high-level program milestones and deep technical execution. You are responsible for balancing performance attributes, cost, quality, and manufacturability while coordinating engineering execution across our internal team and external partners.

In this role, you will:
Serve as the program and technical lead for the vehicle program across Body (BIW, structures), Closures (doors, mechanisms, glazing), and Chassis (suspension, subframes, tires, wheels, by-wire systems), collaborating with internal engineers and external supplier design teams to ensure cohesive engineering execution.
Oversee BOM integrity, approve critical build processes, and drive quality and cost engineering initiatives throughout the supply chain for your major assemblies.
Develop program schedules and partner with suppliers, quality, procurement, service, manufacturing, and engineering teams to drive complex open issues to closure and ensure on-time delivery.
Identify and communicate program progress, engineering challenges, and technical risks while proactively developing and leading strategic mitigation plans across the organization.
Lead the root-cause analysis and tracking of critical build and design issues impacting vehicle performance, quality, and production readiness to drive long-term engineering solutions.
Influence system designs to optimize performance, cost, quality, manufacturability, and serviceability by leading top-level design reviews, DFMEAs, validation programs, and manufacturing mock-builds.

Qualifications
B.S. or M.S. in Mechanical Engineering, Automotive Engineer, or a related technical discipline
12+ years of deep automotive engineering experience, with focus on Body, Closures or Chassis design and project management.
Proficiency with advanced automotive engineering tools and methodologies, including CATIA V5/V6, PLM/BOM management, FMEA/FTA, and structured root-cause analysis (8D, Fishbone), and project management tools (e.g., JIRA, Confluence, Polarion, Gantt charts, ERP, PLM, ALM).
Experience designing for attributes such as crash, NVH, reliability, strength, and corrosion.
A proven track record of managing complex cross-functional projects and delivering components via external design suppliers and contract manufacturers.
End-to-end New Product Introduction (NPI) experience.
Strong collaboration and communication skills across all levels, from peers and suppliers to manufacturing and executive management.
Ability to travel globally as required.

Bonus Qualifications
Familiarity with hardware/firmware product development and vehicle CAN/Firmware.

Base Salary Range
 
There are three major components to compensation for this position: salary, Amazon Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), and Zoox Stock Appreciation Rights. A sign-on bonus may be offered as part of the compensation package. The listed range applies only to the base salary. Compensation will vary based on geographic location and level. Leveling, as well as positioning within a level, is determined by a range of factors, including, but not limited to, a candidate's relevant years of experience, domain knowledge, and interview performance. The salary range listed in this posting is representative of the range of levels Zoox is considering for this position.
 
Zoox also offers a comprehensive package of benefits, including paid time off (e.g. sick leave, vacation, bereavement), unpaid time off, Zoox Stock Appreciation Rights, Amazon RSUs, health insurance, long-term care insurance, long-term and short-term disability insurance, and life insurance.

data.advertised_job_title: Senior Technical Program Manager - Vehicle System Integration
data.job_description:
As the Technical Program Manager for the Systems Engineering team, you will act as the operational engine and technical coordinator behind the vehicle’s functional architecture. This is not a passive task-tracking role; you will own the cross-functional alignment and execution required to take high-level product definitions and drive their translation into technically sound, safe, and traceable system-level implementations.
You will partner closely with Systems Architects, Safety Specialists, Validation, and other cross-functional teams to drive the authoring of System Technical Specifications (STS), manage System Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (SFMEA) lifecycles, and align diverse stakeholders from industrial design to test track validation. In this role, you will:
Manage the release train, maturity lifecycle, and governance for all System Technical Specifications (STS) across all program gates from PI to OKTB. You don’t write the specs, but you ensure the Systems Engineers have the cross-functional inputs they need from all stakeholders in order to meet strict vehicle milestone deadlines.
Act as the operational owner of the System Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (SFMEA) lifecycle. Schedule and facilitate multi-disciplinary workshops, track open action items to strict closure dates, and ensure safety mitigations are integrated into downstream hardware/software schedules.
Build and maintain the master dependency matrix linking Studio (styling/packaging), Product, SDMA (Safety), VSE, VI and Validation. Proactively identify and resolve timeline disconnects before they stall engineering progress.
Lead the program management of Engineering Change Requests (ECRs) at the system level. Ensure that when a requirement changes, all affected downstream stakeholders (from firmware to validation teams) are brought to the table to evaluate timeline and resource impacts.
Define and track the health metrics of the Systems Engineering team’s deliverables (e.g., requirement stability, SFMEA action item burn-down, verification progress). Provide clear, high-density status visibility to executive leadership.

Qualifications
8+ years of experience as a Technical Program Manager or Systems Engineer in an aerospace, autonomous vehicle, or advanced automotive setting, with a proven track record of driving complex, cross-functional projects from requirements through validation.
Deep, practical familiarity with the systems engineering "V-model" lifecycle, fail-operational architectures, and requirements management frameworks.
Proven experience tracking and driving complex safety workflows, specifically SFMEAs, DFMEAs, FTAs (Fault Tree Analyses), and ISO 26262 / MIL-STD-882 compliance.
Strong background in vehicle E/E system design, electrical integration, or managing complex hardware/software interfaces.
Expertise using standard project, change, and configuration management stacks (e.g., JIRA, Smartsheet) alongside requirements management tools and processes (such as Jama, Polarion, or DOORS).
Demonstrated ability to command a room of highly specialized domain experts (hardware, software, safety, manufacturing), facilitate both technical and non-technical discussions, and drive consensus without direct authority.
Self-motivated and proactive with a strong ability to identify risks before they become blockers; thrives in rapid design cycles, remaining flexible and highly organized in the face of uncertainty.
B.S. or M.S. in Mechatronics Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a related technical field.

Bonus Qualifications
Prior experience developing Automotive Systems in Body or Motion Domains (e.g., Brakes, Steering, Suspension or Body Controllers).

data.advertised_job_title: Senior/Staff Design Reliability Engineer – Sensor, Compute and EE Systems
data.job_description:
At Zoox, we have set the goal to provide our customers with the highest level of safety and a best-in-class experience while using our fully autonomous vehicles. You will work with a team of world-class engineers with diverse backgrounds, such as robotics, control, and vehicle engineering, to deliver vehicle performance using virtual tools and methodologies. In taking on the virtual and physical durability development, you will work in predicting where the vehicle is within its lifespan and providing maintenance scenarios and optimization strategies.

In this role, you will:
Set reliability and availability targets. Define top-level hardware availability targets from market requirements and build consensus across product, feature, operations, vehicle engineering, software, and autonomy. Cascade those targets into subsystem and component-level failure budgets for sensors (LiDAR, radar, camera), AI compute, and ECUs, working directly with component owners and the Advanced Hardware and Vehicle Systems Engineering EE teams.
Drive the FMEA process. Drive cross-functional System DFMEA and Supportability FMEA to identify failure mechanisms, system-interaction failure modes, and preventative maintenance opportunities. Define risk classification, FMEA methodology, and mitigation plans.
Drive design mitigations. Partner with hardware and firmware architects on redundancy, thermal management, derating guidelines, and software-level degraded/safe modes, identifying where fault tolerance and fail-operational behavior are needed to support the autonomy safety case.
Prove out designs through test. Using reliability targets, DFMEA outputs, and physics-of-failure principles, partner with validation engineers on virtual and physical test plans combining multi-variable stressors (thermal, vibration, electrical loading, firmware states). Oversee early ALT to establish design margins, latent defects, and acceleration parameters for architectural trade studies. Track and report results in V&V reports.
Define PHM strategy for sensors, compute, and EE systems: available signals, health indicators, degradation models, and failure precursors enabling early fault detection and remaining-useful-life estimation.
Operationalize PHM with software, data, and systems teams across vehicle and backend pipelines, translating reliability risks into monitoring, alerting, and maintenance recommendations.
Close the loop with field data. Use current-fleet telemetry and PHM insights to find improvement opportunities and drive corrective action across design, validation, and operations, feeding lessons learned back into next-gen design.

Qualifications
Masters-level engineering or similar technical degree with 10+ years hands on experience in Reliability Engineering
Detailed understanding of relevant sensors, high-performance computers, and ECUs, and typical failure modes and test methods for these components
Deep understanding of reliability data analysis and risk assessment, and how to develop component reliability targets based on functional safety and business objectives
Experience in failure mode assessment, accelerated reliability testing, and advanced field reliability monitoring concepts
Personable with the ability to lead and coach a high-caliber engineering team toward world-class levels of reliability/dependability

An understanding of ISO 26262 Functional Safety

data.job_description:
We are seeking a highly skilled and visionary Staff Signal and Power Integrity (SI/PI) Engineer to join our advanced hardware engineering team. In this role, you will be the definitive technical expert responsible for ensuring the signal quality, timing, and power delivery robustness of our most complex, next-generation robotaxi electronic systems. As a technical pillar within the organization, you will define overarching SI/PI architectures, establish company-wide simulation methodologies, guide electrical design and layout teams, and own the end-to-end sign-off for cutting-edge high-speed interfaces.

In This Role, You Will
Lead the SI/PI architecture and define constraints for next-generation, high-complexity, high-density printed circuit boards (PCBs) and overall system design.
Collaborate at an architectural level with hardware design, silicon vendors, PCB layout, and mechanical engineering teams to define layer stack-ups, routing strategies, component placement, and power delivery architectures.
Analyze, optimize, and sign off on advanced high-speed serial links (PCIe, Ethernet, MIPI, GMSL) and memory interfaces (LPDDR).
Provide expert-level design guidance and validation for automotive-specific communication and audio protocols (A2B).
Architect and conduct comprehensive Power Delivery Network (PDN) analysis, including DC IR drop, AC impedance modeling, and transient response analysis to ensure stable power delivery across complex multi-board systems.
Drive the development of advanced SI/PI routing rules, simulation methodologies, automation scripts, and sign-off processes for the hardware engineering department.
Tackle the most complex, unprecedented signal and power integrity challenges, performing hands-on root-cause analysis, lab measurements, and correlating simulation models with real-world testing.
Act as a technical mentor and subject matter expert, elevating the SI/PI capabilities of the entire hardware organization and guiding junior to senior engineers.

Qualifications
Bachelor’s, Master’s, or Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Physics, or a closely related technical field.
10+ years of proven industry experience in signal and power integrity analysis for complex high-speed digital designs.
Extensive, proven track record designing, simulating, and troubleshooting high-speed interfaces, specifically
PCIe, multi-gigabit Ethernet, MIPI (CSI/DSI), and GMSL
, through multiple successful product lifecycles.
Deep expertise in memory interface design and simulation, with a strong focus on advanced
LPDDR
technologies.
Familiarity with automotive audio and sensor bus protocols, such as
A2B
.
Advanced proficiency with industry-standard 2D/3D electromagnetic extraction and SI/PI simulation tools (e.g., Ansys HFSS/SIwave, Keysight ADS, Cadence Sigrity, or Siemens EDA/HyperLynx).
Mastery of electromagnetics, transmission line theory, cross-talk, jitter, and advanced PDN design principles.
Expert-level hands-on experience with high-speed lab characterization equipment, including Vector Network Analyzers (VNAs), Time-Domain Reflectometers (TDRs), and high-bandwidth oscilloscopes.

Bonus Qualifications
Direct experience in the automotive industry, particularly developing hardware for advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS) or autonomous vehicles.
Deep understanding of automotive reliability standards, compliance requirements, and designing for harsh environmental operating conditions.
Extensive experience with high-layer-count HDI (High-Density Interconnect) PCB design, advanced packaging, and pushing the boundaries of modern fabrication capabilities.
Proven ability to influence technical strategy, drive cross-functional alignment, and clearly communicate complex technical trade-offs to executive and non-SI/PI stakeholders.

As the Team Lead for Ground Operations (3rd Shift), you will drive operational excellence by leading overnight fleet maintenance, rework, and mission readiness activities. Service efficiency and comprehensive fleet preparedness are key drivers of our success, making this role critical to ensuring that vehicle maintenance, reworks, and fleet readiness activities are optimized overnight during low-demand periods. You will be responsible for the holistic readiness of our vehicle fleet, ensuring maximum fleet uptime and vehicle availability for daytime operations.
In this technical leadership role, you will ensure vehicles are configured, maintained, and prepared for service, while shaping a positive workshop and depot culture. You will lead a team of skilled vehicle technicians and readiness and response associates on the overnight shift. By optimizing workflows and taking ownership of mission-critical readiness targets, you will act as a strategic partner to cross-functional teams, translating high-level operational goals into actionable plans for your 3rd-shift crew.
Shift: Sunday - Thursday, 11:30pm - 8am

In this role, you will:
Strategic Leadership & Team Culture
Overnight Shift Leadership: Provide direct leadership, coaching, and mentorship to both technical staff and contract personnel during the 3rd shift.
Team Development: Engage in the recruiting, hiring, onboarding, and training of workshop personnel. Foster a high-performance culture centered on accountability, safety, and continuous improvement.
Resource Management: Assist in creating and managing employee and contractor schedules, including time-off.
Performance Tracking: Support the tracking of Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) to measure individual and team performance, providing consistent feedback to help your team achieve its mission.
Continuous Process Improvement: Identify bottlenecks in overnight workflows and implement lean methodologies to streamline maintenance, repair, and fleet readiness processes, driving ongoing operational efficiency.
Technical Execution & Maintenance
Overnight Maintenance Optimization: Lead vehicle maintenance and rework activities during low-demand periods to maximize daytime vehicle availability and service efficiency.
Technical Escalation: Serve as the primary escalation point for complex technical issues, ensuring all work meets rigorous internal quality standards.
Data-Driven Operations: Support the analysis, documentation, and reporting of fleet data to aid in root cause analysis on component and vehicle-level issues, preventing future downtime.
Safety Stewardship: Enforce all health and safety policies in the workshop. Ensure the facility remains clean, organized, and free of hazardous materials in accordance with company and OSHA guidelines.
Mission Readiness & Logistics
Software Deployment: Ensure the correct software and firmware are deployed to the right vehicles at the right time to support morning operations.
Pre-Mission Checks & Ingest: Direct the ingest of vehicles, conduct rigorous pre-mission checks, and ensure the completion of readiness checklists for the first shift.
Logistical Support: Oversee the logistical movement and storage of vehicles to ensure seamless shift transitions.
Vehicle Operations: Manually drive and maneuver autonomous and auxiliary vehicles when needed to support readiness workflows and yard logistics.
Multi-Site Support: Support team and vehicle fleet operations across multiple sites within the geo, coordinating across different Mission Readiness and Base Operations locations as operations scale.

Qualifications
5+ years of hands-on automotive technician experience combined with 2+ years of people leadership or supervisory experience.
Willingness and ability to lead overnight operations (3rd shift).
Extensive knowledge of automotive maintenance methods, diagnostic methods, parts, and tools, including high proficiency in CAN/LIN architecture, wiring diagrams, and soldering.
Proven ability to quickly learn technical subjects.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills; must be honest, responsible, and capable of translating technical details for cross-functional stakeholders.
Demonstrated ability to manage time, multitask, and drive priorities effectively in a fast-paced, ambiguous startup environment.
Clean driving record and the ability to travel locally and nationally (less than 20%).

Bonus Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in a technical or business field, or a Technical trade school certificate / Associate Degree in automotive repair.
Strong understanding of electric vehicle architecture and high-voltage systems.
Experience in a fast-paced service environment.
Familiarity with Lean, Six Sigma, or other continuous improvement methodologies.

data.advertised_job_title: Technical Program Manager, PMO - Test Fleet Program (Contract)
data.job_description:
The Program Management Office (PMO) at Zoox is at the center of the company's efforts, responsible for driving cross-functional program planning and execution at the highest level. We partner with leaders from every corner of the company—vehicle development, software engineering, manufacturing, and operations—to deliver on the ambitious milestones that pave our path to launching a revolutionary autonomous mobility service.
The L3 Program within PMO is responsible for the optimal allocation and usage of the test fleet, operated nationwide, with leading-edge hardware and software that will be used in future milestones. Our program managers contribute to the end to end success of all of Zoox's technical, integrated product milestones on our purpose-built robotaxi.
We are excited to launch a new initiative to bring exceptional early-career talent into our PMO team. This is a role for those who have a history of high performance in their academic and project work and are eager to apply their skills to complex, real-world challenges. While we hire for potential and rate of learning, we are looking for individuals who have demonstrated the ability to perform at a high level, regardless of their years of experience. 
As a Technical Program Manager (6-month contract), you will be given concrete, well-defined projects that will allow you to make a real impact from the start. This role is a unique opportunity to grow into a leader who can run, improve, and expand our program structures. Please note that this is an on-site role and requires working from the office five days per week.

In this Role, You Will...
Drive Clarity and Unity: Work independently to gather and analyze information from various teams to create unified program management templates, helping to standardize how we track deliverables across different parts of the company.
Structure for Success: Collaborate with stakeholders across engineering and product to define, structure, and track key program deliverables, ensuring that our most critical initiatives are aligned and on track.
Improve Our Processes: Identify opportunities for process automation and tooling improvements. You’ll have the chance to build better dashboards and tools that enhance program reporting and efficiency.
Dive Deep into the Details: Engage with the technical details of our programs, participating in the review process for project-level deliverables to ensure they meet our strategic intent.
Communicate and Collaborate: Develop strong relationships with a wide range of teams, learning how to communicate effectively and drive progress in a highly cross-functional environment.

Requirements
Deep Passion for a Technical Subject: We love to see candidates who go deep into a topic they are passionate about, whether it's a school project, a personal hobby, or a side hustle. We want to hear you get into the details of what you've learned.
A Builder's Mindset: We are impressed by candidates who have tangible experience shipping projects that work. This could be through student engineering competitions such as FSAE or developing a product out of a hackathon.
A Knack for Collaboration: We value people who make teams work better together. We're interested in your experience adjusting how your team collaborated during a challenge, establishing a new communication routine for a club project, or any other instance where you thoughtfully improved teamwork.

Qualifications
Bachelor's or Master's degree in a technical or quantitative field (e.g., Computer Science, Engineering, Math, Physics, or a related discipline).
A demonstrated passion for learning and a high potential for growth.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
An ability to work independently, manage projects, and show initiative.
A deep curiosity and interest in autonomous vehicles, robotics, or complex software and hardware systems.

Job Description
Semiconductors are much more than the key technology of tomorrow. They are already our core business today. Join us on this journey. Become part of an inspiring team at Bosch that is dedicated to developing leading ASICs and SoCs – for sustainable, safe, and fascinating solutions for the mobility of tomorrow. 
As a mixed-signal ASIC design engineer for analog frontends and ADCs, you will develop high-performance analog interface circuits (incl. ADC and DAC) for mixed-signal SoC ASICs in automotive sensor modules. Examples are low-noise frontends for ultrasonic sensors, frontends for inertial sensors with very low offset drift or high-speed frontends for radar applications. In addition, you will support the layout creation and the development of series test programs. 
In close cooperation with our customers, you will define precise requirements for new circuit solutions and translate them into detailed technical specifications. In addition, you will develop and evaluate innovative concepts for signal analysis and processing – always with the aim of implementing state-of-the-art solutions. 
Your core tasks will include designing and verifying high-power amplifiers, analog filters, ADCs, DACs and dedicated supporting circuits. In addition, you will create reference models of the entire signal path using Matlab/Simulink and/or Verilog-A to comprehensively simulate and validate functionality. 
Last but not least, you will take responsibility for the validation of samples as well as the evaluation of characterization and qualification results to ensure the quality of our products. 

Qualifications
Education: 
Completed university degree in electrical engineering, computer science or a comparable course of study
Experience and knowledge: 
Hands-on experience in IC design, especially in the design of low-noise amplifier and converter circuits; In-depth knowledge of semiconductor processes and solid-state devices; Experience with modern EDA software tools for schematic input, simulation, layout, and design flows; Hands-on experience with MATLAB/Simulink

You are able to drive complex technical topics across departmental boundaries; You work in a structured, responsible and goal-oriented manner; You communicate clearly and coordinate effectively in the team

Very good knowledge of German and English, both written and spoken

Up to and including 16 September 2026
