data.advertised_job_title: Master's Thesis: Automated Sensor Calibration and Error Classification for Intelligent Sensor Networks (f/m/div.)
data.job_description:
Job Description
This project focuses on optimizing the reliability of industrial machines through advanced sensor monitoring and automated calibration. As part of your thesis, you will investigate two main types of sensor failures: physical hardware anomalies and software-related drifts. By combining real-world measurements on the test bench with data analysis, you will develop a system that distinguishes between these types of failures and, where possible, automatically applies software-based corrections. Your final concept will contribute to the development of self-calibrating sensor systems. 
As part of your thesis, you will perform physical measurements on a ball screw (BSD) test bench to record and analyze both error-free ("good") sensor data and hardware-related sensor failures ("bad"). You will analyze a provided, pre-detected dataset with software-related sensor deviations (e.g. sensor drift). You will develop criteria that distinguish a software-correctable drift from a physical hardware failure, so that the sensor is suitable for purely software-based recalibration. In addition, you will research and evaluate various software-based recalibration techniques. 
You will design a robust concept for an automated workflow that triggers the appropriate software-based recalibration based on your classification and then checks whether the sensor is working correctly again. You will also validate your concept with both your newly recorded hardware datasets and the drift datasets provided. Finally, you will identify cases where software-based recalibration is not sufficient (with a special focus on the recorded hardware failures) and propose a strategy for how the system should deal with these physical anomalies (e.g. flagging for maintenance or triggering a hardware replacement). 

Qualifications
Education: 
Master's degree in computer science, data science, electrical engineering, mechatronics, engineering, physics or equivalent, with very good academic performance
Experience and knowledge: 
Very good programming skills in Python as well as confident handling of data science libraries (e.g. Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn); Sound theoretical knowledge and initial practical experience in data analysis and machine learning concepts, especially in the field of classification; Basic understanding of physical measurement principles, sensor technology or industrial automation; Knowledge of collaborative software development as well as platforms such as Git/GitHub
Personality and way of working: 
You are highly motivated, open to collaboration and teamwork, and combine an independent, systematic way of working with strong analytical thinking
Working model:

data.advertised_job_title: Master's Thesis: Description of Hydraulic Systems for Use by AI Agents
data.job_description:
Job Description
The evaluation of the energy efficiency of hydraulic drives in mobile machines is becoming increasingly important as early as the project planning phase. To evaluate different system topologies, the specified output power at individual actuators is calculated back to the required drive power via a system regulation. The implementation of the system regulations is currently done manually in MATLAB, which entails considerable effort for each new system topology. AI agents offer the potential to automate this step – provided that the hydraulic system is available in a machine-readable, unambiguous and physically complete description. So far, there is no established format that combines system topology and parameterization in such a way that an AI agent can generate reliably executable and validatable MATLAB code from it. The aim of this thesis is to develop such a formal description language for work hydraulic systems, to apply it prototypically and to prove its suitability as an interface between engineer and AI agent. 
During your master's thesis, you will analyze the current state of the art and research existing forms of description of hydraulic systems, such as ISO 1219 circuit diagrams or bond graphs, and identify the specific requirements of AI agents for structured inputs. 
You will then design a formal, machine-readable description language that clearly maps the topology and parameters of typical work hydraulic systems in mobile machines. 
As a prototype, you implement an AI agent that reads this formal description and generates a system regulation as MATLAB code. 
You will validate and evaluate your method, compare the automatically generated code with a manual reference implementation and derive concrete recommendations for further development and industrial use. 

Qualifications
Education: 
Master's degree in mechanical engineering, mechatronics or comparable
Experience and know-how: 
Basic knowledge of hydraulics and system modeling; experience in MATLAB is an advantage
Personality and way of working: 
You work independently and in a structured manner on complex issues

data.advertised_job_title: Internship in process development and monitoring in laser beam welding
data.job_description:
Job Description
Electromobility – especially in the field of battery technology – requires highly stable and quality-assured manufacturing processes. Our team develops innovative laser system technology and laser-based welding processes for industrial large-scale production in special machine construction. As part of a research project, we are developing novel laser beam welding processes for battery systems in electromobility in our laboratory. With the help of integrated process monitoring and evaluation methods, we systematically investigate these processes to ensure process stability, seam quality and industrial applicability. 
During your internship, you will familiarize yourself with laser system technology and laser material processing with the support of the interdisciplinary team. The planning, implementation and evaluation of experiments on laser beam welding in the laboratory will be part of your area of responsibility. 
You will analyze laser welding processes for copper and aluminum compounds using different laser and optical combinations. 
In addition, you will be involved in the development, integration and application of processes for process monitoring during laser beam welding, e.g. optical and sensor-based measurement methods. 
Your job will include the acquisition, evaluation and statistical analysis of process and sensor data to evaluate process stability, seam quality and error mechanisms. 
Furthermore, you will examine the weld samples metallographically, statistically evaluate the results and derive recommendations for robust welding processes in industrial series production. 
Last but not least, you will prepare the results in the form of reports and presentations for international project teams and support the construction, commissioning and optimization of highly innovative production plants and system modules. 

Qualifications
Education: 
Degree in mechanical engineering, mechatronics, electrical engineering, physics or comparable with good academic performance
Experience and know-how: 
Ideally, initial experience in the fields of laser technology, optics and/or special machine construction
Personality and way of working: 
you find it easy to grasp complex issues quickly; you always act in a solution-oriented manner and are communicative in the team

data.advertised_job_title: Mandatory internship in purchasing – focus on international procurement of mechanical parts
data.job_description:
Job Description
As part of your internship, you will analyze our current purchasing portfolio with a focus on mechanical components and derive potential for a strategic expansion of the supplier network in China. 
In supplier management, you will identify potential suppliers in China, evaluate them on the basis of technical skills, capacities, certifications and key economic indicators, and participate in their initiation and communication – if necessary in cooperation with local sourcing partners or service providers. 
Together with our Europe-wide purchasing team, you will develop a cross-site purchasing strategy for the Chinese market and accompany its implementation. 
You will systematically compare the total cost of ownership (TCO) between Asian and European purchasing options, taking into account logistics, quality, delivery time, customs and risks. 
With the help of well-founded market and competitor analyses, also using digital tools or AI-supported research approaches, you will gain insights into relevant developments. 
In operational support, you will take on tasks related to enquiries, offer comparisons and supplier evaluations and at the same time work on the further development of standardised purchasing processes to increase efficiency in an international context. 
The creation of presentations and decision templates for management is also part of your area of responsibility, including close coordination with the team leader. 
In the area of digitalization and data analysis, you will get involved in data-driven topics if you are interested, for example in setting up a supplier dashboard (e.g. in Power BI) and in automating analyses and reports (e.g. with Python, Excel VBA or Power Automate). 

Qualifications

Experience and know-how: 
confident handling of MS Office; SAP knowledge; practice in Power BI as well as affinity for AI tools

As a driving force at the interface between IT and production, you evaluate and design the digitalization of our manufacturing processes. As part of your master's thesis, you will take responsibility for the design, implementation and evaluation of an innovative software prototype. This acts as a bridge between physical production and the digital twin. 
You will carry out detailed analyses directly in the production environment. In doing so, you will identify automation potential and translate it into technical requirements. 
In addition, you will design and implement a prototype application to automate the identified interfaces. The technological focus is on a Python-based backend and a modern web frontend (e.g. with Angular). 
Furthermore, you will place a special emphasis on the design of an intuitive, user-optimized interface. In close cooperation with users from production, you will ensure a high level of acceptance and practicality. 
A central scientific aspect of your thesis is the evaluation of the method of "live prototyping" in production-related software projects. You will analyze the advantages and disadvantages as well as the success factors of this agile approach in the industrial environment. 

Qualifications
Education: 
Master's degree in computer science, business informatics, mechanical engineering or comparable with a strong IT focus
Experience and know-how: 
Basic understanding of databases (e.g. PostgreSQL, MySQL)
Sound knowledge of software development, ideally with initial practical experience
Know-how in backend development with Python as well as in frontend development (e.g. with Angular, React or Vue.js) is an advantage
Personality and way of working: 
you are communicative, act independently and in a structured manner; you have the ability to penetrate complex contexts
Enthusiasm: 
enjoy mediating between the worlds of IT and production; ideally a strong interest in Industry 4.0, the digital twin and the analysis of manufacturing processes
Languages: 
Fluent in German and English

Additional information

by arrangement

6 months

data.job_description:
Job Description
As part of your master's thesis, you will model electric drive systems and integrate innovative AI methods. 
You will develop new control and learning methods for electric drives by combining machine learning with model-based approaches. 
You will focus on the design of highly dynamic controls that also take into account the estimation of unknown system behavior. 
You will then implement and validate the new procedures precisely in MATLAB and Simulink. 
Finally, you will apply the developed control system simulatively to a robotics application. 

Qualifications

Master's degree in electrical engineering, technical cybernetics, engineering sciences or comparable

Job Description
Are you passionate about cutting-edge biomedical technology and eager to make a tangible impact on healthcare? This Master thesis offers an exceptional opportunity to dive deep into the fascinating world of microfluidics and contribute directly to the development of a novel microfluidic chip for Digital Polymerase Chain Reaction (dPCR). Join our interdisciplinary team and help shape the future of medical diagnostics.
As part of your Master thesis, you will actively participate in the development and optimization of a microfluidic chip designed specifically for digital PCR requirements.
You will immerse yourself in a broad spectrum of state-of-the-art techniques and gain hands-on experience with microfluidic, biochemical and genetic methodologies, building a comprehensive skill set.
Furthermore, you will conduct thorough literature reviews and experimentally validate scientific hypotheses, including the use of patient samples.
Last but not least, as a member of our highly innovative team, you will regularly document your work, evaluate experimental results, engage in stimulating discussions and present your findings in order to contribute to the collective knowledge of the project and its progression.

Qualifications

You have already proven your enthusiasm for contact with customers and technical solutions in challenging industrial internships. Ideally, you will also have gained initial experience in the hydraulics environment.

data.advertised_job_title: Master Thesis Optimized Design of Robotic Assembly Systems
data.job_description:
Job Description
As a part of your Master thesis, you will review existing industrial solutions and the current state of research in robotic assembly systems, with a focus on multi-robot cells and the integration of special-purpose machines.
You will develop a modelling approach for special-purpose machines. These machines will be represented as kinematic structures composed of simple geometric bodies connected by joints, enabling their integration into the existing simulation framework at an abstract level.
Your area of ​​responsibility includes the further development of the optimization framework to address higher-level system design questions. The objective is to determine an appropriate system decomposition, including the number of cells and robots allocated to each cell, as well as the integration of special-purpose machines.
Last but not least, you will create a model of a real-world use case and evaluate alternative system design configurations based on the extended framework.

Qualifications
Education:
Master studies in the field of Engineering, Computer Science, Natural Sciences or comparable
Experience and Knowledge:
advanced programming skills (e.g., Python)
Personality and Working Practice:
you work independently and in a structured way

Based in Roseville, California, the Product Manager for power semiconductor components is responsible for the strategic product planning and long-term development of Robert Bosch’s Silicon Carbide product portfolio in North America. The role is part of Bosch’s international network of Product Responsible Managers (PRMs) and works in close alignment with headquarters in Germany to connect regional market requirements, technology roadmaps, and business priorities into a competitive, profitable, and future-oriented product offering across the full product lifecycle. A key focus of the role is to identify, develop, and drive new market opportunities for Bosch North America, especially in growth areas outside the automotive industry.
Responsibilities:
Collect customer and market requirements in North America and translate them into product needs, cost indications, priorities, and timelines together with global product management and development teams.
Monitor market trends, competitor activity, new technologies, and key industry players in North America, including coordination of benchmark activities.
Lead pre-selling and market study activities for new applications in high-growth markets outside the automotive industry, such as data centers, EV charging, energy storage, solar, and related industrial segments.
Support and align the product portfolio and roadmap for power semiconductor components (focus on Silicon Carbide) with Bosch headquarters in Germany.
Support customer visits with the regional sales organization to discuss new products, application requirements, and product positioning.
Drive communication and promotion planning for products, including event content, articles, trade fairs, conferences, and customer road shows.
Prepare materials for senior management meetings and support standards-related topics and market intelligence sharing within the North America organization.
Lead strategic partnership and cooperation activities in North America, including collaboration models with external partners in areas such as packaging, foundry, and technology development.

Qualifications
Degree in electrical engineering, physics, or a comparable field; advanced technical understanding of power semiconductor components, ideally including SiC technologies, is preferred.
Experience in product management, strategic marketing, business development, or a comparable function in the semiconductor or electronics industry.
Business acumen and strategic thinking related to partnerships, cooperation models, and growth opportunities in North America, including expansion into new markets outside the automotive industry.
Strong understanding of product lifecycle management, portfolio strategy, market analysis, and competitor benchmarking.
Ability to translate regional customer needs and market trends into product roadmaps, business cases, and aligned development priorities with international stakeholders.
Experience working in global matrix organizations and collaborating effectively across regions, functions, and headquarters interfaces.
Strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, including customer-facing engagement and executive communication.

Job Description
This position is responsible for technical project management of commercial vehicle steering systems, including electrohydraulic and fully electric steering systems. The role requires the ability to work independently, manage technical priorities, and collaborate across mechatronic product-development activities. The individual will work with a multidisciplinary development team—including systems, mechanical design, software, hardware, application and calibration, functional safety, cybersecurity, and project management professionals—to develop project-specific solutions for conventional, driver-assistance, automated-driving, and autonomous-vehicle applications.
The
System Project Lead (SysPL)
serves as the technical lead and technical counterpart to the Program Manager for the customer project. The SysPL is responsible for project-level technical integration and execution, coordinating across engineering disciplines to ensure that steering-system requirements are understood, aligned, validated, and completed within established project timelines.
Evaluate and align customer requirements across relevant engineering domains, including System, Software, Hardware, Functional Safety, Cybersecurity, and other technical disciplines, engaging domain experts as needed.
Coordinate technical activities across engineering domains to ensure an integrated steering system solution that meets customer and project requirements.
Support translation of customer requirements into system requirements and ensure appropriate requirements management and traceability using applicable requirements management tools.
Conduct system-level impact analysis for requirements and design changes and ensure appropriate validation is defined and completed.
Establish and maintain customer relationships as the technical project lead and primary engineering interface for assigned customer project(s).
Lead technical discussions with customers regarding steering system requirements, interfaces, performance, diagnostics, application, and system behavior.
Drive resolution of cross-functional technical issues, risks, and open points, ensuring clear ownership and timely closure.
Provide technical troubleshooting and coordinate appropriate engineering resources to resolve customer and system-level issues.
Ensure system development, validation, and delivery are performed according to applicable guidelines and processes (e.g., ISO 26262, ASPICE, IATF 16949, and applicable cybersecurity processes).
Lead the system-level release process, including assessment and documentation of system release for specified use cases with or without defined constraints, ensuring required validation evidence, open-point evaluation, and approvals are completed and documented.
Plan, schedule, and execute demonstration vehicle builds and retrofits, coordinating across mechanical, electrical, instrumentation, software, and calibration teams to integrate steering systems into customer and prototype vehicle platforms.
Monitor, track, and drive completion of technical open points for system-level topics.
Support creation and implementation of the System FMEA and other system-level risk analyses, including review of Safety Failure Tree Analyses (FTAs) and Software Design Failure Analyses (DFAs), as applicable.
Assist in the creation and review of the technical safety concept and support system-level functional safety activities.
Create and release Technical Customer Documentation (TCD) and other required system-level technical documentation.
Plan and report project engineering, development, and testing budgets and costs.
Report project technical status, risks, open points, and budget status to management and relevant project stakeholders on a regular basis.
Support continuous improvement and cost-reduction efforts throughout the project lifecycle.
Lead and coordinate steering system development activities for conventional applications as well as driver assistance, automated driving, and autonomous vehicle applications.
Coordinate and promote collaboration with global development locations, customers, suppliers, and other stakeholders to achieve project goals.
Travel approximately 15–20%, domestic and international, to customer, Bosch, and supplier locations as required.

Job Description
Bosch Motorsport supplies electronics, sensors, actuators, and engineering services to racing series and teams worldwide. Bosch Motorsport North America provides a collaborative work environment in which employees support technical projects and business objectives.
As a member of the engineering team, this position supports application and development engineers on professional motorsport projects in North America. Responsibilities include contributing to the development, integration, and support of motorsport technologies in accordance with defined project requirements.
What You Will Do
The Motorsport Customer Application Engineer serves as a primary technical contact at customer facilities and race tracks, supporting the development, integration, validation, and optimization of motorsport electronic systems and software. The role requires the ability to perform the essential functions in fast-paced work environments and to travel domestically and internationally approximately 50–80 days per year.
Customer Application and Program Coordination
Provide on-site application engineering support for motorsport products, including engine controllers, vehicle control units, displays, power distribution units, and telemetry modules, at customer facilities and race tracks. Gather and document technical requirements, support project schedule development, and coordinate customer-facing track activities with internal development teams.
Customer and Team Technical Support
Serve as a technical point of contact at track locations for supported race teams. Diagnose and resolve system-level issues within the scope of the role and coordinate with customers and internal teams regarding approved parameter changes.
Controls and Hybrid Strategy Development
Develop and document control strategies for internal-combustion-engine and hybrid powertrains, including hybrid energy recovery systems, torque coordination, and related control algorithms.
Vehicle Electrical Architecture
Develop and validate vehicle electrical and communication network topologies, including analog signals, digital signals, CAN, and Ethernet configurations, in accordance with defined technical requirements.
Simulation and Virtual Development
Develop, maintain, and execute virtual simulation environments using Software-in-the-Loop, Hardware-in-the-Loop, and Driver-in-the-Loop methods to validate controls and support trackside system setup.
Software Tools and Standards
Develop and maintain internal software tools and scripts using MATLAB, Python, C#, or comparable technologies. Contribute to documented coding standards and software architecture practices.
Technical Knowledge Sharing
Provide job-related technical guidance, share documented best practices, and support knowledge transfer among engineering team members.
Domestic and International Travel
Travel domestically and internationally approximately 50–80 days per year to provide application engineering support at customer facilities, test tracks, race tracks, and development locations.

Qualifications
Minimum Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or a closely related field.
At least five years of job-related application engineering experience gained through professional, academic, or project-based work.
At least five years of job-related experience using data-acquisition and data-analysis tools to evaluate technical system performance.
Experience applying engineering principles in professional motorsport, Formula SAE, or another environment involving comparable vehicle systems, controls, data acquisition, and trackside or field support.
Preferred Qualifications
Technical Account and Lifecycle Management
Experience in technical account management or another customer-facing technical role, including documenting customer requirements and supporting system application, issue resolution, and validation.
Customer Communication
Ability to communicate job-related technical information clearly to customers, suppliers, and internal engineering teams.
Controls Development
Experience with internal-combustion-engine, hybrid, or battery-electric powertrain controls or chassis-control development, such as traction control, torque vectoring, or energy-recovery-system integration.
System Design and Analysis
Experience designing, applying, or troubleshooting vehicle systems and implementing solutions within established project or operational timelines.
Network and Protocol Architecture
Knowledge of wired or wireless network architectures, including the design, configuration, or troubleshooting of CAN- and Ethernet-based systems.
Testing and Prototyping Systems
Experience using prototyping, simulation, or test equipment, such as dSPACE or ETAS systems, oscilloscopes, or spectrum analyzers.
Software Architecture and Tool Design
Experience designing or implementing software tools using MATLAB, Python, C#, or a comparable language for data processing, simulation, or test automation.
Technical Guidance and Coordination
Experience providing job-related technical guidance, documenting best practices, or coordinating work across multidisciplinary engineering teams.
Ideal Candidate Characteristics
Calm and Decisive Under Pressure
Comfortable making high-stakes, real-time technical decisions with incomplete data under tight trackside timelines, demonstrating strong personal accountability for vehicle performance and reliability.
Systemic and Anticipatory Problem Solving
Deconstructs highly complex, ambiguous vehicle system issues into distinct components, managing uncertainty and actively anticipating how changes in one system impact other vehicle interdependencies.
Champion of Data-Driven Objectivity
Fosters a rigorous, data-driven team culture that values technical objectivity; remains highly adaptable and open to changing direction based on what the trackside data reveals.
Entrepreneurial Ownership
Applies an entrepreneurial mindset to the complete customer journey, proactively identifying bottlenecks, designing more efficient processes, and championing continuous improvement.
Strategic and Diplomatic Communicator
Masters the art of translating intricate technical data and complex failures into clear, concise, and actionable executive summaries for both internal engineering teams and customers.
Cultivator of Collaborative Growth
Actively encourages peer development, pushing the boundaries of the team’s collective capabilities by mentoring entry to mid-level engineers and promoting continuous learning across all areas of responsibility.
If you’re passionate about motorsport and thrive in a dynamic, collaborative environment, we encourage you to apply. Join Bosch Motorsport in shaping the future of racing technology.
Our Motorsport Culture
Passion and Performance
: At Bosch Motorsport North America, we are a close-knit team of dedicated professionals united by our unwavering passion for achieving peak performance, both on and off the track. Our shared commitment drives us to strive for nothing less than the top step of the podium in everything we undertake.
Entrepreneurial Mindset and Innovation
: Embracing an entrepreneurial mindset, we constantly challenge the conventional norms. Fueled by innovation and a thirst for progress, we fearlessly tackle technical and commercial challenges to pave the way for groundbreaking solutions.
Communication
: Building strong relationships internally and with our valued customers is paramount. Through open and transparent dialogue, we foster a culture of trust and collaboration, ensuring that we understand and meet the needs of everyone involved.
Balance
: While we relentlessly pursue victory, we recognize the importance of balance. We believe in working hard but also cherish the value of a healthy work-life balance. This equilibrium empowers our team members to maintain their passion and drive while enjoying personal well-being and growth.
Together, we embrace a culture that pushes boundaries, fosters innovation, and cultivates genuine connections. Our collective determination and relentless pursuit of excellence propel us forward as a winning team, setting new standards in the world of motorsport.

Job Description
Welcome to Bosch Motorsport, a premier supplier of electronics, sensors, actuators, and engineering services to top racing series and teams worldwide. Here at Bosch Motorsport North America, you'll be part of a growing, dynamic, and entrepreneurial team, taking on challenging tasks.
As a vital member of our engineering team, you will play a key role in supporting our application and development engineers in projects focused on professional motorsport within North America. Embrace this opportunity to make an impact in the exciting world of motorsport technology!
What You Will Do
The Associate Motorsport Customer Application Engineer serves as the primary technical contact at customer locations and race tracks to support the development, integration, and optimization of motorsport electronic systems and software. This position requires the ability to work effectively in fast-paced, dynamic environments and involves frequent domestic and international travel (approximately 50–80 days per year).
Customer Application Engineering
Collect customer requirements, manage project timelines, and deliver technical application support for motorsport products including engine controllers, vehicle control units, displays, power boxes, and telemetry modules.
Trackside Support and Diagnostics
Perform real-time diagnostics and troubleshooting at test events and race locations. Analyze live vehicle telemetry and logged data to identify and resolve performance issues.
Telemetry and Tooling Configuration
Set up and maintain trackside telemetry servers, manage wireless radio connections, and develop standardized data analysis dashboards for performance evaluation.
Systems Integration and Verification
Install, integrate, and validate on-vehicle electronic hardware and software. Verify wiring harness integrity, vehicle communication bus data, and resolve component or system-level issues.
Virtual Testing (SiL/HiL)
Set up and execute Software-in-the-Loop (SiL) and Hardware-in-the-Loop (HiL) simulation tests to validate software updates. Coordinate with development teams to align releases with track activities.
Workflow and Software Tool Development
Support the development and optimization of internal software tools and workflow scripts using MATLAB, Python, C#, or similar languages to improve application processes and team efficiency.
Domestic and International Travel
Travel domestically and internationally, approximately 50–80 days per year, to support development activities at customer facilities, test tracks, and global development locations. This is an essential function of the position.

k

Job Description
As the Director for Simulation and Evaluation, you will sit at the center of the Global AI Backbone, architecting the multi-level simulation ecosystems required to train, evaluate and validate next-generation Foundation Models. You will bridge the gap between high-fidelity sensor simulation and generative world models, ensuring our AI systems are statistically proven to be safe and robust before hitting the road.
This is a global role that requires you to define and manage a global simulation and evaluation ecosystem that enables continuous development and deployment of our ADAS systems.
Key Responsibilities:
Lead AI Simulation & Foundation Model Strategy: Define the roadmap for high throughput, closed-loop simulation.
Research and propose new methodologies to assess the quality, safety, and realism of ML models used for training, evaluation and validation of L2++ and L4 automated driving stacks.
Architect Evaluation Frameworks: Build the infrastructure. Develop tools that allow for rapid iteration of Foundation Models, ensuring model improvements translate into measurable gains in fleet-wide performance.
Drive Generative AI Innovation: Lead the development of World Models to predict and generate complex, realisticedge cases. Build data pipelines for signal discovery, data  labeling, and metric computation based on large-scale simulations.
Production Release Authority: Establish the "gold standard" for evaluation that informs SoP (Start of Production) and model release decisions. Translate complex simulation data into technical strategy documentation for executive decision-making.
Global Technical Leadership: Lead, mentor and inspire a cross-functional global team of SWEs, Data Scientists, and ML experts, fostering a culture of rigorous statistical validation and innovative engineering.

Qualifications
Basic Qualifications:
Master’s or PhD in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Machine Learning, Statistics, Physics, or a related quantitative field.
10+ years of experience in software engineering, with a specific focus on embedded systems, automotive, or robotics.
7+ years of experience leading complex software projects from concept to production within the ADAS or Autonomous Driving domain.
Direct, hands-on experience with L2++ or L4 system Start of Production (SoP), specifically overseeing simulation, testing, and validation protocols for high-stakes deployments.
5+ years of involvement with the development or evaluation of large-scale AI, LLMs, or World Models/Generative AI models for simulation and behavioral prediction.
Expert-level understanding of multi-level simulation platforms, including high-fidelity sensorlevel simulation for perception and scalable object-level simulation for behavioral training.
Proven mastery of data-driven report writing and technical strategy documentation designed for executive decision-making and safety case justifications.
Preferred Qualifications:
5+ years of experience with high-throughput simulation, GPU-accelerated technologies (CUDA), parallel computing, and Reinforcement Learning (RL).
Mastery of C++ and Python. Experience building automated data pipelines for signal discovery, data labeling, and large-scale metric computation.
5+ years of experience managing and mentoring global, multi-disciplinary teams of Software Engineers, Data Scientists, and ML experts.
Working knowledge of automotive industry safety standards and regulations (e.g., ISO 26262, SOTIF) as they apply to virtual validation.

Job Description
The die rebuild support associate supports manufacturing operations by performing standardized tooling preparation, component replacement, cleaning, material handling, and staging activities. Work is performed using established work instructions, approved components, and predefined procedures.
This position is focused on routine, repeatable activities and does not perform skilled maintenance, troubleshooting, machining, fabrication, tool design, or technical repair. Tooling conditions outside established work instructions are escalated to the appropriate technical or maintenance personnel.
Primary Responsibilities
Tooling Component Replacement & Preparation — 60–70%
•    Disassemble and reassemble designated Punch & Pack tooling according to established work instructions and standard procedures.
•    Remove designated worn components and install approved replacement components as specified by standard work.
•    Clean tooling and components using established methods.
•    Perform basic visual checks to verify components are present, properly positioned, and assembled according to work instructions.
•    Identify and escalate damaged tooling, abnormal conditions, or issues outside established procedures to appropriate technical personnel.
•    Return completed tooling to designated storage or staging locations.
•    Complete required documentation and tracking records.
Fixture & Tooling Support — 15–25%
•    Clean fixtures and tooling using established procedures.
•    Replace designated consumable or routine wear components according to work instructions.
•    Perform roller covering and tape replacement using standard methods.
•    Prepare and stage fixtures, components, and tooling for production use.
•    Escalate fixture or tooling conditions that require adjustment, repair, troubleshooting, or technical evaluation.
Inventory & Material Handling — 10–15%
•    Maintain organized inventories of approved tooling replacement components and consumable materials.
•    Retrieve, kit, and stage components required for scheduled tooling activities.
•    Organize tooling, fixtures, and components in designated storage locations.
•    Support inventory replenishment using established reorder methods.
•    Identify shortages or inventory discrepancies and communicate them to the appropriate personnel.
Production Support — 10–15%
•    Prepare and stage tooling required for production changeovers.
•    Transport tooling and components to designated production or storage locations.
•    Support production activities according to established standard work.
•    Maintain clean and organized tooling and work areas in accordance with 5S requirements.
•    Cross-train on designated production operator tasks as required.

Qualifications
Must be flexible and able to adapt quickly
General Math skills
Ability to multitask
Ability to stand for 8 hours
Ability to read and follow instructions
Ability to lift (up to) 40lb. boxes
High School Diploma or GED required
Prefer experience in machine operating

Additional Information
All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

Conduct consistent in-person field visits with independent repair shops and targeted accounts to build relationships, identify needs, and support Bosch Mobility Aftermarket growth.
Represent Bosch as the local field contact for workshops, reinforcing brand value, program benefits, and available parts, tools, equipment, diagnostics, and service solutions.

Job Description
Bosch Research is looking for an intern in electrochemical modelling technologies. Our goal is to enable improved Bosch products through deep understanding of thermodynamic, kinetic, and transport phenomena at the mesoscale level using a variety of computational tools. Strong focus is placed on development and application of computational methods for understanding of next-generation materials, primarily for electrochemistry and energy conversion.
In this particular position, the intern will contribute to the modeling of degradation mechanisms in proton-exchange-membrane electrolyzers. The goal is the accurate prediction of the aging kinetics for iridium in the Anode catalyst layer, under various operating conditions.
As part of Bosch Corporate Research, we are dedicated to long-term fundamental investigations of transformative energy technologies. Our modeling team supports global experimental efforts with fundamental understanding, emphasizing innovation and high technological impact. Using both internal funding and government grants, we collaborate closely with a network of leading computational and experimental teams which includes top universities, national labs, and industrial partners. Working closely with Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, the Controller provides financial insights and analysis that support effective asset management, strong internal controls, operational performance, and informed business decisions. Job Description
We are seeking a highly motivated power component architect (PCA) for our silicon carbide product release team in Roseville. As a PCA you will work on innovative product developments based on Silicon Carbide under tight timing with demanding customers for the automotive applications as part of a team of international experts. The PCA plays a central role in the release process of bare-die and discrete SiC products for use in automotive electronics of the future.
Success in this role relies on intense collaborations with the team and all relevant stakeholders and a high degree of personal responsibility. This requires the ability to coordinate and communicate with the different project stakeholders about technical performance of our devices during the release process and beyond. Furthermore, the role requires affinity with documentation, formal procedures and adherence to good practices and methods. The work involves a significant amount of data analysis, which means that fundamental understanding of statistics is a prerequisite. Basic programming skills (e.g., Python, MATLAB) or a strong willingness to learn are highly valued.
Finally, you will be responsible for product support on the development side after series release, identifying root causes of failures, and collaborating with cross-functional teams to drive continuous improvement in our processes. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in semiconductor physics and manufacturing, statistical data analysis, along with the ability to work structured and efficiently in a dynamic and fast-paced environment.
Core responsibilities
Managing the chip specifications of our silicon carbide power devices: Data analysis, product- and technology release processes and stakeholder management, incl. formal release aspects and documentation.
Sample planning and coordination of verification and validation testing during the engineering phase.
Definition of a series testing concept to safeguard device performance over lifetime during production.
Support in technical focus topics and setting-up as well as maintaining engineering methods and structures.

Qualifications
Completed university studies (Master's) in (semiconductor device) physics, electrical engineering, or equivalent in education.
Experienced in statistical data analysis, applied statistics and Design of Experiments (DOE).

Analytical Mindset: Capability to break down highly complex, multi-domain problems into structured, logical, and actionable architectural approaches.

Excellent skills in technical procedure writing / documentation and verbal communication.
Communicative team player with the ability to coordinate teams and a high degree of willingness to work across departments in an international environment.
Preferred Qualifications

Knowledge about (power) semiconductor manufacturing
Knowledge of German language (speaking, reading, writing) is a plus
Experience with electrical laboratory measurements and its challenges and limitations

Job Description
The
QCC Group Leader
is the ultimate custodian of quality standard operating procedures and educational excellence (OEM) across all delivery sites. This role does not directly manage front-line customer service agents but governs the global training and evaluation framework. The primary objective is to harmonize quality standards and ensure that agents in all operational sites deliver a seamless, uniform brand experience.
This position is fully onsite at our Fort Lauderdale, FL location.

Qualifications
Experience:
5+ years of Quality Assurance & Training leadership experience within a multi-site, multi-lingual call center environment.
Systems:
Deep familiarity with Quality Assurance platforms (experience with
2Mares
or migrating to modern platforms like Playvox/Scorebuddy is highly valued) and Learning Management Systems (LMS).
Language:
Native-level or fluent professional English (written and verbal).
The "Analytical Educator":
Highly structured, pedagogical, and detail oriented. Able to translate complex data into simple, actionable training plans.
Cross-Cultural Collaborator:
Skilled at managing relationships and aligning standards across diverse, international teams in all delivery sites.
Proactive Problem Solver:
Able to diagnose root causes of low CSAT or high escalation rates and rapidly deploy curriculum updates to address them.
Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
Calibration Alignment Rate:
Maintain a QA scoring variance at target levels across all sites during monthly calibration audits.
Curriculum Update Velocity:
Rapid deployment of training modifications following a process or system change.
New Hire Time-to-Baseline:
Achieve target threshold of new hires reaching operational QA performance baselines within the post-training nesting window.

Additional Information
Global Curriculum & Training Governance:
Own and design the end-to-end global training curriculum, onboarding pathways, and continuous education materials. Identify global and local training needs.
Monthly Calibration Ownership:
Run and govern monthly quality calibration sessions involving local site QA leads and Team Leaders across all delivery sites to maintain absolute evaluation alignment.
QA Tooling Migration Support:
Lead the QCC team in utilizing the current QA platform (
2Mares
) while actively spearheading the evaluation, setup, and deployment of a new, modernized QA evaluation tool.
Performance Diagnostics & Insights:
Analyze data trends from Quality Checks, CSAT/NPS, escalated customer cases, and agent knowledge tests to pinpoint performance gaps.
Actionable Hand-offs to Local Operations:
Package QA findings and deliver structured recommendations to local delivery site managers. Ensure local Team Leaders are equipped with the exact insights needed to coach agents effectively.

Job Description
The
SCC Group Leader
is the "air traffic controller" of the international service center. This role holds full operational and disciplinary responsibility for the workforce management (WFM) pipeline and intraday steering team. The primary objective is to balance customer demand with agent supply, maintaining high cost-efficiency (agent occupancy) while consistently meeting international Service Level Agreements (SLAs).
This position is fully onsite at our Fort Lauderdale, FL location.

Qualifications
Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
Balanced Steering Index:
Maintain a highly optimized, weighted score that balances overall
SLA Achievement
with target
Agent Occupancy
(preventing both over-staffing and under-staffing).
Multi-Horizon Forecast Accuracy:
Keep volume and workload forecasting variance within a strict defined accuracy band.
Proactive Shrinkage Mitigation:
Timely escalation of shrinkage anomalies to the GOM with immediate capacity recovery plans.
Requirements & Tech Stack
Experience:
5+ years of workforce management (WFM) leadership experience, specifically managing multi-site, multi-queue routing environments.
Systems:
Advanced, hands-on administrative expertise in
Verint WFM
software (essential) and ACD telephony systems (e.g., Genesys, Avaya, Cisco).

Additional Information
Key Responsibilities
Multi-Horizon Planning:
Oversee the end-to-end forecasting and capacity planning pipeline, managing dedicated planners to predict call volumes and staffing needs across short, mid, and long-term horizons.
Schedule Ownership & Sign-off:
Direct the agent scheduling process and sign off on final rosters across all regions, ensuring optimal coverage that respects local labor laws in the US, Costa Rica, and the Philippines.
Tactical Intraday Command:
Direct real-time steering. Holds
absolute authority
to instruct local operations to move agents between lines of business, queues, and countries during SLA emergencies (local operations are
informed
of moves, not negotiated with).
Shrinkage & Risk Management:
Monitor, track, and proactively flag shrinkage metrics (e.g., absenteeism, unplanned time off, meeting/training overhead) and escalate remediation plans directly to the GOM.
Data-Driven Reporting:
Provide daily, weekly, and monthly performance reviews analyzing SLA delivery, forecast accuracy, shrinkage impact, and agent occupancy levels to the GOM.
Leadership Style & Competencies
The "Air Traffic Controller":
Highly decisive, calm under pressure, and comfortable commanding a room. Able to make rapid, high-stakes tactical decisions to save SLAs.
Analytical Powerhouse:
Gifted with numbers, statistical forecasting models, and trend analysis.
Assertive Communicator:
Confident in giving direct instructions to local Site Managers to relocate staffing resources globally.

is a provider of diversified powertrain products and solutions across all market segments and with a product portfolio ranging from gasoline and diesel injection systems, electronics control units and software, to electrified powertrains with battery and fuel cell technologies.
We are the customer innovation management team within Bosch’s Powertrain Solutions (PS) division responsible for all technical collaboration activities with our customers in North America. We have access to a global pool of cutting-edge technology development that we utilize to engage our customer and carry these technologies from the innovation phase all the way into series production.

Take the lead:
You are the engineering interface to our North American customers for internal combustion engine, hybrid powertrains and electrification, fuel cell, thermal management, electronics, software, and connected powertrain projects
You’re in charge:
You manage and coordinate all internal and external stakeholders on powertrain innovation and acquisition programs
Deliver excellence:
You lead cross-functional project teams to ensure portfolio alignment and customer satisfaction
Leave your footprint:
You engage our customer on advanced engineering collaborations and product innovation activities
Keep us on track:

The HydraForce Technical Assembler Rotational Program is designed to develop future leaders in manufacturing by providing hands-on experience across key areas of our operations. Participants will build a strong foundation in hydraulic manufacturing while gaining exposure to HydraForce processes, standards, quality systems, and continuous improvement practices.
Throughout the program, participants will rotate through nine key departments, working alongside experienced team members and a dedicated mentor who will provide guidance, support, and feedback throughout the program.

Support / Logistics

Quality – Inspection
– Develop skills in inspection methods, measurement, and quality standards.
Honing

Assembly
– Build knowledge of hydraulic component assembly processes and standards.
Testing
– Learn testing procedures and how to verify product performance and functionality.
Quality – Auditing
– Understand quality audits, compliance, and process controls.
Quality – Warranty
– Gain insight into warranty processes, root-cause analysis, and customer-focused quality.
Manufacturing Engineering
– Learn how manufacturing processes are developed, optimized, and supported.
Lean Manufacturing
– Apply Lean principles and continuous improvement methodologies to improve safety, quality, delivery, and efficiency.
Each rotation includes defined learning objectives, activities, and timeframes to ensure participants develop a broad understanding of hydraulic manufacturing and how the various functions work together.
This program provides a unique opportunity for individuals who are interested in manufacturing, hydraulics, leadership, and continuous improvement to develop the technical knowledge and cross-functional experience needed to grow their careers with HydraForce.

This role is hybrid remote with 60% monthly in-office presence in Mount Prospect, Illinois. (3 days in office per week).

Create and mentor others for on-product warning label content per ANSI Z535
Review product photography, videography, and marketing artwork for accurate representation of reasonably safe use and compliance with operating instructions and warnings.
Mentor and train other Product Safety Engineers.
Train product development teams on Product Safety requirements and workflow.
Create and update Product Safety procedures and design guidelines.
Support product investigations for testing and field returns.

Job Description
As a Senior Cycle Counter, you will be a cornerstone of the plant’s inventory control function and a key driver in our mission to achieve best-in-class inventory accuracy. You are a proactive, hands-on expert responsible for not only executing complex cycle counts but also for investigating, analyzing, and resolving the root causes of inventory discrepancies.
Your primary mission is to significantly improve our inventory accuracy, which is currently a critical challenge with a discrepancy rate of 40%. By identifying systemic process gaps and ensuring our physical inventory aligns with SAP S/4HANA records, you will directly contribute to strengthening our internal controls, reducing financial losses, and improving operational efficiency. This role is crucial for ensuring our financial and operational processes are fully aligned with global Bosch standards for accuracy and compliance in direct coordination with the Plant management and the Finance department.
Key Responsibilities
· Lead Root-Cause Analysis & Investigation (60%):
o Lead detailed, second-level investigations into inventory discrepancies identified during cycle counts.
o Perform comprehensive root-cause analysis by auditing transaction histories in SAP (e.g., goods receipts, production postings, scrap movements) to identify process breakdowns.
o Partner with Materials Management, Receiving, Production, and Shipping to resolve systemic errors that lead to physical-to-system imbalances.
o Work with IT support staff to clear up queue issues where items get stuck and help get MM and WM inventories to sync.
o Document findings and present clear, actionable recommendations to the Inventory Supervisor to prevent recurrence.
· Execute Advanced Cycle Counting & Audits (30%):
o Conduct daily, scheduled, and ad-hoc cycle counts for high-value (Category A), critical, or complex inventory items, including raw materials, WIP, and finished goods.
o Perform process audits to ensure adherence to standard operating procedures (SOPs) for material handling and system transactions on the shop floor.
o Ensure all count data is entered into SAP S/4HANA with exceptional accuracy and timeliness, serving as the final verifier for count integrity.
· Drive Process Improvement & Team Mentorship (10%):
o Continuously analyze and identify opportunities to streamline counting procedures, improve warehouse organization, and enhance inventory transaction accuracy.
o Provide expert guidance, training, and daily support to Cycle Counter I and II team members, acting as the subject matter expert for counting best practices and SAP procedures.
o Serve as the on-site specialist for inventory control processes, acting as the first point of contact for troubleshooting complex counting and system-related issues.

Job Description
Our Bosch Research team occupies a critical position between academic research and product development, distinguishing us from many other companies. We engage with academia, incubate ideas, advance them to the prototype stage, and collaborate with development teams in our business units to support product development based on our research outcomes. We are seeking a research scientist with a strong academic background, proven industry experience, and a passion for tackling complex, real-world problems in molecular diagnostics.
Our R&D center is located in Sunnyvale, CA, USA. This is in the heart of Silicon Valley in close proximity to Stanford University and UC Berkeley. The candidate will be a key contributor to our research and development efforts, from conceptualization to the creation of novel technologies. This is an exciting opportunity for someone with industry experience who is eager to make a significant impact in the field of molecular sensors and biotechnology.
Responsibilities:
Identify, incubate, and translate cutting-edge academic research into functional, scalable proof-of-concept technologies in molecular diagnostics and biosensing.
Lead hands-on development and testing of prototype diagnostic systems, integrating microfluidics, electrochemical sensing, soft electronics, and chip-scale nanofabrication.
Collaborate closely with internal business units, engineering teams, and external academic partners (e.g., Stanford, UC Berkeley) to transition early-stage research into commercially viable product pipelines.
Design and execute advanced experiments for single-molecule detection, assay integration, and sample-to-answer cartridge performance.
Protect innovation through patent filings while contributing high-impact scientific publications and technical documentation.
Serve as a subject matter expert in biosensors and bioelectronics, advising multidisciplinary teams on technical feasibility, risk mitigation, and system architecture.

Qualifications
Education:
PhD in a relevant field (e.g., Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Bioengineering, Physics, or a related discipline)
Industry Experience:
3-5 years of previous industry experience in a relevant biotechnology company. We highly value experience in translating academic ideas into real-world products.
Molecular Diagnostics Expertise:
Proven experience in building real-world solutions in the biotechnology sector, particularly in single molecule detection and instrumentation for molecular diagnostics.
Integrated Systems Experience:
Demonstrated experience with integrated molecular diagnostic platforms, such as cartridge design, on-chip sample-prep, and electronics.
Soft Electronics:
experience with soft electronics for applications in biosensing.
Micro/Nanofabrication:
experience with chip design and process development for applications in biosensing.
Electrochemical Sensing:
experience with electrochemical systems and biosensors.
Biochemistry:
familiarity with the principles of biochemistry.
Proven track record of scientific accomplishment/patent filings
Soft skills: highly motivated and passionate about developing new technologies and products; strong documentation, oral and interpersonal skills, experience working in a multidisciplinary team.

Additional Information
This is a U.S. based position, domestic relocation and local sponsorship considered on a per candidate basis.
The U.S. base salary range for this full-time position is $170,000 - $200,000. Within the range, individual pay is determined based on several factors, including, but not limited to, work experience and job knowledge, complexity of the role, job location, etc. Your Recruiter can share more details about the specific salary range for this position during the interview process.
In addition to your base salary, Bosch offers a comprehensive benefits package that includes health, dental, and vision plans; health savings accounts (HSA); flexible spending accounts; 401(K) retirement plans with an employer match; wellness programs; life insurance; short- and long-term disability insurance; paid time off; parental leave, adoption assistance; and reimbursement of education expenses.
Equal Opportunity Employer, including disability / veterans.
*Bosch adheres to Federal, State, and Local laws regarding drug-testing. Employment is contingent upon the successful completion of a drug screen and background check. Candidates who have been offered the position must pass both screenings before their start date.

Job Description
The Line Planner is responsible for the daily technical performance of the assigned production line. This role serves as the primary engineering partner to Operations, ensuring equipment, processes, and cross-functional resources work together to maintain safe, stable, and efficient production.
The Line Planner provides real-time visibility into line performance, coordinates issue resolution, leads structured escalation of production risks, and drives rapid recovery to standard operating conditions. While focused on daily execution, the Line Planner also identifies recurring issues and partners with the Process Group to implement long-term improvements.
Key Responsibilities
Daily Production Performance
Own the daily technical performance of assigned production lines.
Monitor machine status, production flow, and key performance metrics.
Identify production risks and proactively communicate impacts to Operations.
Issue Management & Escalation
Lead structured escalation of safety, quality, delivery, and equipment issues.
Coordinate cross-functional resources including Operations, Maintenance, Quality, and the Process Group.
Ensure production issues are documented and communicated effectively.
Production Recovery
Drive rapid problem solving to restore production to standard conditions.
Verify that corrective actions achieve expected performance.
Escalate recurring or systemic issues for long-term investigation.
Standardization
Maintain manufacturing documentation including work instructions and engineering standards.
Support adherence to standardized work across the production line.
Identify opportunities to improve standard work based on daily observations.
Performance & Capacity Support
Monitor production performance trends and identify emerging risks.
Support production planning through cycle time, capacity, and equipment performance analysis.
Assist with launch activities and production readiness.
Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
Line OEE
Downtime reduction
Mean Time to Recovery (MTTR)
Schedule attainment
First Pass Yield / Scrap performance
On-time issue escalation
Completion of corrective actions
Accuracy of production reporting
The Line Planner is the engineering owner of daily production performance, ensuring manufacturing operates safely, efficiently, and consistently by coordinating rapid problem resolution, maintaining production standards, and enabling Operations to achieve stable performance every day.

Qualifications
Education
Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or related technical discipline.
Experience
3–7 years of manufacturing engineering or production engineering experience.
Experience supporting automated high-volume manufacturing operations.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to interpret complex production data
Excellent organizational and project management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities
Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to collaborate effectively across departments, extreme willingness to share know-how.
Detail-oriented mindset with a commitment to quality and operational excellence
Technical Skills
Root cause analysis (8D, A3, 5 Why, Fishbone)
Lean Manufacturing principles
Statistical process understanding
TRC & MRC
Manufacturing KPIs (OEE, FPY, Scrap, Tech/Org Downtime, Cycle Time)
Microsoft Excel and data analysis
MES, ERP, or production monitoring systems preferred
Databricks & Query language experience preferred
Success Profile
A successful Line Planner is someone who:
Thinks with urgency while remaining organized.
Can quickly prioritize competing production issues.
Communicates effectively across Operations, Maintenance, and Quality.
Uses data to drive decisions rather than assumptions.
Builds strong relationships across functions.
Escalates issues early and follows through until resolution.
Balances immediate production needs with continuous improvement opportunities.

Job Description
The Senior Sales Account Manager position is an individual contributor responsible for managing all aspects of component sales (sensors and semiconductors) including management of the relationship with automotive OEMs and automotive Tier-1 customers.
Key Responsibilities:
Commercial Management: You will oversee the commercial activities for defined directed-buy Tier customers, OEM business, and foundry business. You will be responsible for ensuring smooth business operations with these accounts including but not limited to: sales (price and volume) reporting by calendar year, logistics and sample coordination, special sales tracking, price and contract negotiations, and all other commercial related topics.
Quotations & Order Management: You will manage the end-to-end process for customer quotations, purchase order confirmations, and order management. This will include handling inquiries, preparing accurate quotes, and ensuring timely confirmation of orders to meet customer expectations.
New Acquisition & Price Negotiations: You will lead negotiations on applicable price adders with Tier customers, ensuring that pricing is competitive and aligned with business objectives. You will maintain strong relationships with your customers to facilitate successful outcomes. Ascertaining new business opportunities and acquisition of Bosch’s Semiconductors and Sensor components with new and existing customers.
Collaboration with OE Sales Teams: You will work closely with original equipment (OE) sales teams to ensure alignment on business strategies and customer requirements. Your collaboration will be critical to ensuring seamless communication between the Tier customers and OE teams.
Account Receivables Management: You will take ownership of account receivables for your Tier customers, foundry customers and OEM customers, actively monitoring payments, and initiating escalation steps when necessary. Your goal will be to maintain healthy cash flow and resolve any payment-related issues.

Qualifications
Required:
Bachelor’s Degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science Engineering, Business Administration OR 10+ years of relevant Sales experience in the Semiconductor space
7+ years of experience working in a commercial sales role in the automotive or mobility space, with a focus on semiconductors and sensor components

Engineering Trainer - Commercial HVAC Applications
will be a key member of the Bosch Home Comfort Factory Training team, reporting directly to the Sales Technology and Training Innovation Lead. This role is central to our mission of driving the specification of Bosch technologies by empowering the engineering and design community. The position champions a design-focused training philosophy, educating specifying engineers, design-build contractors, and bid-spec representatives on the superior application and performance of our commercial HVAC portfolio.
As a technical authority, the Application Trainer is pivotal in supporting the market integration of our newly expanded commercial product lines. The role involves creating and delivering sophisticated, application-focused training that positions Bosch, FHP, and Hitachi systems as the preferred solution in competitive bids and project specifications. The ideal candidate has deep expertise in the system design, application, and specification of light commercial rooftops, commercial Water Source Heat Pump (WSHP) systems, and 3-phase Variable Refrigerant Flow (VRF) systems. This mid-level salaried position involves up to 30% travel across the United States and Canada and requires a blend of engineering acumen, polished presentation skills, and a passion for influencing the future of building design.

Job Description
We are seeking a hands-on, results-oriented
Prototyping Specialist
to support our engineering team by manufacturing prototype components, improving fabrication processes, and advancing our prototyping capabilities. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys solving technical challenges, working with a variety of manufacturing technologies, and contributing directly to product innovation. You will be supporting the prototype shop quality management system by developing work instructions, maintaining documentation, participating in audits, and ensuring compliance with established procedures.
Responsibilities
Manufacture prototype components to support new product development and engineering validation activities.
Program, set up, and operate 3-axis CNC milling equipment to produce precision parts.
Perform post-processing, inspections, and quality verification of machined components.
Fabricate non-CNC components using manual machining equipment (mills and lathes), metal cutting and forming equipment, woodworking tools, welding, brazing, fiberglass layup and other fabrication methods.
Produce prototype components using FDM and SLA 3D printing technologies, including post-processing and finishing.
Assemble fabricated components into functional prototype assemblies.
Collaborate closely with engineers to modify designs and develop manufacturable prototype solutions.
Recommend improvements to fabrication methods, material selection, and component designs to improve manufacturability, quality, and build efficiency.
Estimate project timelines, prioritize work, and communicate project status to stakeholders.
Maintain a safe, organized, and efficient prototype shop environment.
Perform preventive maintenance and routine calibration of CNC equipment and shop tools.
Monitor inventory levels of materials, tooling, and shop supplies and coordinate replenishment as needed.
Identify and implement continuous improvement opportunities that enhance safety, efficiency, quality, and cost effectiveness.
Advanced Responsibilities (Highly Qualified Candidates)
Evaluate and implement advanced CNC programming strategies, tooling, and machining technologies.
Research and assess emerging additive manufacturing technologies, materials, and fabrication methods.

Qualifications
High school diploma or equivalent.
3+ years of experience
in a prototype, machine shop, manufacturing, or fabrication environment.
Experience programming, setting up, and operating CNC milling machines.
Experience with CNC programming software (Mastercam preferred).
Experience operating manual machine tools, hand tools, and power tools.
Experience producing high-quality prototype or low-volume production components.
Familiarity with 3D CAD software (SolidWorks preferred).
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications.
Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, GD&T, and technical specifications.
Strong mechanical aptitude and problem-solving skills.
Ability to prioritize multiple projects while maintaining attention to detail.
Ability to safely lift up to 40 pounds and work in a manufacturing/shop environment.

Associate's degree or higher in Manufacturing Technology, Mechanical Engineering Technology, Mechanical Engineering, or a related technical field.
Experience with additive manufacturing technologies, including FDM and SLA printing.
Experience with welding, brazing, fiberglass fabrication, or composite manufacturing.

Experience implementing Lean Manufacturing or continuous improvement initiatives.

Job Description
The Senior Sales Manager position is an individual contributor responsible for managing all aspects of component sales (sensors and semiconductors) including management of the relationship with automotive OEMs and automotive Tier-1 customers.
Key Responsibilities:
Commercial Management: You will oversee the commercial activities for defined directed-buy Tier customers, OEM business, and foundry business. You will be responsible for ensuring smooth business operations with these accounts including but not limited to: sales (price and volume) reporting by calendar year, logistics and sample coordination, special sales tracking, price and contract negotiations, and all other commercial related topics.
Quotations & Order Management: You will manage the end-to-end process for customer quotations, purchase order confirmations, and order management. This will include handling inquiries, preparing accurate quotes, and ensuring timely confirmation of orders to meet customer expectations.
New Acquisition & Price Negotiations: You will lead negotiations on applicable price adders with Tier customers, ensuring that pricing is competitive and aligned with business objectives. You will maintain strong relationships with your customers to facilitate successful outcomes. Ascertaining new business opportunities and acquisition of Bosch’s Semiconductors and Sensor components with new and existing customers.
Collaboration with OE Sales Teams: You will work closely with original equipment (OE) sales teams to ensure alignment on business strategies and customer requirements. Your collaboration will be critical to ensuring seamless communication between the Tier customers and OE teams.
Account Receivables Management: You will take ownership of account receivables for your Tier customers, foundry customers and OEM customers, actively monitoring payments, and initiating escalation steps when necessary. Your goal will be to maintain healthy cash flow and resolve any payment-related issues.

Qualifications
Required:
Bachelor’s Degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science Engineering, Business Administration OR 10+ years of relevant Sales experience in the Semiconductor space
7+ years of experience working in a commercial sales role in the automotive or mobility space, with a focus on semiconductors and sensor components
Ability to build relationships with internal and external stakeholders, both locally and globally
15-20% travel nationally/internationally as required for customer meetings, training, and customer support (May be required to spend 2 weeks in Germany for initial commercial and technical training)
Preferred:
Sales experience with silicon carbide, power electronics, semiconductors and/or MEMS semiconductor devices
An understanding of the major Automotive OEM customers, Tier-1 suppliers, and related semiconductor electronics market
Knowledge of vehicles systems utilizing power electronics (i.e. inverters, onboard chargers, converters etc.)
Knowledge of other vehicle systems including, navigation and mobility, safety systems including airbag systems, and/or braking systems
Ability to work both independently and as part of a global team
Excellent organizational skills to properly track and report customer account progress to management
Excellent communication skills with the ability to convey detailed messages to customers and to international audiences
Experience in customer account management including negotiations and commercial functions
Strong entrepreneurial mindset with a clear understanding of the business environment

Be the Key Contributor to the marketing strategy development and ensure strategy implementation of external product communication plans for the assigned Business Unit technology.
Drive top-of-funnel inbound marketing and ensure integration of appropriate content and messaging from central business units in Germany into the North American Region, while also harmonizing across all mediums of communications.
Provide all Marketing support for the business unit trade fairs and events along with Product Management and Sales.
Coordinate the development and execution of technology-specific content, communication materials, and/or campaigns to meet brand guidelines.
Utilize an integrated multichannel approach to marketing for both online and offline channels. Select appropriate communication mix, content, and timing to deliver the right message to the right audience to maximize effectiveness.  This includes, but is not limited to, public relations, editorial opportunities, social media, paid media, event marketing content, technical product content development (tech papers, whitepapers, etc), e-communications, videos, newsletters, webinars and more.
In collaboration with agency, select appropriate media, content, and timing to deliver the right message to the right audience to maximize total contacts and qualified leads, impressions, and other defined KPI. Ensure contacts generated are qualified and nurtured to further their journey to becoming sales qualified.
Compile, maintain data, and report on success of campaigns and marketing activities for assigned technology topics. Identify, track and report on lead generation. Manage spend for defined budget and report on monthly basis to key stakeholders.
Collaborate with other members of Marketing and Product Management to integrate consistent product content, promotions strategy, and branding into various platforms, media, with customization by distributor as needed. Ensure the timely and frequent update of website content for assigned topics.
Continuously utilize market research and market intelligence to benchmark Bosch Rexroth against key competitor go-to-market positions, maintain in-depth knowledge of how to differentiate Bosch Rexroth’s technology within the market.
Support distributor-specific projects with communication materials, communicate marcom plans that enhance distributor growth, maintain relevant content availability on extranet systems (myRexroth).
Support the marketing communications manager and greater marketing department in the development and execution of cross-technology content and tactics as needed.

Fundamental financial acumen to manage and track marketing budgets.

German language skills and/or SAP experience.
