1318_Autonomous Driving System Architect for Heavy Machinery and Construction Machinery
Job Overview
[Background]
Under the mission of "democratizing autonomous driving," TIER IV is releasing autonomous driving software as open source and advancing product development as a system actually embedded in vehicles. The technology accumulated during research and demonstration stages is now entering the mass production phase, with full-scale introduction across multiple vehicle models and platforms. 
Software for mass production requires design quality that can withstand years of maintenance, added features, and deployment (porting) to other platforms, in addition to performing prescribed operations. To develop autonomous driving software, which is built on numerous algorithms, from a mere "running" state into a "reliable product for business," it is essential for experienced architects to understand the overall system configuration and make decisions regarding software architecture and quality standards. 
On top of that, in addition to initiatives for paved driving environments such as urban areas and main roads, our company is also developing for the practical introduction and commercialization of autonomous driving under so-called off-road (rough) driving conditions such as unpaved gravel roads and rocky rough roads. 
Among the above, in the field of uneven terrain where heavy machinery and construction machinery take center stage, you will serve as a software technology leader, participating in architectural design that analyzes hardware and software, formulates design policies tailored to the conditions of the client where the equipment is introduced, distinguishes between in-house development and external technologies, and promotes the selection and collaboration of development partners. Knowledge of heavy machinery and construction machinery, which exhibits behavior different from paved roads and customer requirements, is also a major factor. 
[Job Description]
Our main focus is autonomous driving systems for heavy machinery and construction machinery, based on the open-source autonomous driving software "Autoware." As a technical leader in this field, we are responsible for promoting design and development for individual projects and establishing common design policies across projects, delving into both software and hardware aspects. 
With different assumptions depending on the site and application, our mission is to equip Autoware and related tools according to the situation, raise the level of stable use in actual fields (quality sufficient for service operation), standardize the outcomes of each project internally as much as possible, and lead to company-wide optimization. 
Examples of Main Responsibilities
- Design of hardware and software for autonomous driving for heavy machinery and construction machinery, assuming uneven terrain conditions
- Formulate individual design policies for each project
- Promoting the standardization of autonomous driving architectures for heavy machinery and construction machinery within the company
- Deciding whether to adopt external technologies in function development for the same field and promoting collaboration with partner companies
[Challenges & Rewards]
TIER IV is committed to providing practical systems and services for a wide range of customers in pursuit of the "democratization of autonomous driving." This position focuses especially on heavy machinery, construction machinery, and uneven terrain driving conditions, playing a leading role in technology. 
The stages of projects you will be responsible for vary widely, from verifying the level where vehicles can be operated using Autoware (such as proof of concept and PoC), to the full-scale commercialization phase that raises the quality to sustainable operation. You can expect opportunities to be deeply involved throughout the entire process from planning, construction, to operation.

1403_Head of Safety Strategy
Job Overview
[Background]
To become a platformer in the autonomous driving field and provide solutions for Level 4 service realization, it is essential that TIER IV’s solutions possess safety assurances recognized globally. We are seeking a leader to establish the framework for explaining the safety of our organization, products, and processes.
[Job Content]
You will be responsible for coordinating the formulation and implementation of a global-standard safety strategy. This involves establishing a Safety Management System (SMS) that integrates all elements of the organization, product, and process, and translating this into organizational activities that enable the creation of Safety Cases for individual products or projects.
Specific Responsibilities:
SMS Establishment: Lead the development of strategic and tactical Safety Management System (SMS) implementation plans. Define the ideal state of SMS based on the current status and clarify the gap between the current state and the ideal.
Safety Case Framework: Build the organizational capability to create Safety Cases that explain the safety of individual products and projects. Establish a working structure to identify logical gaps and evidence needs for the safety case for continuous improvements.
Gap Analysis & Execution: Identify gaps in current SMS and Safety Cases; prioritize activities to address them and build an execution structure in collaboration with other departments (D&T, DevOps, etc.).
Stakeholder Consensus: Gain consensus among internal stakeholders, partners, and customers on safety definitions and risk acceptance strategies using the established SMS and Safety Case frameworks.
Global Benchmarking and activity promotion: Research global standards for SMS and Safety Cases to ensure our policy is aligned with industry best practices and promote TIER IV’s safety activities globally.
[Challenges / Rewarding Aspects]
Global Impact: You will shape the company wide safety strategy in a high-paced and interdisciplinary environment aiming to be a global platformer for L4 autonomous driving, ensuring our technology is trusted worldwide.
Strategic Leadership: This role moves beyond execution into defining "How" organizational safety is managed, directly influencing the company's ability to deploy services. You will be working with first-in-class colleagues of various functions on a daily basis.
Cross-Functional Influence: You will act as the bridge between engineering, operations, and external stakeholders, creating the "Safety Logic" that underpins our commercial success.

Job Overview
[Background of Recruitment]
At TIER IV, for the social implementation of autonomous driving systems, not only technology development but also the establishment of regulatory compliance, certification, quality assurance, and experimental management systems for demonstration experiments, commercial implementation, and various projects is becoming increasingly important. 
Going forward, to systematically streamline and strengthen tasks related to experimental management and regulatory compliance, we are seeking individuals with practical experience in regulatory compliance, certification, quality assurance, and experimental management at OEMs and automotive-related companies.

1406_Test Platform Engineer, System Verification & Validation
Job Overview
[Background]
At Tier IV, to achieve its mission of democratizing autonomous driving, we open-source autonomous driving software and provide reference designs that integrate hardware (sensors, ECUs, vehicles) that meet the requirements of that software. 
By lowering entry barriers for new autonomous driving system developers and service developers, we aim to revitalize the autonomous driving community and accelerate community-led autonomous driving system development. 
To ensure the safety and reliability of autonomous driving software, you will be responsible for the conception, design, and development of a next-generation evaluation platform that combines simulation and actual equipment. 
Our mission is to build the entire ecosystem that supports the core of autonomous driving development, from automatically generating scenarios based on the vast driving data collected from actual fleets, to automated testing in CI/CD pipelines and automatic pass/fail judgments. 
[Job Description]
- Analysis of evaluation needs and concept design: Analyze product evaluation needs, design the evaluation environment concept, and create a development plan.
- Building an automatic evaluation scenario generation pipeline: Develop a mechanism to extract edge cases and critical driving scenarios from actual fleet driving data and automatically generate evaluation scenarios
- Integration and development of simulation environments: Build an end-to-end evaluation environment combining various in-house and OSS/commercial simulators (CARLA, Vissim, Foretify, etc.) and scenario generation tools (in collaboration with the simulator development team)
- Promoting CI/CD and test automation: integrating CI/CD systems with simulation environments and integrating them into the DevOps cycle (in collaboration with the CI/CD team)
[Challenges & Rewards]
At Tier IV, we are developing autonomous driving systems to advance the "democratization of autonomous driving." 
We are challenging ourselves to broadly understand autonomous driving and to create something that operates safely.

Scope of change: In addition to the above, the tasks designated by the company

data.job_description:
1805_Technical Project Manager & Autonomous Driving System Development
Job Overview
[Background]
At Tier IV, we uphold the vision of "democratizing autonomous driving," developing and operating the world's first open-source autonomous driving software, Autoware, and globally providing products, solutions, and services related to autonomous driving. Our ecosystem includes companies from around the world, accelerating the pace of technological innovation while promoting the social implementation of practical Level 4 autonomous driving in fields such as public transportation and logistics. 
To realize this grand vision, it is essential to highly integrate AI, software, hardware, and vehicle platforms to function as a single complete "system." In the yet-to-be-definitive autonomous driving development, we are seeking a technically savvy project leader who can unravel complex technical dependencies, drive projects from the engineering frontline, and establish Tier4's competitive advantage. 
[Job Description]
As the commander of autonomous driving system development, you will lead technical management from the formulation of the development roadmap to implementation and evaluation. Our mission is to act as a bridge between the engineering team and the business and on-site operations teams, ensuring technical validity while achieving a high degree of balance between "zero development stagnation" and "maximizing safety and quality." 
< Formulation of development plans and establishment of master schedules>
Integrate the needs and technical feasibility of each business division to define a roadmap for functional development of autonomous driving systems. 
Visualize complex software stacks and hardware dependencies to identify critical project paths. Build and manage master schedules. 
< Controlling Technology Dependencies>
Inter-team coordination: 
Leads interface coordination between software and hardware (sensors and computers) to prevent inconsistencies during integration. 
Eliminating technical bottlenecks: 
Overcome technical trade-offs arising during development (e.g., balancing computational resources and recognition accuracy), it derives optimal solutions from an architectural perspective and accelerates decision-making. 
< Execution instructions and quality control of the development process>
Instructions to the engineering team: 
Based on established milestones, optimize sprint priorities and resource allocation. Quantitatively track development progress and detect and eliminate delay risks early. 
Ensuring safety and reliability: 
Concepts such as functional safety (ISO 26262) and SOTIF (ISO 21448) are incorporated into the development process to ensure quality that can withstand demonstration experiments and social implementation. 
< Consensus building and allocation among stakeholders>
When technical challenges or resource constraints arise, develop development scope adjustment plans based on company-wide priorities. Lead consensus building among stakeholders, including management, customers, and partner companies. 
< Rapid adaptation based on field data>
Immediately feedback evaluation results from demonstration experiments and test courses back to the engineering team. 
For edge cases or defects that occur on-site, short-term recovery measures and medium- to long-term functional improvement measures are organized and directly reflected in development plans to prevent delivery stagnation.

2006_Project Manager / Logistics Business Domain / Customer Projects
Job Overview
[Background]
TIER IV develops and operates the open-source autonomous driving software "Autoware" under the vision of "democratizing autonomous driving." It is building an ecosystem where companies worldwide can contribute to the evolution of autonomous driving technology, accelerating the pace of technological innovation. 
Through this initiative, we actively contribute to social implementation. 
- Public Transportation: Accelerating the realization of autonomous vehicles, systems, and services aimed at improving convenience and traffic safety.
- Logistics: Aiming to improve productivity and ensure occupational safety through automation at various sites such as factories, civil engineering sites, and steel mills.
We develop software platforms based on Autoware, "Pilot.Auto" and "Web.Auto," supporting customers' efficient development and operations. Pilot.Auto is TIER IV-verified autonomous driving software and reference design, while Web.Auto is a cloud-native DevOps development environment. 
To further advance these initiatives, we are recruiting project managers (logistics field, technology) to lead projects utilizing Pilot.Auto and Web.Auto. 
* Reference Information
https://pilot.auto/ 
https://web.auto/ 
[Job Description]
The role of the project manager (logistics, technical) is to work closely with engineers and lead the entire process from the design to operation of autonomous driving systems and services. You are responsible for the success of projects that deliver our autonomous driving solutions using Autoware to a wide range of customers, including truck manufacturers, construction equipment manufacturers, and operators responsible for their own logistics and transportation. 
The specific duties are as follows. 
- Project management and promotion: 
- Thoroughly listen to customer requirements (vehicles and use cases) and design the entire project
- Define project KPIs (Key Performance Indicators) and KGIs (Key Goal Indicators) to visualize and manage progress
- General project management, including staffing, budget and cost calculations, and schedule management
- Project Leadership from a Technical Perspective: 
- Deep understanding of Autoware's specifications and features, standing in the customer's shoes to present the overall technical direction of the project
- Involve development and evaluation teams to integrate diverse internal and external technologies to build and deliver optimal solutions for customers
- Collaboration with customers: 
- Attempt to answer technical inquiries and challenges during project progress independently, and collaborate with engineers to develop solutions as needed.
- Deeply understand customer needs and propose optimal solutions to ensure our autonomous driving services contribute to their business to the fullest extent
This position goes beyond simple development and operation, aiming to solve challenges in the logistics industry and improve customer satisfaction through autonomous driving services. Together with someone who possesses deep knowledge of Autoware and autonomous driving technology in general, overall project management skills, and a perspective that understands customer needs, we aim to create the future of logistics. 
[Challenges & Rewards]
- A sense of accomplishment from implementing advanced technology in society
This position is a role that consistently leads the entire process from the design to operation of autonomous driving systems. Solving complex technical challenges and leading the entire project to success is a major challenge. Your strategic decisions lead to the creation of innovative autonomous driving services that do not yet exist, leading to a sense of accomplishment that makes a significant social impact. 
- Leadership leveraging a wide range of expertise
The success of a project depends on the strength of the entire team. You will not only manage but also leverage your deep knowledge of Autoware and autonomous driving technologies to lead the resolution of technical challenges. By working closely with the development and evaluation teams and demonstrating leadership that maximizes each person's expertise, you will find great fulfillment in guiding projects to achieve their goals. 
- Creating the future with diverse stakeholders
You will engage with professionals from various positions, including truck and construction machinery manufacturers, logistics operators, as well as in-house engineers and executives. By gaining a comprehensive view from multiple perspectives such as technology, business, and customer needs, and driving projects, you can greatly broaden your horizons and deepen your career. 
- Pioneering the future of autonomous driving with your own hands
We are not just applying existing technologies; we are creating new autonomous driving services themselves. This position represents the greatest challenge as a core member of a startup shaping the future of autonomous driving, challenging unexplored territory that no one has yet accomplished.

Job Overview
[Background]
At Tier IV, to achieve its mission of "democratizing autonomous driving," we have open-sourced autonomous driving software (Autoware) and are promoting joint development of vehicles equipped with autonomous driving systems with partners such as domestic and international automakers (OEMs/ODMs), auto parts suppliers, and software development companies, as well as demonstration experiments based on close collaboration with national and local governments. By promoting broad joint development with major domestic and international companies as well as startups in the automotive industry, we are accelerating the social implementation of safe and convenient autonomous driving both domestically and internationally. 
Among the above initiatives, we are seeking people who can promote and manage demonstration pilot projects across various regions to further advance the social implementation of autonomous driving in Japan.

- Management of team members such as promotion staff

2040_Strategic Supply and Demand Management Lead
Job Overview
[Background]
At Tier IV, we uphold the vision of "democratizing autonomous driving," developing and operating Autoware, an open-source autonomous driving software, providing products, solutions, and services related to autonomous driving. This initiative has created an environment where companies worldwide can contribute to the evolution of autonomous driving technology, accelerating the pace of technological innovation and advancing social implementation. 
To realize this ambitious vision, it is essential to optimally source cutting-edge sensors, computers, and vehicle platforms from around the world and build a solid global supply system. In the autonomous driving market, where there is still no right answer, we are seeking leaders who can design logistics and supply networks from scratch that break free from traditional frameworks and establish Tier IVo's competitive advantage from an SCM perspective. 
[Job Description]
As the commander of strategic parts procurement, you will lead supply-demand planning linked to each project and vehicle development schedule. Our mission is to present data-driven strategies and policies to the SCM Department (logistics and order processing) and Procurement Department (purchasing and contracting), which handle practical operations, to achieve a high degree of balancing "zero stockout risk" with "optimization of inventory and capital efficiency." 
- Aggregation of demand information and building master schedules
-- Proactively conduct interviews with each business division and development project manager, integrating and visualizing company-wide parts demand based on the project's major schedule and vehicle construction plans. 
- Strategic PSI management and supply scenario planning
-- Design and operate PSI (Production, Sales, Inventory) charts yourself to forecast medium- to long-term inventory trends and their impact on cash flow. 
-- Considering lead times for each component, manufacturing process constraints, geopolitical risks, and more, we develop preventive procurement and production scenarios, including contingency plans (alternatives). 
- Cross-departmental execution instructions and orchestration
-- Instructions to the SCM Department: Based on confirmed demand, present optimal solutions for order timing and delivery priority. Manage and supervise the progress of PO (Order of Order) issuance operations. 
-- Collaboration with the Procurement Department: Understand supplier supply capacity and contract terms. Jointly promote priority supply negotiations during tight supply and strategies to secure long-lead products (including EOL products) in advance with the Procurement Department. 
- Completion of strategic allocation (internal allocation adjustment)
-- In situations where material supply is constrained, formulate optimal inventory allocation plans for each project based on company-wide priorities. Lead consensus building among stakeholders, including management. 
- Rapid adaptation to technological and quality changes
-- Work closely with the development team to detect early impacts on supply from changes in technical specifications and quality issues. Immediately feed back substitute securing and plan changes into supply and demand planning to prevent delivery stagnation.

2043_Business Management Manager & Business Planning
Job Overview
[Background]
Tier4 is developing Autoware, an open-source autonomous driving software aimed at popularizing and democratizing autonomous driving technology. This initiative has created an environment where companies and researchers worldwide can contribute to the evolution of autonomous driving technology, accelerating the pace of technological innovation. 
Furthermore, Tier4 provides commercial solutions for autonomous driving software and hardware platforms utilizing Autoware to automotive OEMs, integrators, and transportation operators, and is expanding its business. 
For Tier 4 to expand its autonomous driving technology business globally, it will be necessary to promote the business while appropriately managing planning and profitability by collaborating with domestic and international stakeholders such as business partners, development, manufacturing, sales, and affiliated companies. 
Against this backdrop, we are seeking a business management manager who can lead business expansion by promoting overall planning, budget and actual management, business analysis, and cross-departmental management within each business division. 
[Job Description]
- Formulation of medium-term plans and budget plans for business divisions, as well as budget management
- Reporting to management and business managers involved in business management
- Management and support of various cross-departmental projects
- Market analysis, data collection, and report preparation for business strategy formulation
- Establishment and operation of business portfolio management systems (improving customer databases, sales processes, etc.)

3019_Human Resources Planning Specialist
Job Overview
[Background]
In response to business growth and organizational expansion, TIER IV introduced a new total reward system (compensation, evaluation, and rating system) starting October 2025. In addition, initiatives such as the company-wide engagement survey to visualize organizational status, 360-degree evaluations to promote multifaceted growth, and DEIB initiatives that turn diversity into strength are also fully launched. For this recruitment, we are not only seeking candidates who will not only operate these new systems but also lead their penetration and retention in the field, rapidly running PDCA cycles to improve the quality of the system itself. 
[Job Description]
You will lead the planning, operation, and improvement of new HR systems and organizational development initiatives. 
- Improvement of the new evaluation system and ongoing deepening of operations
- Planning and delivery of evaluator training and other activities
- Planning, designing, operation, and issue analysis of engagement surveys
- Support for formulating organizational improvement actions based on survey results
- Operation of 360-degree evaluations aimed at human resource development
- Promotion of company-wide DEIB initiatives
[Challenges & Rewards]
Our personnel at TIER IV aim to become a new "reference model" within Japan's HR system, just as we lead the world in autonomous driving technology. 
Currently, we are working backward from the ideal image five years from now, building the ideal organizational form and deepening its operations.

3034_Service Desk Leader
Job Overview
[Background of Recruitment]
TIER IV operates a corporate IT and general affairs service desk for all employees company-wide. We have introduced a service operation system based on ITIL and begun developing processes for incident management, service request management, and change management. We have been promoting inquiry management based on a ticket management system and automation through chatbots, and as the next stage, we have entered a phase to further enhance service quality by further improving completion rates and lead times, enhancing overall team skills, and strengthening our organizational structure. Furthermore, strengthening IT controls and information security management systems (in compliance with ISO 27001) will become an important mission going forward. We are recruiting leaders who will autonomously promote these efforts, lead both "defense (stable operation and security control)" and "offense (business process improvement and digitalization)," and lead the team to improve overall quality, efficiency, and employee experience. 
[Job Description]
- Managing SLAs and KPIs (completion rate, lead time, and pending count) in handling inquiries via the ticket management system and leading continuous improvement
- Lead initial response to incidents, grasp the scope of impact, and escalation decisions, manage progress until all cases are closed, and analyze root causes to prevent recurrence
- Strengthening the team's overall responsiveness through 1st line work instructions, development, skill enhancement, and cross-training
- Promotion of self-service and improved automation rates through chatbot, service catalog, and FAQ development
- Continuous improvement of ITIL processes (incident management, service request management, issue management, change management) and introduction of other process management (such as service level management)
- Formulation of the service desk's medium- to long-term roadmap and alignment with corporate IT and general affairs strategies
- Designing, implementing, and analyzing employee satisfaction surveys, visualizing and improving silent dissatisfaction
- Establishment and clarification of escalation standards and processes for the 1st → 2nd lines
- Information security management for ISO 27001 compliance: risk assessment, formulation, implementation, and audit response of management measures
- Preparation and reporting of monthly service operation materials
- Planning and implementing basic IT training and promoting the use of AI tools
- Updating internal announcements and manuals, and maintaining an information-sharing system
[Challenges & Rewards]
- Lead service desks across both corporate IT and general affairs domains in an integrated manner, directly contributing to improving the work experience for all employees. 
- Beyond simple operational management, you can proactively drive "proactive improvements" by leveraging data and automation such as chatbot adoption, self-service adoption, and employee satisfaction survey design. 
- It is rewarding to lead phases of change, such as establishing 1st/2nd line systems and organizational changes, and designing scalable service desks. 
- This is a rare career opportunity that allows you to simultaneously advance the two major missions of further maturing ITIL operations and compliance with ISO 27001.

3037_New Graduate Recruitment Planning Specialist
Job Overview
[Background]
Tier IV is a deep tech startup with the vision of "democratizing autonomous driving," working on the social implementation of autonomous driving by utilizing open-source software. On July 22, 2026, it achieved a new listing on the growth market, and its business and organization continue to grow rapidly as we collaborate with many partners to realize this vision. 
To drive further business expansion and discover and acquire talent who will become the core of the organization in the future, we are launching and strengthening new graduate recruitment, and we are recruiting new graduate recruitment planning specialists who can handle everything from planning to execution of recruitment operations. 
[Job Description]
You will be responsible for the entire process of new graduate recruitment. Taking into account the career orientation and characteristics of new graduates, trends in the recruitment market and competition, and your company's strategy and business situation, you will formulate new graduate recruitment strategies and lead recruitment with significant autonomy by involving management and field managers. We will primarily target science and engineering students who have researched fields such as autonomous driving, AI, and robotics, and carefully select outstanding individuals who will be immediately effective to acquire talent. 
Additionally, the department you will be assigned to is the 'New Graduate Recruitment & Development Department,' where you will mainly be responsible for new graduate recruitment. While company-wide talent development is also part of your organizational mission, you will be responsible for everything from new graduate recruitment to post-hire development, allowing you to expand your role according to your career orientation and expertise. 
- Planning and executing new graduate recruitment strategies
- School visits, company information sessions, internship planning and management
- Communication with candidates (scouting, interviews, interview handling, etc.)
- Follow-up for successful candidates and planning and management of offer and induction ceremonies
- Onboarding planning and management
- Analysis of recruitment data, planning and implementation of improvement measures
- (Depending on other preferences and expertise) Planning and execution of talent development for new graduate hires, company-wide talent development planning, etc.
[Challenges & Rewards]
Our goal of "democratizing autonomous driving" is a challenge that no one has yet accomplished by creating a new ecosystem with partners worldwide through open source. Through the experience of Zero-One, which builds recruitment strategies and culture that attract the next generation of top talent, while accompanying a fast-paced business environment where top engineers gather, you can feel both your business growth and personal growth. 
New graduate recruitment has only just begun, with about 10 people hired in April 2026 and in the process of further full-scale operations. Therefore, rather than relying solely on established operations, you can take the lead with discretion from planning recruitment strategies to execution. Among various talent acquisition methods, you can engage in lively discussions with management and business leaders about why new graduate recruitment should be strengthened, and experiment with new initiatives.

aiDrive is an automated driving platform with revolutionary virtual sensor technology that brings unparalleled data reusability for all levels of autonomy and different sensor setups. Using the latest available camera and radar sensors as well as navigational map support, aiMotive can create state-of-the-art Highway Assist solutions with Automatic Lane Change and Highway Interchange Management. aiDrive can also enable vehicles to move through and park in structured parking environments without the driver being in or near the car with its proprietary Automated Valet Parking Application.
An accurate understanding of the surroundings of the vehicle is at the heart of automated driving applications, detecting and providing 3D properties of static and dynamic objects surrounding the vehicle is one of the fundamental building blocks in delivering a safe and reliable automated driving experience.
As a Research Engineer in the Road Model team, you will take part in prototyping new solutions, porting prototypes as reliable modules into real-time self-driving applications and improving and benchmarking existing solutions related to road structure and markings, traffic signs, traffic lights and their accurate 3D localization. You will work on solutions deployed in different environments like driving on a highway, city and you will see your code running in real cars on multiple continents.
Job Summary
- Research, develop, implement, and test artificial intelligence algorithms to improve the quality and robustness of the static world model in automated vehicles.
- Special focus on:
- Road structure – lanes, curbs, drivable trajectories
- Traffic sign and traffic light detection – including 3D position and class
- Produce maps of the static world based on detections
- Participate in designing the training and evaluation framework pipeline, propose architecture changes and perform code reviews
- Integrate prototype models into real-time self-driving systems
Key Requirements
- BS, MS, or PhD in Robotics, Computer Science, Physics, Mathematics, or related field
- Minimum 3 years of experience in an engineer role
- Strong Python programming and software design skills
- Strong mathematical skills (linear algebra and probability distributions)
- Experience in deep learning frameworks (Pytorch/Tensorflow)
- Experience in computer vision
- Experience in software development (git, code reviews, unit tests)
- Ability to work independently and systematically
Considered as a plus
- Programming in C++, working in Linux
- Experience in machine learning and data analysis
- Experience in Docker, Jenkins, Kubernetes
- Experience in robotics
- Experience in developing safety critical, embedded, or real-time systems
- Experience in computer graphics, physics simulation or other mathematics-intensive applications
What We Offer
- Competitive salary
- Fitness opportunities
- Corporate health insurance package
- Free lunch every office day, nearby at one of the best all-you-can-eat restaurants in Budapest or delivered by Wolt for Work
- Work on the hottest applied research problem in an agile working culture, backed by a strong, stable and future-proof industrial partnership
- Develop solutions for one of the largest car manufacturer with a global reach
- Test your solution in realistic simulated scenarios and a fleet of cars across multiple continents every day
- Be proud of seeing your solution on the road
- Visit relevant international conferences, submit patents of new solutions
- We believe: people over process, we are keen to maintain a work-life balance

- Compiler development for custom NPU
- Performance estimator for runtime execution of different Neural Network workloads

About
the Mission
GM’s vision of Zero Crashes, Zero Emissions, and Zero Congestion guides everything we do in autonomous and assisted driving. The AV organization is building advanced automated driving technologies, including Level 4–capable fully self-driving systems, to move us toward safer, more sustainable, and more accessible mobility.
For the AI Kernels & Compilers team, that mission shows up in the details: turning cutting‑edge perception, prediction, and planning research into production‑grade software that can run efficiently and reliably on real vehicles at scale. We pioneer new approaches to model export, kernel development, and performance engineering so that every cycle on our accelerators translates into better situational awareness, faster reaction times, and more robust behavior on the road.
If you want your compiler and kernels work to directly influence how automated vehicles understand and react to the world — while operating at the safety, reliability and scale of a company like GM — this is where that impact becomes real.
About the Team
The AI Compiler team sits at the heart of how advanced AI models make it onto the car. We own the compiler that turns high‑level models into fast, reliable inference across GPUs powering GM’s next‑generation autonomous and assisted driving features.
Our work spans graph lowering, operator coverage, kernel integration, and deployment tooling, with a mandate to squeeze every millisecond out of on‑vehicle workloads while preserving correctness and robustness in real‑world conditions. We partner closely with AI Deployments, AI Solutions, Runtime, and AI Kernels teams to co‑design a platform that enables new ideas in research to be quickly and safely shipped to production fleets.
You’ll join a group of deep compiler, systems, and GPU engineers who enjoy working on hard problems, and diving into MLIR/ONNX and CUDA/TensorRT internals. We value clear thinking, strong engineering fundamentals, and a culture where people can do the best work of their careers on problems that directly shape the future of automated driving.

As a Senior Compiler Engineer on the AI Kernels & Compilers team, you will work on the compilation stack that takes high‑level models and turns them into highly optimized inference artifacts running on GM’s autonomous and assisted driving platforms. You’ll be a key contributor to a pipeline and tooling that makes that path fast, reliable, and effortless for ML engineers across the AV organization to compile their models.
You will work on an evolving a state-of-the-art model export and compilation pipeline—from capturing high‑level model graphs, through intermediate representations and compiler transforms, into accelerator‑specific inference engines and their integration with our runtime— so that we can simultaneously optimize compilation throughput, model fidelity, and on‑vehicle latency. WE ARE LOOKING FOR THE BEST




ABOUT US

42dot is a mobility AI company committed to solving mobility challenges with software and AI. As the Global Software Center of Hyundai Motor Group, 42dot pioneers the future of mobility by advancing the development of software-defined vehicles. 

We develop safety-first, user-centric software-defined vehicle technologies that deliver the latest performance through continuous updates like smartphones. By advancing software and AI technology, 42dot envisions a world where everything is connected and moves autonomously through a self-managing urban transportation operating system.




As a Staff VLA Engineer you'll contribute to next-generation autonomous driving intelligence research, working alongside the team to push past current VLA capabilities. You'll bring hands-on expertise in foundation models, multimodal learning, world models, or autonomous systems, and help turn research ideas into real technical progress.

Responsibilities

Contribute to Next-Generation VLA Architectures

 - Research and prototype next-generation Vision-Language-Action architectures.

 - Explore scalable multimodal foundation models for autonomous driving.

 - Help develop architectures with improved generalization, reasoning, and long-horizon decision making.

 - Support work on large driving models that unify perception, planning, and action generation.

Support World Model & Driving Reasoning Research

 - Build and experiment with world-model-based approaches for predictive driving intelligence.

 - Work on future-state prediction, behavior forecasting, and counterfactual simulation.

 - Contribute to long-horizon planning and reasoning research for autonomous driving.

 - Help build models that understand complex traffic interactions and latent agent intentions.

Explore Agentic Driving Systems

 - Research goal-driven autonomous driving agents.

 - Help develop architectures that integrate reasoning, planning, memory, and action.

 - Investigate driving agents capable of adaptive decision making in open-world environments.

 - Contribute ideas toward future driving-agent architectures as successors to current VLA systems.



Qualifications

 - MS or PhD in Computer Science, Robotics, Machine Learning, Electrical Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience).

 - Strong hands-on experience with deep learning frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, JAX).

 - Solid understanding of foundation models, multimodal learning, or transformer-based architectures.

 - Experience training or fine-tuning large-scale models (vision, language, or multimodal).

 - Strong software engineering skills and experience working with large-scale data pipelines.

 - Ability to read, implement, and extend ideas from recent AI research papers.

 - Excellent collaboration and communication skills, comfortable working across distributed, cross-functional, and cross-cultural teams (Silicon Valley + HQ Korea).



Preferred Qualifications

 - Research experience in autonomous driving, robotics, or embodied AI (e.g., perception, planning, control, or end-to-end driving models).

 - Experience with world models, model-based reinforcement learning, or predictive/generative simulation.

 - Familiarity with Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models or agentic AI architectures (reasoning, planning, memory, tool use).

 - Publications at top-tier AI/ML/robotics venues (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CVPR, CoRL, RSS).

 - Experience with large-scale distributed training and model optimization.

 - Prior experience contributing research to production systems or bringing prototypes to deployment.

 - Familiarity with simulation environments for autonomous driving (e.g., CARLA, nuPlan, Waymo Open Dataset).
   
   

Interview Process

 - Application Review - Coding Test - 1st interview - 2nd interview - Offer Negotiation - Hiring

 - The screening procedures may vary depending on the position, schedule, or other circumstances.
   
   You will be individually notified of the screening schedule and results via the email address provided in your application.

 - $189,000 to $311,220

Applied Intuition, Inc. is powering the future of physical AI. Founded in 2017 and now valued at $15 billion, the Silicon Valley company is creating the digital infrastructure needed to bring intelligence to every moving machine on the planet. Applied Intuition services the automotive, defense, trucking, construction, mining and agriculture industries in three core areas: tools and infrastructure, operating systems, and autonomy. We're searching for a Manufacturing Technician to build Aurora's Hardware in accordance with Engineering Specifications. MFG Technicians have a wide range of duties and responsibilities, including but not limited to complete end-to-end vehicle integration, which involves the full up-fitting of a vehicle, whether it be a car or truck. This process is also referred to as vehicle kit or kitting. Additionally, technicians are responsible for the completion and assembly of sub-assemblies, which includes wiring harnesses, computer modules, and other mechanical assemblies.



In this Role, you will

Be responsible for assembling self-driving vehicles and their sub-assemblies. Your role will involve working within the Aurora Manufacturing Quality Management System (QMS). You will need to adhere to safety standards and meet internal deadlines while working with minimal oversight. 

Additionally, you will help aid in the creation of build documentation, attend training sessions through on-the-job mentorship, or a traditional classroom environment.  As a Hardware Technician on Aurora's Manufacturing Team, you will play a crucial role in bringing self-driving technology to life. Your primary responsibilities will center around the hands-on assembly of cutting-edge self-driving vehicles and their intricate sub-assemblies. This demanding yet rewarding position requires meticulous attention to detail and a commitment to precision.

A fundamental aspect of your work will involve operating strictly within the guidelines of the Aurora Manufacturing Quality Management System (QMS). Adherence to these established procedures is paramount to ensuring the highest standards of quality and reliability in all manufactured components and vehicles. You will be expected to consistently uphold rigorous safety standards, contributing to a secure and productive work environment for yourself and your colleagues. Furthermore, you will be tasked with meeting internal deadlines, often working independently with minimal oversight, demonstrating your ability to manage your time effectively and deliver results efficiently.

In addition to your core assembly duties, you will actively contribute to the ongoing improvement of our manufacturing processes. This includes assisting in the creation and refinement of detailed build documentation, which is essential for consistent and repeatable manufacturing. Your professional development will be a priority, and you will participate in various training sessions designed to enhance your skills and knowledge. These learning opportunities may take several forms, including on-the-job mentorship, where you gain practical experience and insights, or more traditional classroom environments, providing a deeper theoretical understanding of complex systems and manufacturing principles. This blend of practical application and formal instruction will ensure you are continually growing and adapting to the evolving landscape of autonomous vehicle technology.

Required Qualifications

 - We warmly welcome candidates with 2+ years of experience with a background in technical trade school or other educational equivalent. Familiarity with ISO-9001 or standardized process environments is preferred.

 - Candidates must demonstrate the capacity, resources, and motivation to build self-driving trucks with top-level integrations. They should be able to assemble wiring harnesses, read wiring schematics and layouts, and have experience with various software tools and standard documentation practices. Basic proficiency in both Windows and Mac operating systems is necessary.

 - Candidates must be able to work independently as well as collaboratively in a team environment. They should possess a customer-focused mindset regarding delivering quality and be willing to reason, isolate, and resolve issues.

 - Physical abilities are important, as candidates will need to handle, feel, and control objects, as well as grasp, move, and assemble small items. The role requires the ability to stand, walk, climb, carry materials, bend at the waist, reach, and kneel for extended periods. Candidates must be able to ascend and descend ladders, scaffolds, and stairs that are 20 to 25 feet high, with a maximum unassisted lift of 50 pounds and a typical lift of 20 pounds or less. They should also be able to pull or push wheeled equipment to build locations. Exposure to moving parts and tools such as impact tools, drills, and cutting equipment is expected, and wearing personal protective equipment (PPE) daily is mandatory.

Desired Qualifications

 - IPC training and certification, or equivalent experience
   
   - IPC J-STD-001, IPC-A-610, IPC/WHMA-A-620, IPC-7711/7721
   
   - GD&T (geometric dimensioning and tolerancing certification)

 - Production workshop experience

data.advertised_job_title: Lead Test Engineer AV Safety Assurance
data.job_description:
About the team
Avride builds autonomous driving technology for vehicles and delivery robots, and tests it on public roads in Austin. Before anything reaches those roads it goes through our QA team: checks on every pull request, a daily validation of main, and release-candidate qualification over a large set of recorded scenes. Every one of those gates produces a verdict, and the safety part of that verdict is the one people act on.
About the role
You will own
how safety is tested, judged and reported across our QA team.
Our Head of Safety owns the company's safety framework and the safety case built on top of it. You own the layer beneath: the gates, the criteria and the reports that turn day-to-day testing into evidence that argument can rest on.
The hard part of this is not the collisions. Those are obvious, and nobody argues about them. It is everything short of a collision  the near miss, the late brake, the hesitation at an intersection that looked wrong to one engineer and fine to another where the judgement has to be made and then made the same way again next week, by someone else, on a different run. Turning that into criteria a whole team applies consistently is the craft of this role.
You will lead through process and through people who do not report to you.
What you’ll do
Own the safety gates.
What counts as a safety-relevant finding, how it is classified and escalated, the criteria that hold a merge or a release, and how findings are tracked to closure  with the recurring ones feeding back into the criteria.
Own the acceptance criteria.
Decide what we measure at each gate from collisions and near misses to right-of-way and hard braking where the thresholds sit, and move them as the technology changes.
Own the safety report.
Define the format the whole QA team writes to: comparable between runs, explicit about what was not covered, and short enough to be read before a decision rather than after it.
Coach the QA team.
Run calibration sessions, review reports, and teach the reasoning behind the criteria, so that safety judgement is something the team applies on its own rather than something you add at review.
Be the safety voice in the release decision.
Releases are decided by a review that brings together engineering, safety and operations. Your part is the one nobody else can supply: what the testing actually showed and what is still unknown  put plainly enough that the decision is made with its eyes open.
Connect hazards to evidence.
Take hazard analysis output  STPA, FMEA, HAZOP  through to what our scenario set has to contain, through to results, through to something our safety case can stand on.
Work with the safety organization.
Translate the safety framework into testable requirements with our Head of Safety, and work with development and analytics on the tooling that makes those requirements measurable.
Keep up with the rules that apply to us.
Track the standards and regulation governing driverless operation in Texas and beyond, and bring what matters into how we test.
What you'll need
7+ years in testing, verification or validation,
including ownership of something that outlived your involvement — a gate, a review, a reporting standard.
Experience where being wrong had physical consequences.
Autonomous vehicles, aviation, medical devices, rail, industrial automation, defence — the field matters far less than the habits it builds: claims backed by evidence, limits stated rather than glossed over, and a clear head about what is still unknown.
Hazard-driven thinking.
You start from what can go wrong and work forward to what would have to be tested to know — and you can work with the output of a hazard analysis rather than needing it translated for you.
Comfort with residual risk.
You can say what we do not know and how much of it we are accepting, without overstating it and without smoothing it away.
Influence without authority.
Much of this job is persuading engineers and QA colleagues to change how they work because your argument is good, not because you can require it.
A habit of checking the number yourself.
When a safety metric looks wrong, you go to the data behind it rather than accepting the dashboard.
Fluent use of LLMs as a working tool
— reading through standards, logs and results quickly, and drafting the documents this role produces.
Excellent written English.
Other people's decisions rest on your documents.
Nice to have
Working knowledge of the standards that govern this work
— ISO 21448 (SOTIF), ISO/TS 5083, UL 4600, ISO 26262, ISO 34501–34505 — or their equivalents from your own field, such as DO-178C, IEC 62304 and ISO 14971, EN 50716, or IEC 61508. Whoever takes this role will become fluent in the AV-specific ones; we do not expect you to arrive that way.
Autonomous vehicles, ADAS, or another domain that operates without a human fallback.
Direct contribution to a safety case, a Voluntary Safety Self-Assessment, or a regulatory submission.
Experience defining on-road testing safety protocols and safety-driver procedures.
Experience hiring engineers.
Hands-on SQL and Python for digging into results yourself.

Company Introduction
At Bot Auto, we are revolutionizing the transportation of goods with our cutting-edge autonomous trucks, enhancing the quality of life for communities around the globe. With the agility of a start-up and the wisdom of seasoned experts, Bot Auto boasts a team that has achieved numerous world-firsts and unparalleled innovations. United by a shared vision, we create miracles and propel the future of transportation. Join us and transform your dreams into reality.
About the Role
Bot Auto is seeking a
Senior Functional Safety Engineer
to help define, analyze, validate, and continuously improve the safety of our autonomous trucking platform. In this role, you will work across autonomy, vehicle platform, hardware, software, operations, validation, and fleet teams to ensure our autonomous driving system is designed, tested, and operated with rigorous safety principles.  This role will focus heavily on the functional safety and redundancy designs of our next generation platform working with our hardware and infrastructure software systems team.
You will own and contribute to hazard analysis, safety requirements, safety case development, operational risk assessments, verification and validation evidence, and launch readiness reviews for Level 4 autonomous trucking operations. This is a high-impact role for an engineer who can bridge deep technical analysis with practical deployment needs in real-world freight operations.
What You’ll Do
Lead system safety analysis for Bot Auto’s autonomous trucking platform, including autonomy software, vehicle controls, perception, planning, prediction, localization, compute, sensors, communications, fallback behavior, and operational processes
Develop and maintain safety artifacts such as hazard analyses, functional safety concepts, technical safety requirements, safety cases, risk assessments, fault trees, FMEAs, STPA analyses, ODD assessments, and validation evidence
Translate hazards and operational risks into clear, testable safety requirements for engineering, validation, operations, and fleet teams
Partner internally with autonomy, software, hardware, vehicle integration, infrastructure, security, operations, and test teams to ensure safety requirements are implemented and verified
Implement the Functional Safety Manager type of role for our autonomous vehicle platform working externally with suppliers, the distributed safety development/DIA, and tracking of functional safety case work products across tiered suppliers and integrators
Support definition and refinement of the Operational Design Domain, including operating routes, environmental constraints, traffic conditions, vehicle behavior boundaries, fallback strategies, and minimum-risk maneuvers
Evaluate safety impacts of new autonomy features, software releases, hardware changes, sensor configurations, operational procedures, and route expansions
Drive safety reviews for on-road testing, driverless readiness, commercial operations, incident response, and post-event analysis
Analyze logs, simulations, test results, disengagements, safety-driver interventions, fleet events, and edge cases to identify safety trends and improvement opportunities
Define verification and validation strategies for safety-critical requirements across simulation, closed-course testing, structured road testing, shadow mode, and operational deployment
Work with cross-functional teams to ensure traceability from hazards to requirements, implementation, test coverage, and safety-case evidence
Contribute to safety governance, launch readiness criteria, change management, release approval processes, and operational safety metrics
Support regulatory, customer, partner, insurer, and internal safety reviews as needed
Promote a strong safety culture while enabling fast, disciplined engineering execution
What We’re Looking For
Bachelor’s degree in Systems Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Robotics, Computer Science, Aerospace Engineering, Automotive Engineering, or a related technical field
7+ years of experience in systems safety, functional safety, autonomous vehicles, robotics, aerospace, automotive, heavy vehicles, safety-critical software, or complex cyber-physical systems
Strong experience performing safety analyses such as HARA, FMEA, FTA, STPA, failure mode analysis, requirements decomposition, and risk assessment
Experience developing or contributing to safety cases for safety-critical systems
Strong understanding of autonomous vehicle system architecture, including perception, prediction, planning, control, localization, mapping, vehicle actuation, compute, sensing, and fleet operations
Understanding of highly redundant, fault tolerant architectures and fail operational ADS and vehicle health management
Familiarity with safety standards and frameworks such as ISO 26262, ISO 21448/SOTIF, UL 4600 Safety Case, SAE J3016/J3018, MIL-STD-882, IEC 61508, or similar safety-critical system standards

Familiarity with emerging standards and best practices for road vehicles using physical AI and driven by ADS, such as AVSC Best Practices, SAE standards, and ISO PAS 8800
Ability to convert ambiguous technical and operational risks into structured engineering requirements and actionable mitigations, arrive as a leader in your field ready to drive our AV safety readiness
Experience working with verification and validation teams to define evidence needed to support safety claims
Strong technical communication skills, including the ability to present risk decisions, tradeoffs, and safety arguments to engineering leaders and cross-functional stakeholders
Comfort working in a fast-moving startup environment where safety rigor, execution speed, and practical deployment constraints must be balanced

Experience with autonomous trucks, commercial vehicles, robotics, AV operations, fleet operations, or on-road testing
Experience with ISO26262 or similar safety audit and assessment process
Experience supporting driverless launch readiness, route readiness, ODD expansion, or commercial autonomous vehicle deployment

Safety-case evidence supports operational readiness decisions for new features, routes, and deployment milestones
Cross-functional teams understand key hazards, mitigations, fallback expectations, and validation requirements
Safety risks are identified early, communicated clearly, and resolved through practical engineering and operational controls
AV vehicle architectures and risk assessment organized per ISO26262 and relevant safety standards with strong leadership across safety critical suppliers and delivered components and safety analyses
Who You Are
You are a systems thinker who can understand the full autonomous trucking stack—from sensors and autonomy software to vehicle actuation, operations, and real-world deployment. You are rigorous but pragmatic, comfortable challenging assumptions, and able to partner with fast-moving engineering teams without becoming a bottleneck. You care deeply about safety, but you also understand that safety engineering must produce actionable decisions, not just documentation. You can explain–even teach–complex topics in autonomy safety with clarity and to build support across multiple stakeholders and partners.

Gatik's Class 3-7 autonomous trucks are commercially deployed across major markets, including Texas, Arkansas, and Ontario, Canada, driving innovation in freight transportation.

Partner closely with Autonomy Software, Middleware, Infrastructure, and Systems teams to embed functional safety into daily agile development processes.

Deep expertise in ISO 26262, UL 4600, and ISO 21448.

Experience defining architecture for deterministic, real-time autonomous systems.

data.job_description:
Who We Are
Nuro believes self-driving vehicles are the most immediate and profound opportunity for AI to drive positive change in the physical world. Safer streets, more time for what matters, and easier access to the world around us, that’s why we’re building a universal autonomy platform: self-driving for all roads and all rides.
Founded in 2016, Nuro is a physical AI company developing Level 4 autonomous driving technology for a wide range of vehicles, use cases, and markets. Powered by the Nuro Driver™, our universal autonomy platform enables the global mobility ecosystem to deploy autonomy at scale, from robotaxis and logistics fleets to personal vehicles.
With years of real-world deployment experience and a flexible, partner-led business model, Nuro is working toward a future where millions of autonomous vehicles powered by our technology help make everyday life safer, easier, and more connected.
Nuro has raised over $2B in capital from Uber, NVIDIA, Google, Softbank, Fidelity, T. Rowe Price, and other leading investors.
About the Team
The Perception ML Operations team sits at the center of how Nuro's vehicles learn to see. We are responsible for the training and evaluation data that powers perception models across every sensor modality: vision, lidar, radar, and beyond. We work alongside ML engineers, product owners, data engineers, and external labeling partners to turn ambiguous, fast-moving requirements into data deliverables the Perception team can build on with confidence.
This is a team that operates at the intersection of ML urgency and operational discipline. Here is what the work actually looks like day-to-day:
Sitting in a roadmap review, hearing a new feature requirement land, and walking out with a concrete data collection and labeling plan already scoped against timeline and budget.
Reviewing vendor throughput against milestone dates and catching a capacity gap before it would become a release risk.
Querying pipeline data directly to understand where quality is slipping, rather than waiting for a ticket or ML engineer to surface the problem.
Being the person Perception Engineering calls when they need to know whether a data deliverable is real, on time, and within budget, and making sure the team you manage translates that bar into terms vendors can execute against without ambiguity.
If that sounds like the kind of ownership that energizes you, we would love to talk.
About the Role
This is a role built for someone who wants to own outcomes, not just track them. You will translate company-wide perception feature requirements into concrete data deliverables, manage vendor allocation and budget against Nuro's milestone and release timelines, and keep a clear, defensible view of outcomes, risk, and data quality across the pipelines you own — distinguishing a one-off labeling error from a systemic labeling process problem, and closing the gap either way.
The work connects directly to Nuro's mission. Perception models are only as good as the data behind them, and every gap in coverage, every misallocated vendor hour, and every quality blind spot eventually shows up in how the vehicle sees the world. You are the person who catches that upstream, before it becomes an engineering fire drill or a safety question.
You'll partner closely with ML engineering leadership, product owners, and vendor operations, with the access and visibility to make real calls on scope, budget, and quality tradeoffs. What we ask in return is rigor, clear communication, and genuine ownership of the outcome.
About the Work
Translate Requirements into Deliverables
Synthesize company-wide perception feature needs into detailed, actionable data deliverables covering vision, LiDAR, and additional sensor modalities.
Own the end-to-end labeling process, from data availability through an outcome Perception can train on, directing data annotation partners to execute against that bar.
Own Vendor Allocation and Budget
Manage vendor allocation and budgeting in direct alignment with Nuro's milestone and release timelines.
Oversee large-scale vendor and managed service provider relationships against quality, latency, and volume targets, and hold them accountable when performance drifts.
Track Outcomes, Risk, and Quality
Define and maintain clear, current tracking of outcomes, risk, and data quality so that status is never a surprise to engineering or leadership.
Own quality as an outcome, not just a status: define what "good" looks like for deliverables within your pipelines, and hold vendors to that bar before problems surface downstream.
In response to quality dips, identify whether the issue is an isolated labeling error or a broader process failure, and address the root cause rather than just the single error.
Translate high-level product roadmaps and engineering requirements into granular operational execution plans, with resource allocation and throughput modeled explicitly.
Query databases directly using SQL (Python a plus) to analyze throughput and quality metrics and generate reporting without waiting on engineering support.
About You
We are not looking for someone who has done everything. We are looking for someone who thinks in systems, owns outcomes rather than status updates, and has genuine command of both the operational and technical sides of perception data.
What You Bring
5+ years of experience in Technical Program Management or Operations Strategy, managing complex, cross-functional programs within technology, autonomous driving, or AI/ML.
Demonstrated ability to translate high-level product roadmaps and engineering requirements into granular operational execution plans, including managing resource allocation and throughput for large-scale workflows.
Experience overseeing large-scale vendor operations or managed service providers, specifically against quality, latency, and volume targets.
Proficiency with SQL to query databases, analyze throughput metrics, and generate reports independently.
A track record of holding vendors accountable to a quality bar you've defined yourself, not just monitoring metrics someone else set.
Bonus Points
Background in autonomous vehicles, robotics, computer vision, or ML model training.
Prior experience in ML engineering, data engineering, or technical consulting.
Demonstrated track record of improving data quality or throughput at scale, with metrics to show for it.
Familiarity with autonomous vehicle sensor modalities (LiDAR, Radar, Camera, Thermal) and their respective data annotation requirements.
Bachelor's degree in a technical or business discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

For this position, the reasonably expected base pay range is between $132,000 and $198,000 for the level at which this job has been scoped. data.job_description:
About Zoox
Zoox is an autonomous ridehailing company building the world's first purpose-built robotaxi — fully electric, bidirectional, with no steering wheel or driver's seat. Backed by Amazon and founded to make transportation safer, cleaner, and more accessible, Zoox designs its vehicles entirely around the rider. We're currently operating in Las Vegas and San Francisco, with Austin and Miami on the horizon, and testing underway across seven U.S. markets.
About Our Part-Time Student Worker Program
Zoox's part-time student worker program puts you at the center of one of the most ambitious challenges in transportation. You'll contribute to real projects, work alongside engineers and researchers pushing the boundaries of autonomous technology, and gain experience that goes well beyond the classroom. We're looking for students who bring strong academic foundations, curiosity that doesn't stop at coursework, and a drive to be part of something that matters.

Role Overview
This role focuses on building a data-driven safety risk model that quantifies and improves autonomous-vehicle driving performance, along with the data analysis work that supports it. The student will work within the Safety Strategy & Operations team on a 6-month project spanning model development, empirical experimentation, and large-scale driving/simulation data analysis.

Responsibilities
Support designing, building, and iterating on a data-driven safety risk model that quantifies driving performance and surfaces safety-relevant signals across the autonomy stack
Assist developing and maintaining dataset management pipelines — curation, labeling, versioning, and quality checks — that feed the risk model and downstream analyses
Support defining and running empirical experiments that “show it with data” rather than relying on assumptions

Required Qualifications
Assist analyzing large-scale driving and simulation datasets to identify trends, edge cases, and opportunities to improve autonomy performance
Currently pursuing a B.S. or M.S. in a relevant quantitative field (Engineering, Computer Science, Statistics, Physics, or similar)
Strong programming skills in Python
Help work through ambiguous, open-ended problems with a researcher’s mindset and a bias toward rapid iteration
Solid data manipulation understanding (e.g., SQL, PySpark, Scala)
Solid foundation in statistics, machine learning, and risk or reliability modeling
Help communicate complex results, trade-offs, and uncertainty clearly to the team and stakeholders
Comfort operating independently under high uncertainty on open-ended problems

Bonus Qualifications
Excellent written and verbal communication; able to convey complexity and ambiguity clearly
Experience with safety, reliability, or risk modeling (e.g., survival analysis, Bayesian methods, causal inference)
Experience with large-scale dataset management, data pipelines, or MLOps tooling
Strong teamwork and collaboration skills
Background in autonomous vehicles, robotics, or a related quantitative discipline
Prior research experience taking ambiguous, end-to-end problems from zero to a result, independently

Program Requirements
Genuine interest in autonomous vehicles and Zoox’s mission
Currently enrolled in a B.S. or M.S. program in a relevant discipline.
Available to commit to a minimum three-month assignment.
Able to commit a minimum of 20 hours per week.
Able to work on-site at one of our office locations.
Must adhere with Zoox confidentiality requirements, including refraining from using or sharing proprietary company information outside of Zoox, such as in academic research, theses, publications, or presentations.

data.job_description:
The Prediction & Behavior ML team is responsible for developing machine learning (ML) algorithms that learn and predict behaviors from data, applying them both on-vehicle to influence driving behavior and off-vehicle to provide ML capabilities to simulation and validation. Given the tight integration of behavior forecasting and motion planning, our team collaborates closely with the Planner team to advance overall vehicle behavior. We also work closely with our Perception, Simulation, and Systems Engineering teams to accelerate our ability to validate our driving performance.
 
As a Learned Trajectory Machine Learning Engineer you will be responsible for developing deep learned models that produce trajectories for our vehicles to drive. Given the tight integration of behavior prediction and motion planning, you will closely collaborate with the Planner and Perception teams in the advancement of our overall vehicle behavior.

In this role, you will:
You will develop new deep learning models that use imitation learning and reinforcement learning to generate driving plans for our autonomous vehicle. You will also work on techniques to estimate the quality of those driving plans along the dimensions of safety, progress, comfort etc.
You will leverage our large-scale machine learning infrastructure to discover new solutions and push the boundaries of the field
You will develop metrics and tools to analyze errors and understand improvements of our systems

During your thesis, you delve into physics-based models of electric drives and our Python component library while simultaneously reviewing current literature on robust system identification and the design of experiments.

You comprehensively evaluate the approach you have developed using a practical benchmark use case.

Job Description
The
Engineering Trainer - Commercial HVAC Applications
will be a key member of the Bosch Home Comfort Factory Training team, reporting directly to the Sales Technology and Training Innovation Lead. This role is central to our mission of driving the specification of Bosch technologies by empowering the engineering and design community. The position champions a design-focused training philosophy, educating specifying engineers, design-build contractors, and bid-spec representatives on the superior application and performance of our commercial HVAC portfolio.
As a technical authority, the Application Trainer is pivotal in supporting the market integration of our newly expanded commercial product lines. The role involves creating and delivering sophisticated, application-focused training that positions Bosch, FHP, and Hitachi systems as the preferred solution in competitive bids and project specifications. The ideal candidate has deep expertise in the system design, application, and specification of light commercial rooftops, commercial Water Source Heat Pump (WSHP) systems, and 3-phase Variable Refrigerant Flow (VRF) systems. This mid-level salaried position involves up to 30% travel across the United States and Canada and requires a blend of engineering acumen, polished presentation skills, and a passion for influencing the future of building design.
Key Responsibilities
Develop and deliver high-level technical presentations, seminars, and workshops for engineering firms, specifying engineers, and other design professionals.
Create and maintain a library of technical sales and design tools, including application guides, system selection software tutorials, BIM object libraries, and master specification documents.
Translate complex product features into compelling performance and application benefits relevant to the design and specification process.
Deliver specialized training on our expanded portfolio, including our light commercial RTUs, Hitachi VRF, and Bosch WSHP systems, as well as key industry trends like electrification, decarbonization, and the transition to low-GWP refrigerants.
Serve as a go-to technical authority for the application and design of Bosch's commercial HVAC systems, providing expert guidance to internal teams and external partners.
Provide direct support to the specification community, assisting with system design, energy modeling, and the development of project-specific specifications that favor Bosch solutions.
Collaborate closely with Product Management, Engineering, and Quality teams to stay current on new products, system updates, and evolving building codes and energy standards (e.g., ASHRAE 90.1).
Act as a key technical partner to our manufacturer's representatives and distribution partners, equipping them with the knowledge to effectively call on and support engineering firms.
Develop content for and participate in industry events, trade shows, and professional organizations (e.g., ASHRAE, AIA) to promote Bosch's technical leadership.
Gather and analyze feedback from the engineering community to inform product development, competitive positioning, and future training strategies.

Qualifications
Minimum of 3-5 years of relevant experience in the HVAC industry, with a strong background in commercial system design and application.
Demonstrated experience working with or for engineering firms, with a deep understanding of the bid-spec process.
Expertise in the system design and specification of some or all of the following systems:
Light commercial rooftop units.
Commercial Water Source Heat Pump (WSHP) systems, including geothermal and cooling tower/boiler applications.
3-phase Variable Refrigerant Flow (VRF) systems, including heat recovery models.
