Job Description
Job description
Bosch Corporate Research is seeking a Research Engineer to conduct applied research in computational materials science at the atomistic level and contribute to the development of next-generation Bosch products. The Research Engineer will be expected to utilize the full suite of tools available for atomistic simulation, from conventional classical and electronic structure calculations to emerging AI techniques, to rapidly move from conceptualization to qualitative screening to quantitative modeling, in pace with engineering development cycles and experimental campaigns.
As connection to physical product development is paramount in this role, the successful candidate will be able and interested in engaging with experimental efforts, both in conventional and self-driving lab contexts, and expanding broad professional networks both within Bosch and externally with industry partners, national labs and academia.
Your responsibilities
Conduct applied research in materials science rooted in rigorous physical and chemical principles, focusing on simulations at the atomistic level
Apply both conventional atomistic methods and emerging AI tools to derive actionable insights on materials behavior, selection, and optimization, supported by appropriate model validation
Identify, connect, and work with external collaborators
Communicate research results through internal presentations, technical reports, peer-reviewed publications, conference presentations, and intellectual-property disclosures.
Contribute to a collaborative, interdisciplinary research environment spanning materials science, physics, chemistry, AI, simulation, software, and experimental automation.
Create a scientifically rigorous AI-based framework that empowers ordinary Bosch engineers to confidently apply atomistic simulation to complex, industrially relevant materials with high quality and impact.

Qualifications
Required
PhD in materials science, chemistry, physics, chemical engineering, mechanical engineering, biophysics or a closely related field.
Demonstrated experience in atomistic simulation and computational materials science, including hands-on application in one or more of the following areas: density functional theory, molecular dynamics, Monte Carlo simulation, phase-field modeling, multiscale modeling, as well as high-performance computing environments.
Proficiency in programming and software engineering, with demonstrated experience in the scientific Python ecosystem or equivalent computational tools.
Documented experience applying AI/machine learning techniques to scientific problems, such as active learning, Bayesian optimization, reinforcement learning, automated workflows, or autonomous lab systems.
Demonstrated ability to conduct independent research, including formulating research questions, analyzing complex data, and developing working prototypes or proof-of-concept solutions.
Evidence of research impact through peer-reviewed publications, patents, open-source software contributions, or equivalent professional accomplishments.
Demonstrated written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate technical concepts across technical disciplines and organizational levels.
Preferred
Experience with the validation and integration of atomistic simulation results with experimental data, including the use of scale-bridging techniques, identification of appropriate experimental methods, and interaction with experimental teams
Broad scientific network to identify collaboration opportunities with state-of-the-art methods and top researchers in academia, national laboratories, and industry
Experience working with industry-academic partnerships or multidisciplinary research consortia.

Additional Information
The annual U.S. base salary range for this position is $140,000-$160,000. Within the range, individual pay is determined based on several factors, including, but not limited to, type of degree, work experience and job knowledge, complexity of the role, type of position, job location, etc. Your Hiring Manager can share more details about the specific salary range for this position during the interview process.*
All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

Customer Service Representative
(Full-Time) plays a significant role at Roadside Protect, Bosch Service Solutions. You will be helping customers solve various roadside problems, which could considerably impact their personal or professional lives. Therefore, your ability to empathize and display social skills will be critical to building rapport with customers and getting the information you need to help them.
Since Roadside Protect was founded in 2002, RP has managed more than 2,000,000 dispatches. Our key mission is to deliver a better service when it matters the most - the critical minutes when people are stranded on the road and in need of help.
Responsibilities:
Answer inbound calls and provide professional, empathetic customer support
Accurately gather required information and enter data into dispatch systems, or perform fleet intake, gather vehicle, driver and indicant information accurately.
Follow scripts, workflows, and client specific requirements
Communicate clearly with customers or drivers regarding next steps, expectations and processes
Escalate issues according to policy when necessary
Maintain confidentiality of customer and company information
Contribute to a positive team environment and uphold service standards
Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required.  Duties, activities, and responsibilities may change at any time with or without notice to meet the needs of the business.

Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Friday, and Sunday

High School Diploma or GED required
High level of attention to detail and problem-solving skills

Reliable, strong attendance and professionalism

Ability to speak and communicate clearly with callers and team members for extended periods

Want to be part of transforming road freight? Einride is showing the world a new way to move, based on the latest digital, autonomous and electric technologies. We build the technology that hauls freight efficiently, and we put it to work for the world's leading manufacturers, retailers, logistics providers and defense organizations, all working toward a future where moving goods cost less for our customers, and less for the planet.
Founded in 2016, Einride became the first company in the world to deploy a cab-less autonomous electric vehicle on a public road (Sweden, 2019). In 2022, we were the first to successfully operate such a vehicle on a U.S. public road. In June 2026, Einride became a publicly listed company on Nasdaq, a milestone that reflects a decade of turning what once looked like science fiction into everyday reality. Today, our technology moves freight across North America, Europe, and the Middle East for some of the world's biggest shippers.
Einride Logistics Inc. is a transportation company operating as a federally regulated motor carrier across multiple states, running a mixed fleet of conventional diesel and battery-electric commercial vehicles. We are hiring our first dedicated Environmental Health & Safety leader to own the safety and regulatory compliance program end to end.
This is a builder's role, not a caretaker's. You will own DOT/FMCSA compliance, driver and fleet safety, and environmental compliance for the entire operation — writing the policies, standing up the systems, training the people, and answering for the numbers. You will be the company's subject-matter authority in front of regulators, auditors, insurers, and customers, and a visible safety partner to drivers and terminal teams in the field.
You will:
DOT & FMCSA Regulatory Compliance
Own the DOT compliance program
across all operating authorities and states, ensuring adherence to 49 CFR Parts 380–399 and maintaining audit-ready records at all times.
Manage driver qualification vendor and supplier
end to end — MVRs, medical certificates, road tests, employment verifications, and annual reviews of driving records — including the annual MVR review required under Part 391.
Administer Hours of Service compliance
, including ELD program management, log auditing, exception review, and coaching on false-log and form-and-manner violations.
Run the DOT drug and alcohol testing program supplier / vendor
under 49 CFR Part 40 and Part 382: pre-employment, random, post-accident, reasonable suspicion, and return-to-duty testing; serve as the company's Designated Employer Representative (DER).
Manage FMCSA Drug & Alcohol Clearinghouse obligations
, including full pre-employment queries, annual limited queries for every driver, and timely reporting of violations and return-to-duty information.
Monitor and improve CSA/SMS performance
across all compliance categories — Unsafe Driving, Crash Indicator, Hours of Service, Vehicle Maintenance, Vehicle Maintenance (Driver-Observed), Driver Fitness, and HM — using roadside inspection data to target intervention before FMCSA does.
Oversee vehicle compliance records
, including annual inspections, DVIRs, preventive maintenance documentation, and out-of-service violation follow-up in partnership with Fleet Maintenance.
Fleet Safety & Driver Training
Design and run the driver safety program
, from new-hire onboarding and entry-level driver training (ELDT) through ongoing professional development.
Own the telematics and camera program
— set event thresholds, review footage, and build a coaching workflow that changes behavior rather than simply generating reports.
Chair the accident review committee
, determining preventability, identifying root causes, and driving corrective action to closure.
Lead incident investigation and response
for collisions, injuries, and near misses, including post-accident testing decisions, scene documentation, and DOT-recordable determination.
Develop targeted countermeasures
for the company's highest-frequency and highest-severity loss types, and measure whether they actually work.
Partner with Recruiting and Operations
on driver hiring standards, ride-alongs, probationary reviews, and progressive discipline where safety performance falls short.
Manage workers' compensation and liability claims
in coordination with insurers and legal, including return-to-work coordination and reserve management.
Program Leadership & Safety Culture
Write and maintain the safety management system
— policies, SOPs, the driver handbook, and the corrective action process — and keep them current as regulations and operations change.
Build safety reporting and dashboards
that give leadership a clear view of leading and lagging indicators, not just an accident count after the fact.
Deliver training in the field
, not just from a desk — terminal walkthroughs, toolbox talks, driver meetings, and hands-on coaching.
Establish a near-miss and hazard reporting channel
that drivers and technicians actually trust and use.
Advise executive leadership on safety risk
, including the risk implications of new lanes, customers, sites, and equipment before commitments are made.
Scale the function
— define the structure, tools, and headcount the EH&S program will need as the network grows, and build the team.
We expect you to:
Bachelor's degree in occupational safety, environmental science, transportation, logistics, or a related field — or equivalent professional experience.
7+ years of progressive EH&S or safety and compliance experience, with at least 3 years in trucking, fleet, or another DOT-regulated transportation environment.
Demonstrated working knowledge of the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations (49 CFR Parts 40, 382, 383, 387, 390–399) applied in a live operation, not solely in theory.
Direct experience managing CSA/SMS performance and the DataQs process.
Hands-on experience with ELD and telematics platforms and driver coaching programs (e.g., Samsara, Motive, Lytx, Netradyne, or Geotab).
Experience leading incident investigations and root cause analysis through to corrective action.
Working knowledge of OSHA general industry standards (29 CFR 1910) and recordkeeping requirements.
Ability to travel to operating sites, including occasional short-notice travel following a significant incident.
Valid driver's license and an acceptable motor vehicle record.
Preferred Qualifications
Preferred experience with battery-electric commercial vehicles, high-voltage systems, or EV charging infrastructure.
Multi-state environmental compliance experience, including hazardous waste generator obligations.
Experience supporting autonomous, automated, or other emerging vehicle technology programs.
Class A CDL, or substantial experience working directly with CDL drivers.
Experience building an EH&S function from the ground up in a growing organization.
Working knowledge of hazmat requirements under 49 CFR Parts 171–180 (if the operation adds hazmat freight).
This is a full-time position based in the US, ideally in; Dallas, Houston, New Jersey, or Los Angeles. We recommend that you submit your application as soon as possible since selection and interviews are held continually.
Please note that as part of our standard recruitment process, we conduct a background control on the final candidate for this role. This may include verification of education, employment history, any relevant professional certifications or other information that may be of our interest.

The role
As a software engineer in Wayve’s Core Simulation team, you will help develop the simulation system used to evaluate and improve Wayve’s driving intelligence.
Wayve’s end-to-end driving stack creates unique simulation challenges. Rather than testing independently specified modules, we need to reproduce the behaviour of a learned driving system across a complex combination of sensor data, model inference, routing, control and vehicle dynamics. Our simulator must be realistic enough to provide meaningful signal, reproducible enough for teams to trust the results, and descriptive enough to understand differences between simulated and on-road behaviour.
Our open-loop and closed-loop simulation workflows share a common codebase, with different components executed and configured depending on the use case. You will initially work with the team focused on high-scale open-loop evaluation, while contributing to shared components and infrastructure used across the broader simulation system.
This is a hands-on software engineering role working across C++ and Python. Develop and maintain production-quality components within Wayve’s simulation system using modern C++ and Python.
Integrate driving-stack components, simulated robot systems and new vehicle-platform capabilities into the shared simulation environment.
Support different simulation configurations and ensure components interact correctly across applicable workflows.
Investigate differences between on-road and simulated execution, identifying issues across data, inference and simulated components.
Improve simulation reproducibility, reliability and debuggability through automated testing, observability and better developer tooling.
Profile and improve simulator performance, helping us run increasingly large evaluation workloads efficiently.
Work with internal users and adjacent engineering teams to clarify requirements, resolve integration issues and deliver scoped improvements.
Contribute to technical designs and help evolve the quality and maintainability of the simulation codebase.

Professional experience developing, delivering and maintaining production software in a collaborative engineering environment.
Strong software development skills in C++ and Python, with depth in at least one and the ability to work effectively in both.

Experience debugging complex systems and reasoning about interfaces, data flows, timing and failure modes.

Strong communication and collaboration skills.

Wayve is seeking a
Staff Robotics Engineer, 3D Sensing
to lead the technical development of our LiDAR and cross-sensor 3D sensing capabilities. You will own the systems used to calibrate, synchronise and align LiDARs with cameras and other vehicle sensors, enabling accurate and reliable 3D data for perception, reconstruction and ground-truth generation.
This is a senior individual-contributor role with responsibility for shaping the architecture and technical roadmap for 3D sensing, while remaining deeply involved in algorithm development, implementation, evaluation and deployment. You will solve challenging problems arising from real sensor systems—including imperfect time synchronisation, rolling-shutter cameras and LiDAR sweep patterns—and develop robust methods that operate across diverse vehicles, environments and operating conditions. You will collaborate broadly across Wayve and provide technical leadership and mentorship across the 3D sensing stack.

Define and evolve the technical architecture and roadmap for Wayve’s LiDAR and cross-sensor 3D sensing capabilities, aligned with product and vehicle-programme requirements.
Lead the development of target-based and targetless LiDAR calibration and registration methods, including LiDAR-to-camera alignment using geometric and learned approaches.
Develop robust temporal alignment and motion compensation methods using techniques such as LiDAR odometry, nonlinear least-squares optimisation and factor graphs.
Establish evaluation methodologies and productionise reliable, scalable 3D sensing systems that operate across diverse vehicles, environments and sensor configurations.
Work with engineering and research teams to deliver end-to-end 3D sensing capabilities, while providing technical leadership and mentorship to other engineers.

Significant experience developing robotics or autonomous-driving systems involving LiDAR, cameras and 3D sensor data.
Strong experience with target-based or targetless sensor calibration and registration, including LiDAR-to-camera alignment.
Strong understanding of 3D geometry, state estimation and optimisation techniques, including nonlinear least-squares methods or factor graphs.
Experience accounting for sensor timing and motion effects, such as time synchronisation, LiDAR sweep distortion, rolling-shutter cameras and motion compensation.
Strong software-engineering skills in C++ and/or Python, with experience taking robotics algorithms from prototype through evaluation and production deployment.
Experience defining evaluation methodologies, datasets and metrics for assessing calibration, registration and 3D sensing quality across real-world conditions.
Demonstrated technical leadership, including setting technical direction, solving ambiguous cross-functional problems and mentoring other engineers.

Experience handling dynamic scenes using object detection, motion segmentation or tracking methods.
Practical experience with optimisation libraries such as GTSAM, Ceres Solver or g2o.

We are building a high-fidelity simulation platform for next-generation autonomous driving development, which requires establishing a vehicle dynamics model that can accurately reflect the driving characteristics of different vehicle models, providing a reliable foundation for training, testing, evaluation, and closed-loop simulation of autonomous driving algorithms. 
We are looking for engineers with backgrounds in vehicle dynamics, control, simulation modeling, or autonomous driving to be responsible for the design, development, parameter calibration, validation, and engineering implementation of vehicle dynamics models. 
This position centers on model mechanisms, engineering implementation, and real vehicle data calibration. Experience in data-driven modeling or Machine Learning will be a plus. 
Job responsibilities
1. Development of vehicle dynamics models
- Responsible for designing, developing, and continuously iterating vehicle dynamics models for autonomous driving simulations. 
- Establish models of the vehicle's longitudinal, lateral, vertical, and six-degree-of-freedom movement for the entire vehicle. 
- Establish vehicle kinematic models, dynamic models, and tire models, including center of mass movement, yaw, lateral deviation, and lateral and longitudinal tire forces. 
- Develop vehicle models with varying complexity levels according to different simulation needs, balancing accuracy, real-time, and stability reasonably. 
- Creating vehicle models suitable for different vehicle types, operating conditions, and road conditions. 
2. Modeling of key vehicle components and subsystems
- Models of key subsystems such as vehicle steering, braking, drive, motor, and transmission. 
- Establish tire models, including longitudinal/lateral forces, lateral deviation characteristics, combined slip, etc. 
- Establish necessary physical models for suspension, air resistance, rolling resistance, slope, etc. based on actual vehicle characteristics. 
- Research tire models, powertrain models, steering models of different complexities according to simulation requirements. 
3. Model parameter calibration and fit with real vehicle data
- Identification and calibration of vehicle dynamic model parameters based on real vehicle test data. 
- Analyzes vehicle data such as CAN, IMU, GPS, wheel speed, steering angle, acceleration, and yaw rate. 
- Design parameter identification, curve fitting, and optimization methods to estimate vehicle mass, center of mass position, moment of inertia, tire parameters, steering system parameters, and more. 
- Establish a complete workflow from real vehicle data → parameter identification → model calibration → simulation verification. 
- Continuously analyze differences between simulated vehicles and real vehicles, and optimize model accuracy. 
4. Closed-loop simulation of autonomous driving
- Integrates vehicle dynamics models into autonomous driving simulation systems to provide real vehicle responses for modules like Planning/Control. 
- Supports vehicle motion simulation under different driving control inputs, including Steering, Throttle, Brake, and more. 
- Verify the stability and robustness of autonomous driving control algorithms across different vehicle models. 
- Analyze the error between planned trajectory, control commands, and actual vehicle movement. 
- Supports real-time or accelerated simulation in large-scale autonomous driving scenarios. 
5. Model validation and evaluation
- Establish offline and closed-loop evaluation systems for vehicle dynamics models. 
- By comparing real vehicle test data with simulation data, the model's accuracy under different operating conditions is evaluated. 
- Covers typical conditions such as acceleration, braking, steering, lane changes, emergency obstacle avoidance, and low-adhesion road surfaces. 
- Studying the model's stability and physical rationality under extreme driving and extreme conditions. 
- Establish model reuse, parameterization, and automatic calibration capabilities across different vehicle models. 
6. Simulation system engineering
- Responsible for modular, parameterized, and engineering implementation of vehicle dynamics models. 
- Optimized model computational performance to meet requirements for real-time simulation and large-scale parallel simulation. 
- Collaborate with teams such as simulation engines, planning control, vehicle controllers, and scene generation. 
- Driving vehicle models to migrate from prototype environments such as Matlab / Simulink / CarSim to production-grade simulation systems.

1198_Senior Backend Engineer, Release Engineering & CI/CD (Pilot.Auto)
Job Overview
【Position Overview】
TIER IV is the creator of Autoware, the world's leading open-source software for autonomous driving, with the mission to democratize intelligent vehicles. We work with partners worldwide to deploy safe, scalable Level 4 (L4) autonomy across a range of vehicle platforms and real-world environments. 
Pilot.Auto is the autonomous driving software we build on top of Autoware and ship to real vehicles. Today, getting a release from a developer's branch onto a fleet involves many teams, many hand-offs, and too much manual work. We are looking for a senior backend engineer to own this problem end-to-end: define how Pilot.Auto is versioned, built, tested, and released, and build the CI/CD pipelines and internal tooling that make every release fast, repeatable, and traceable. This is a hands-on, high-ownership role for someone who has built platform and test infrastructure for production systems and knows how to bring process and engineering together across an organization. 
【Key Responsibilities】
Own the design and rollout of the internal release process for Pilot.Auto — branching and versioning strategy, release cadence, code-freeze and hotfix flows, release notes, and the go/no-go criteria for shipping to vehicles. 
Design, build, and operate the CI/CD pipelines that build, test, package, and publish the Pilot.Auto stack as versioned, reproducible artifacts for x86 and ARM-based in-vehicle ECUs. 
Build the backend services and internal tools behind the release process: artifact and image registries, release dashboards, automated release gating that pulls results from simulation, scenario-based evaluation, and driving-log regression pipelines. 
Raise the reliability of our test infrastructure — flaky-test detection and quarantine, test-time reduction, hermetic builds, and integration of hardware-in-the-loop and bench environments into the pipeline. 
Establish end-to-end traceability from requirement and code change through build, test evidence, and deployed release, in collaboration with the Safety and QA teams, so the release process supports our safety-case and change-management needs. 
Coordinate the release schedule and process across Perception, Planning, Control, Vehicle Integration, Field Operations, and Product; drive adoption of the new process through clear documentation, tooling, and enablement. 
Own the cost, performance, and security of our build and release infrastructure on AWS and GitHub, including runner fleets, caching, secrets, and access control. 
Mentor engineers on CI/CD and release best practices and propagate a culture of automation and observability across the AD engineering organization. 
【Position Overview】
As the creator of Autoware, the world's leading open-source autonomous driving software, Tier 4 is committed to the mission of "democratizing autonomous driving." - Responsible for cost-performance and security of build release platforms on AWS and GitHub (including runners, caches, secrets, and access controls). 
- Mentor engineers on CI/CD and release best practices, and instill a culture of automation and observability throughout the AD development organization.

[Background]
We are advancing the development of autonomous driving systems, and improving quality and ensuring quality are key factors for business expansion. 
The quality assurance regulatory framework supporting this contributes to improving quality across the entire company, and confirming the formulation and implementation of these regulations and rules is an immediate challenge. data.job_description:
About
The HIL Platform and Services team in the GM Autonomous Vehicle (AV) Organization is responsible to develop and scale high-fidelity and reliable Hardware-in-Loop validation platforms to test AV software prior to deployment, to ensure enterprise usability, end-user functionality, and provide high quality, use case driven signals, such as AV Performance Validation and AV System Reliability.
Role
As a Software Engineer on the HIL Platform and Services Team, you get to be at the intersection of AV software and AI models, and the hardware systems that are responsible for vehicle autonomy! You will have an opportunity to work on what it takes to run, deploy, and test on the next generation of GM AVs.
This is a highly collaborative team with close collaboration with various teams within the core AV organization including Embodied AI, Model Deployment, Middleware, OS, Sensor Applications, and Vehicle Integration. This role blends expertise in Software development, software optimization, managing and deploying HIL Services as a PaaS, and hardware-aware engineering.
What you’ll be doing (Responsibilities)
Develop software to increase the capabilities, fidelity, observability and scale of our HIL Platform and Integration services
Deliver reliable software through requirements generation, continuous integration, automated testing, issue tracking, and code reviews
Collaborate with colleagues across multiple teams
Deliver complex projects through incremental development
Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications)
2+ years of experience writing production-quality software
Strong system fundamentals and coding abilities (Python, C++)
Understanding of how to design high-performant software components
Excellent interpersonal skills
Experience developing in a Linux environment
BS, MS or PhD in CS, or related technical field
What Will Give You A Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications)
Experience with optimizing and/or evaluating complex software systems on dedicated hardware
Experience with ROS architectures
Experience with low latency or real time systems
Experience in the AV industry
Experience with SQL
Large build system such as bazel working experience

GM offers a variety of health and wellbeing benefit programs. Benefit options include medical, dental, vision, Health Savings Account, Flexible Spending Accounts, retirement savings plan, sickness and accident benefits, life insurance, paid vacation & holidays.
